## Appendix P13a.10 (P13a steps 4 and 5: no poison flag on a no-unwind store; admit proves I1, `m4_import`)

### P13a.10.1 Method

Step 4 (no poison flag). The `PruvStore` poison flag (P11.4) exists because an entry that panics halfway through its
writes leaves the state half-updated. In a verified Rust-backend program that is impossible except at one place:
every check inside a body is erased (Pruv callers call `f__pruv_body`, the caller proved `requires`, no cost counters),
and every operation the verifier accepted is total on the proved domain (unchecked indexing, plain arithmetic, lengths
bounded by 2^40). The only panic left is the entry's own `requires` check, which runs before the body writes. So the
judgment "the state is the result of complete entry calls" is a consequence of the proof, and the host keeps only the
side effect (owning `T`). Both compilers compute the same predicate, `raw_unwind_free`:

    verified && !printed && !g6 && !g10 && !proc && !net && !ev && par callees empty

and then emit `RAW_STORE_FREE` instead of `RAW_STORE`: the same API (`new`, `with`, `is_poisoned`, `PruvPoisoned`), so
adapters compile unchanged, but `with` is `Ok(f(&mut self.data))` and `is_poisoned` is `false`. Excluded, keeping the
flag: `--no-verify` (bodies keep checks), `print` (`println!` panics when stdout fails, mid-body), foreign code (G6
boundary checks and trusted Rust may panic), the G10
file / process / socket / event runtimes, `par` groups (threads, locks), and the LLVM backend and the C adapter (their
store is a separate text; unchanged in this package). Allocation failure and stack overflow abort and do not unwind.
SPEC.md "No-unwind store" states the rule, and one adapter rule the types cannot enforce: the `with` closure changes
`T` only through the entries (a host write to `T` followed by a host panic inside `with` is no longer caught). No
language change, so no must_reject rows.

Step 5 (I1 as ensures). P13a.8 left admit's I1 facts as runtime checks without a stated contract. They are now a
ground predicate on raw words:

- `ent_i1(st, e, top, ab, at)` (`pub opaque fn`, bool, no requires) states for entry e, at
  `st[c32(st[5]) + 20 * e + f]`, bud_store::ea's address (a valid store has `st[5] = 16 + slots <= 2^32 + 16`; the base
  is clamped to 2^32 as `c32` clamps it; an opaque body allows only immutable lets, so the two base cases call the
  plain bool `ent_w(st, b, ...)`): state 0 or 1; roots 0..2 live with owner -1; key span
  (words 4, 18) and blob span (12, 19) inside the arena `[ab, at)`; a free entry's next link -1 or below top; a live
  non-root entry's owner below top; key length in `0..2^30` and `kn <= 4 * kcap` (`words(kn) <= kcap`); blob length
  within its cap; links 7..10 -1 or below top; word 11 >= 0.
- `span_w` replaces `span_ok`: the same test without `requires` (it tests the arena bounds first), because a function
  with `requires` is not expanded into a contract.
- `entry_ok` reads the words directly instead of through `ef`/`words` (both have `requires`, so their bodies are
  invisible to the ensures), returns the same codes in the same order (-3, -2, -5, -6, -8, -4, -5, -6, -7), and
  `ensures result >= 0 ==> ent_i1(st, e, top, ab, at)`.
- admit tests the header words it bounds by as plain words (`0 <= st[5] <= 2^32 + 16`, `top = st[7] <= 2^32`,
  `0 <= st[9] <= st[10] <= 2^40`; every valid store passes, else -1) and its entry loop carries
  `forall j in 0..e: ent_i1(st, j, top, ab, at)`.

One encoding fact matters here (P13o): an opaque call is the uninterpreted `opq!F` symbol, but under a quantifier
whose bound variable reaches an argument it is expanded to its body. entry_ok's ensures gives the symbol at `e`; the
invariant's forall needs the body at `j = e`. The loop therefore says `reveal ent_i1;` after the entry check, which
ties the two. Callers of admit see only the symbol form unless they reveal it.

Adapter wiring (P11.5): `root_m4.pruv` gets `m4_import(st, inout cnt) -> i64`,
`ensures result == 0 ==> bud_store::valid(st)`, for a buffer handed in from outside the entries (2 on any admit
failure). The Rust-store drivers (`m4`, `m4raw`, `m4nv`, `m4eq`, `m4llvm*`) load it as an adapter would load a host
buffer: right before the program's `observe` they copy the state into a fresh store, admit it (must return 0 with at
least the three roots visited), check that its observation equals the old store's, and swap it in, so the observation
checked against the model runs on the imported store; a copy whose entry 0 state word is 7 must return 2 and is never
served from. The C-handle lanes (`m4c`, `m4cb`) have no host buffer and admit the handle's own state (last field
`-`). `run.py` requires exactly one `import` line per program with those values and prints
`import admission checks: N/N programs`.

### P13a.10.2 Changed contracts

| function | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `bud_admit::admit` | `result >= 0 ==> valid(st) && result <= 2^32` | adds the header bounds above and `forall e in 0..st[7]: ent_i1(st, e, st[7], st[9], st[10])`; header words out of those bounds now return -1 (no valid store has them) |
| `bud_admit::entry_ok` | none | `requires 0 <= ab <= at <= 2^40`, `0 <= e < top <= 2^32`; `ensures result <= 1`, `result >= 0 ==> ent_i1(...)` |
| `bud_admit::ent_i1` | (new) | opaque predicate, above |
| `bud_admit::ent_w` | (new) | ent_i1's word tests at a given base, no requires |
| `bud_admit::span_ok` | span test with requires | removed; `span_w` (no requires) |
| `root_m4::m4_import` | (new) | `result == 0 ==> valid(st)` |
| `PruvStore` (Rust backend, raw entries) | poison flag always | no flag when `raw_unwind_free`; same API |

Not stated by `ent_i1` (entry_ok still checks them at run time): the owner's live state and the key padding
(`key_pad_ok` reads through `ent_u16::rd`, which returns i64 through a branch and cannot appear in a contract).

### P13a.10.6 Remaining work

- The LLVM backend store and the C adapter keep the flag; the same rule could drop it there.

### P13a.10.7 Audit

One review (Codex, delegate role review) of the package diff. Required findings and what was done:

1. `print` lowers to `println!`, which panics when stdout fails, after body writes: a verified printing program could
   leave a half-written state under the flag-free store. Fixed: `printed` joins the predicate in both compilers;
   check_raw_entries gains a printing program that must keep the flag.
2. A host closure that writes `T` and then panics inside `with` is no longer caught. Not a code change: such a write
   already breaks the adapter rule (state changes only through the entries) and the forwarders' safety text; SPEC.md
   now states the rule next to the store.
3. At the largest layout (`st[5] = 2^32 + 16`) admit returned -1 where HEAD returned -2, and ent_i1's base differed
   from `ea`'s clamped base. Fixed: the bound is `2^32 + 16` and the base is `c32(st[5])` in ent_i1 and entry_ok.
4. `m4_import` was called on the final state only, so no op or observation ran on an imported store. Fixed: the Rust
   drivers import a copy before `observe`, compare and swap it in (P13a.10.1).
5. run.py passed a program with no `import` line and accepted `-` on every lane. Fixed: exactly one line, `2` on the
   Rust lanes and `-` only on the C-handle lanes.

Optional findings (left as remaining work above): par / runtime cases in check_raw_entries; forwarding the I1 ensures
through `m4_import`. A confirmation review of the five fixes found 1, 2, 3 and 5 done; on 4, a second `init` in the
same `q` session kept the first world's import result. Fixed: `init` resets it, so each world is imported before its
own `observe` (checked by hand with `init 232, observe, init 232, observe`; generated programs have one `init`). Findings and decisions: `work/p13a45/audit_findings.md` (not committed).

## Appendix P13b (row P13 B/host.rs: reserve, grow, failure; byte and copy accounting)

### P13b.1 Method

Growth protocol (unchanged in shape, now proved and sized in Pruv). An op that cannot fit returns status 1 (Grow) with
`N = out[0]` before any write: every bud_world mutator calls `bud_map::make_room` / `room` (bud_store::need on the
entries and arena words it will add) first, and room writes nothing unless it rehashes the index in place (same
observation); its rehash-then-Grow branch is unreachable for resident states (audit note, not proved), so a Grow
status means the op made no observable change. The host allocates a zeroed buffer of exactly `N`
words, calls the grow entry (`m4_grow` / `grow_copy`), drops the old buffer and retries the same op, at most 3 times.
Nothing is replayed: the retry is the same single call on the copied state, and an op that returned Grow emitted no
effect and answered no query (checked by the M10 replay counters, P13b.5).

Every decision stays in Pruv:
- `bud_store::need` decides N. It doubles from `2*len(st)` (at least 464) until the fresh layout fits, is capped at
  2^40 words (the array length bound), and states `result == 0 || 464 <= result <= 2^40` and
  `result == 0 || len(st) > 2^39 || result >= 2*len(st)`. The geometric step is a proved fact, so growth is amortized
  linear without a host choice; the host's former `max(N, 2*len)` is gone (host.rs, driver_m4).
- `grow_copy` proves `len(nxt) == len(old(nxt))` and `result != 0 || valid(nxt)` with no exit check: `init_store`
  proves `valid(nxt)`, and `copy_node`, `copy_leaves` and `copy_kids` now state `kept(nxt, old(nxt))` (the P13a.9
  writer preservation), so the root loop carries `valid(nxt)` as an invariant. The former O(1) exit `valid` check is
  removed.
- `grow_copy` copies the shapes the world builds (root 0 flat, roots 1 and 2 two levels). Admission accepts deeper
  trees; their deeper entries used to be dropped silently. Now a live count of nxt that differs from prev's returns
  2 (old state kept), so a grow never loses entries.
- `bud_store::copy_words(st)` (new, O(1), header only) gives the copy accounting: 20 words per entry up to the entry
  top (roots included) plus the arena words in use; the header is not counted. `root_m4::m4_copied` forwards it.

Failure semantics (no poison flag, P13a.10). `grow_copy` reads prev only, so every failure on the grow path leaves the
old buffer valid and unchanged and the op reports failure:
- allocation refused: host.rs `alloc_zeroed` and driver_m4 `try_zeroed` call `std::alloc::alloc_zeroed` and return
  None on a null pointer (no abort, no unwind); `vec![0; n]` aborted. The zeroed allocation keeps fresh pages lazily
  zeroed, like `vec![0; n]` (a `try_reserve_exact` + `resize` version written first touched every page and raised peak
  RSS by about 0.5 MiB at n = 1000; replaced in this package);
- `N <= len` (need at its cap with a layout that still does not fit): the host refuses before allocating;
- grow status != 0 (unsupported shape, invalid prev) or the retry limit: Err, old buffer kept.
host.rs `step_inner` runs under a `NoUnwind` guard that aborts on unwind: `Core` is a public trait, so an
implementation other than the proved entries could change st and then panic; the guard keeps the no-unwind premise of
the flag-free store for any implementation.

### P13b.2 Changed contracts

| function | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `bud_store::need` | none | `result == 0 \|\| 464 <= result <= 2^40`; `result == 0 \|\| len(st) > 2^39 \|\| result >= 2*len(st)`; capped at 2^40 |
| `bud_store::copy_words` | (new) | `0 <= result` |
| `bud_map::copy_node`, `copy_leaves`, `copy_kids` | budget bounds only | add `kept(nxt, old(nxt))` |
| `bud_map::grow_copy` | `result != 0 \|\| valid(nxt)` through an exit check | same ensures proved (no check), plus `len(nxt) == len(old(nxt))`; 2 when the live counts differ |
| `root_m4::m4_copied` | (new) | forwards `copy_words` |

No language change, so no must_reject rows; neither compiler changed.

### P13b.4 Byte and copy accounting (`harness grow N`, host.rs, Q2 then Q3 puts)

Q2 = n puts of 8 record words, Q3 = n puts of `40 + (i % 80)` words on the same keys; ops = 2n; the state starts at
256 words. `alloc_words` is the sum of the N the host allocated, `copy_words` the sum of `m4_copied` over grows.

| n | ops | Q2 grows | grows | final len | alloc words | copy words | alloc/op | copy/op |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 256 | 6 | 6 | 16384 | 32256 | 7146 | 126.0 | 27.9 |
| 300 | 600 | 7 | 8 | 65536 | 130560 | 40133 | 217.6 | 66.9 |
| 3000 | 6000 | 10 | 11 | 524288 | 1048064 | 337028 | 174.7 | 56.2 |

Checks (fails 0 at all three sizes): each grow at least doubles; one buffer per grow; the installed lengths sum to the
requested N exactly; Q2 grows; Q3 grows whenever its record words exceed the post-Q2 buffer (at n = 128 they fit);
alloc and copy words each at most 2 x final length (amortized linear: a doubling sequence sums below twice its last
term, and a copy is bounded by the old length); the fresh store copies exactly 60 words (3 roots x 20, empty arena);
each further put of one shape adds the same count, at least 20 + its record words; copy words >= 60 per grow. With
an allocation failure injected before every op, exactly the clean run's grow points fail with `GROW_ALLOC_ERR`, the
state words and the observation equal the pre-op snapshot, the retry succeeds, and the run ends in the clean state.

- `harness grow N` (above): Q2/Q3 growth, exact N, accounting, allocation-failure injection.
- `m10_test/run_m10.py replay`: the same program on a small start buffer (456 grows) and on a big one (0 grows) gives
  identical effect and query logs (726 effect lines); public calls 981 in both; small run 1093 attempts > 981 calls, and
  24 public calls hit Grow and then completed with effects or query answers; big run attempts = calls. So a grown call
  emits its effects once (no replay).
- `m34_test/run.py admit`: `admit_grow` grows every admitted case into 2 x len; a 0 result must keep the live count
  (cases 19 to 22), and the nested-tree cases (0, 14, 23) return 2 with the old state kept.
- m34 `lanes`: 922 grows across 300 programs on every lane, size formula checks 1922/1922.

### P13b.8 Remaining work

- Peak RSS above hand on 8 of 9 M4 cells (1.02 to 1.15x): split the excess by component (entry words, slot table,
  slack, old + new buffer at a grow) and shrink it; candidates are a smaller entry layout and a lower grow overlap.
- `grow_copy` copies only the shapes the world builds; deeper admitted trees now fail the grow (2) instead of losing
  entries. Either copy any depth or make admission reject them.
- No proof that the retry after a grow fits (the host's 3-retry limit covers it at run time).
- The out-buffer size (start 4096, doubling on status 3) is a host choice, not decided in Pruv.
- LLVM backend and C adapter: the poison flag and the growth path there are unchanged (P17).
- `m4_import` forwards only `valid(st)`, not admit's I1 forall (P13a.10.6).
- The rehash-then-Grow branch of `room` is unreachable for resident states but not proved so.
- `harness grow 30000` is slow (the injected run takes a snapshot at each grow point and the observation is linear);
  only up to n = 3000 is in the gate.
- M5_NOTES: store_find (n = 500, 1000) and store_find_enc (n = 1000) are above 1.0x hand, open.

### P13b.9 Audit

One review (Codex, review role) of the package diff, seven required findings, all fixed: (1) grow_copy dropped
entries of deeper admitted trees: live-count check returns 2, tested by admit_grow; (2) the public `Core` trait could
unwind after changing st: NoUnwind guard; (3) need could return up to 2^41, above the array bound, and a retry at the
same size was possible: cap at 2^40 with ensures, host refuses `N <= len`; (4) driver_m4 allocated with
`vec![0; n]` (aborts): fallible zeroed allocation; (5) copy accounting was only upper-bounded: exact-N and known-state
copy checks (P13b.4); (6) M10 replay passed with no public call through Grow: call and grown-call counters;
(7) `grow 128` required Q3 growth unconditionally: required only when Q3's record words exceed the post-Q2 buffer.
A confirmation review closed 1 to 6; on 7 it found that the count used whole op lengths, fixed to record words only.
Findings: `work/audit_findings.md` (not committed).

### P13c.1 Facts measured

- Process start (before `World::new`) is equal on both sides: about 1504-1520 KiB.
- Resident `__TEXT` of the executable: Pruv 304 KiB, hand 224 KiB in every cell (+80 KiB fixed). `__text` is
  338 KiB vs 282 KiB; the extra is mostly generated code (`World::exec` with `m4_op` inlined is 55 KB; `import_check`,
  `observe`, `bud_map::remove`, `put_at` 4-7 KB each).
- The peak is at the end of the prefill, not at a grow: current RSS never drops after a grow (phase probes:
  sessions 1000 goes 1632 -> 1792 -> 1872 -> 1984 -> 2176 KiB over its four grows, 2272 at the end of the prefill;
  `grows=0` in the timed loop).
- Freed state buffers stay in resident size. They are medium-zone malloc blocks (32-512 KiB); macOS keeps freed
  medium pages resident (reusable), and the next, larger buffer cannot reuse them. `malloc_zone_pressure_relief`
  after each grow does not lower the peak (measured, no change).
- `alloc_zeroed` of 64 KiB and more is lazy (untouched pages are not resident); 32 KiB is touched. So the untouched
  arena slack of the final buffer costs nothing.
- Grow history: n = 100 one grow (4096 -> 8192), n = 500 three (to 32768), n = 1000 four (to 65536), on all axes.
- Final buffer, sessions 1000: slots 2048, entry top 1003, arena top 31544 of 65536, so 31544 words (246 KiB) are
  touched; the entry table alone is 1003 x 20 words = 157 KiB. Clocks 1000: arena top 25544 (200 KiB). Hand's whole
  malloc heap (vmmap, allocated) is 217 KiB (sessions 1000), 343 KiB (tools 1000), 315 KiB (clocks 1000).

### P13c.3 Candidates and the decisions they need

1. Old buffers. Ablation result (KiB, 3 runs): sessions 1792/1915/2043, tools 1813/2027/2245,
   clocks 1787/1904/2000. Below hand only on clocks 500/1000; the rest still carry the +80 KiB text.
   Options: (a) the host maps state buffers directly (mmap/munmap for state-sized allocations; a host allocation
   choice, decisions stay in Pruv; each map is still counted in `allocs=`); (b) a Pruv in-place grow (realloc the
   buffer, then move the regions inside it with a proved relocation), which removes the abandoned buffer at the root
   but is a larger change to `bud_store` / `bud_map` and their proofs. Decision needed: is (a) an admissible host
   choice for the 1.0x comparison (hand keeps the default allocator), or is (b) required.
2. Text +80 KiB. It is generated code size, so the root fix is in codegen (pruvc / pruvc-rs), which this package may
   not change without stopping first. Measured build-flag effects on the driver (n = 100 peak, sessions / tools):
   default 1808/1808, `codegen-units=1` 1792/1808, `panic=abort` 1776/1824, `lto=fat` + `codegen-units=1`
   1712/1760 (`__text` 326 KiB; tools 1000 core time 36.0 vs 36.8 ns/op). Building only the Pruv side with LTO is
   a toolchain choice the hand side does not get; decision needed on whether it is admissible, or whether the
   codegen size work goes to a compiler package.
3. Entries (tools rest +5/+27/+69). After 1 and 2, tools 500 and 1000 would still be above hand. A smaller entry
   layout (for example two 32-bit fields per word) touches `bud_map`, `bud_store`, `bud_world`, `bud_admit`, their
   proofs and the M10 replay counters; it is its own step.

Step 1 left steps 2 and 3 waiting on these decisions. The Python compiler's generated code was not measured in

### P13c.4 Decisions

1. Old buffers: option (a). The host maps state-sized buffers by pages itself; this is the product host allocation
   path (`host.rs` and every driver that uses it), not a benchmark-only switch. Hand keeps the default allocator.
   "Hand + the same mapping path" is measured once as a reference column (P13c.7), so the part of the gain that is an
   allocator effect and not a Pruv advantage is visible. No in-place grow (b).
2. Text +80 KiB: building only the Pruv side with `lto=fat` is not admissible. Both sides with
   `lto=fat` + `codegen-units=1` is measured once as a reference (P13c.7). The root fix (generated code size) is queued
   as P13d (compiler); this package does not touch the compiler.
3. Entry layout: queued as P13e, not in this package.

### P13c.5 Change: `StateBuf` (`bench/l3/budget/state_buf.rs`)

- `StateBuf` is an owned, zero-initialized `[i64]` of fixed length. Buffers of `STATE_MAP_BYTES` = 64 KiB or more are
  an anonymous private `mmap` (zero-filled, pages resident only when touched) and are `munmap`ed on drop, which
  returns their pages at once. Smaller buffers use the global allocator with `alloc_zeroed`. Drop picks the path again
  from the same byte size.
- Threshold 64 KiB: 4 pages of 16 KiB (macOS arm64) or 16 pages of 4 KiB. Below it the malloc zones reuse freed blocks
  well and a mapping would waste most of a page; from it up, `alloc_zeroed` is already lazy on macOS (P13c.1), so
  mapping does not touch more pages than before.
- Why the default allocator keeps old buffers resident: on macOS the malloc medium zone keeps freed 32 KiB - 8 MiB
  blocks resident until memory pressure, and the next, larger state buffer cannot reuse them (P13c.1). On Linux glibc
  already serves blocks of 128 KiB and more with `mmap` (`M_MMAP_THRESHOLD`), but the threshold is dynamic: freeing a
  mapped block raises it to that block's size, so whether a later buffer is mapped depends on the allocation history
  (not measured here). `StateBuf` maps from a fixed 64 KiB on both, independent of the allocator's threshold.
- Targets: the mapping path is compiled for 64-bit macOS / iOS and Linux on x86_64, aarch64 and riscv64 (constants
  `MAP_PRIVATE` 0x02, `MAP_ANON` 0x1000 on Apple and 0x20 on Linux). Every other target (Windows included) compiles
  the fallback under `cfg`, where `AVAILABLE` is false and every buffer uses the default allocator. Only the macOS
  path was run in this package.
- Users: `host.rs` (`ResidentState.st: StateBuf`; the `Core` trait and `harness.rs` take slices, which is what the
  generated entries take), `host/src/lib.rs` (includes `state_buf.rs` before `host.rs`), and the M4 test driver
  (`m34_test/driver_m4.rs`, `Store<StateBuf>`; `run.py` writes the include into `main_<tag>.rs`). The C-runtime lanes
  (`m4c`) allocate in `runtime.c` and are unchanged.
- Kept from P13b: sizing stays in Pruv (`bud_store::need` gives N, the host allocates exactly N words); a refused
  allocation (`StateBuf::zeroed` returns `None`, or the injected `fail_allocs` hook) keeps the state of that grow
  attempt and returns the failure, with that attempt's counters unchanged; the M10 replay counters are the same
  (P13c.9). Scope (unchanged from P13b): the guarantee is per grow attempt. If one op grows, retries and a second grow
  fails, the first grow's buffer and counters stay; that state observes exactly as before the call. The error string
  is a small allocation; if that fails too, the process aborts as any Rust allocation does.
- 32-bit targets: N comes from Pruv as `i64` (up to 2^40); an N above `usize` is refused like an allocation failure
  (`host.rs` grow and init, `driver_m4.rs` grow), not truncated. `STATE_MAPS` and the driver's counter are `AtomicUsize`,
  which every std target has.
- Accounting: each mapping counts in `STATE_MAPS`, and the driver's `allocs=` adds it to the counting global
  allocator's count, so one state buffer is one allocation on either path.

## Appendix P20 (B/bud_charge.pruv, m8_test: counters, sums, bounds)

Status: done on the Rust and Python compilers (2 of the 4 pairs; the LLVM pairs wait for P17a-c). Commits 3006b2f
(steps 1-2), 4852bfa (step 3), ca56901 (step 4), 5171524 (step 5, audit follow-ups), on top of 6aa266a. Changed:
`bud_charge.pruv`, `m8_test/` (root, driver, three hand lanes, runner, corrupt control). No compiler, `SPEC.md`,
`tests/run_all_rows.txt`, `bud_lifecycle.pruv` or `bud_tools.pruv` change.

Machine: macOS arm64, 10 cores, shared with other work (load average noted per run). Compiler: the shared
`pruvc-rs/target/release/pruvc`, which was rebuilt during the package with main's T0 (417dd56, 2^40 length bound at
every host entry); see P20.4. Python compiler: `pruvc/` of the same main, run as `work/p20/pypruvc`. Raw logs in
`work/p20/` (not committed).

### P20.1 What changed

- KD-M8-1 (N20): a `noteTool` that would take `tools` past ±(2^53-1) now refuses with 5 before the dedup insert, so
  the activity is not recorded (before: the insert ran, then the bump refused). The room test is the same single
  range test the bump uses; the bump after the insert keeps its own test.
- Counters work in place on the resident record words (`charge_at`, `note_failure_at`, `tool_room_at`,
  `add_tool_at`, all with `requires 0 <= b && b + 14 <= len(w)`), instead of copying the 15-word frame out and back.
  `cur_off` finds the current record and, on the fast path, proves `off + n <= len(st)` once. The frame functions keep
  their API and call the `_at` versions with `b = 1`. All five sums are formed before any write; any sum outside
  ±(2^53-1) answers 5 with the record unchanged.
- C/D fixtures and 22 negative/boundary controls (N01-N22) run through the oracle runner; controls check every call's
  line, the final counters and (N21, N22) the final toolSeen activity lists.
- Perf runs that name `charge` or `failure` stop before the tool setup in every lane (Pruv driver, hand16/hand16w,
  fxmix/fxmixw built from the u16 source, oa/oaw, old hand), so that item's peak RSS is not the tool setup's.

### P20.4 Attribution of the remaining instruction gap

- Matched boundary (hand16w, oaw: the same wire i64 op words) is the <= 1.0x cell. hand16 (pre-decoded keys) is
  unmatched: about 100 instructions per call are wire framing that hand16 skips.
- Pruv core after dispatch is about 346 instructions vs hand16's 337 (pre-T0 gen, failure 100).
- Compiler gap: `bud_map::find_w` is emitted `#[inline]` and not inlined at the hot call (about 25-29 instructions,
  ~1 ns). Not worked around in source.
- T0 (main, not P20): per-entry `pub fn t_call` wrapper with the 2^40 length test and `t_call__pruv_body`. Ablation
  on the same driver, instructions per call at n = 100, failure / charge: pre-T0 gen 467 / 597; T0 gen 513 / 653;
  T0 gen with only the length test line removed 502 / 636. So T0 adds 46 / 56, of which the test itself is 11 / 17
  and the rest the wrapper split. Queued on main as P13f (hoist the check where the driver holds the length).
- Library cost (research pass): field address recomputation and owner/generation checks in `bud_map`/`bud_store`
  lookups (P13e), frame parsing and rechecks after `rec_end`. The ±(2^53-1) tests are business rules and stay.

### P20.5 Checks the proofs removed

- `charge_at` / `bump_at` / `tool_room_at` index record words `w[b + 3..b + 13]` without bounds checks: one
  `b + 14 <= len(w)` at the caller (from `cur_off`) discharges them all.
- `cur_off` fast path: one `off + n <= len(st) && bs + bm <= len(bk)` test, then plain indexing and one `eq_range`
  memcmp for the id; the `rd` slow path stays only for records that fail it.
- The 15-word copy-out / copy-in of the frame (`load_cv` / `store_cv`) and its length rechecks are gone from the
  resident path; they remain only on the slow path, taken when `b + 14 <= len(st)` does not hold.
- Kept on purpose: the ±MAX sum tests (refusal contract), the state/unlimited/halt branches (oracle behaviour).

### P20.6 Proof time (root_m8, 3 runs each, wall seconds)

Rust compiler: main 7.68 / 6.73 / 6.96, P20 6.95 / 6.94 / 6.83. Python compiler: main 28.04 (cold cache) / 11.50 /
12.02, P20 11.36 / 11.42 / 11.00. Equal within run-to-run spread.

### P20.7 Audit

One package audit (static). Three findings were filed as must-fix; none was accepted, with evidence:

- Negative amounts/counters accepted: intended. The reference `charge` adds negatives (`amount > 0 &&` only guards the
  halt), `M8_NOTES.md` keeps "negative amounts are added and never halt", C09 records it; the bound is ±(2^53-1)
  (spec row "ResourceBound(number) outside ±(2^53−1), including increments/negative charges").
- An earlier key's over-limit halt before a later key's out-of-range sum: the reference halts at the first over-limit
  key before any later sum exists, so the halt is the exact oracle result (N09, N10 pin both orders).
- Open (not P20-specific): on a CORRUPT resident buffer whose record overlaps the dedup insert area, `noteTool` can
  insert and then refuse. The corrupt-buffer contract is byte equality with the old revision (387/0), and valid
  stores are atomic (N20, N21). Making corrupt buffers atomic too needs a record/insert non-overlap check or a
  commit-at-end insert in `bud_tools` (P21).
- Taken: the new-activity-on-existing-turn control (N21), negative tools (N22), old hand lane early stop, chk report
  lane names. Noted, not changed: wire frame preparation differs per lane outside the timer; chk gate checks key
  sets per round; ns are rounded to 0.1 before the overlap test.

## Appendix P18 (row B/bud_lifecycle.pruv: current/isHalted/reopen lookups by proven indexing)

Commits 123ae15 (step 1, source), 81979b2 (step 2, perf item), 5fe70f0 (step 3, this appendix), 06c3426
(step 4, audit fixes), 12e67a0 (step 5, appendix) and cb217c2 (step 6, result-tag harness and `found_at` order),
base 6aa266a. Changed files:
`bench/l3/budget/bud_lifecycle.pruv`, `bench/l3/budget/m7_test/{driver_m7.rs,hand_m7_u16.rs,run_m7.py}`. No
compiler file, `SPEC.md`, `tests/run_all_rows.txt` or `bud_charge.pruv` change. Raw logs: `work/p18/` (not
committed).

### P18.1 Change

- `found_at(st, se, bk, bs, bn)` (new): one `bud_store::eb` entry address, one blob span check
  (`0 <= off && off <= len(st) - n`, `n >= 30`), the state range check (0..2) and the identity check (`id_at`). Its
  `ensures` gives callers `16 <= a, a + 20 <= len(st)`, the span in `st` and the state in 0..2; `-2` is returned
  only when the span lies outside `st`.
- `id_at(st, off, n, k, ks, kn)` (new): `requires` the record span; reads the id length word `st[off + 24]` directly
  and compares the packed id words with one `eq_range` when they lie inside the record and inside `k` (one dynamic
  check each); otherwise falls back to `id_is` (same reads as before).
- `current_entry`, `current_at`: now `found_at`. `current`, `is_halted`: read `st[a + 12]`, `st[a + 13]` and the
  state word `st[st[a + 12]]` directly and write `out[0..3)` directly (lengths already tested).
- `found_at` order (step 6, cb217c2): the state word is read and range-checked after `id_at`, not before it. Same
  checks and answers; read first, `is_halted`'s own read of the same word paid a reload chain (P18.3).
- Perf harness (step 6, `driver_m7.rs`): the Pruv typed lane consumes `(status, out[0])` in one `black_box` per
  call, matching the hand typed lane's `black_box` of its `Res` (confirm audit, P18.6a).
- `reopen`: the header reads `st[off]`, `st[off + 18]` and the in-place writes of words 0, 18, 19, 22 are direct.
  The rewrite path (`ended.at` text present) is unchanged.

Checks removed by proofs (each was a dynamic bounds or field check in the base):

| removed check | where | discharged by |
|---|---|---|
| entry field reads a+12 (blob offset), a+13 (blob length) | `current_at`, `current`, `is_halted`, `reopen` | `eb` ensures `16 <= a, a + 20 <= len(st)` |
| `field_addr`/`entry_addr` checked address | `current_at` | `eb` |
| state word read `st[off]` | `found_at`, `is_halted`, `reopen` | span check `off <= len(st) - n`, `n >= 30` |
| id length word `st[off + 24]` | `id_at` | span + `30 <= n` |
| per-word id compare bounds | `id_at` | one range test, then `eq_range` |
| header reads/writes off+18, +19, +22 in `reopen` | `reopen` in-place path | `found_at` ensures through `current_at` |
| `ent_u16::wr` checked output writes | `current`, `is_halted`, `reopen` | `len(out)` tests already in the function |

Kept dynamic: the blob span check, the state range check and the identity check (unit count and words); the
`bud_map` hash in `find_w` is outside this row. Behaviour change on corrupt stores only: a blob span outside `st`
(`n >= 30` but `off + n > len(st)`) makes `found_at` answer -2 first, so `current` answers status 2 and `is_halted`
and `reopen` answer false (the base answered `current` 2 only after the state read succeeded, and the base
`is_halted` could answer true from the state word); an admitted store (I1, `bud_admit.pruv:52-56`) never has such
a span, and every Q/B gate below is unchanged.

### P18.4 reopen lookup above 1.0x: compiler gap (open, not worked around in source)

`reopen` is emitted as a separate `#[inline]` function and not inlined into the dispatch. Its prologue builds a
320-byte frame and saves 12 registers, because the rewrite path (`blob_copy`, a `Vec`) is in the same body; the miss
path pays that cost. `find_w` is a call in both `current` and `reopen`. Experiments (S = 100, interleaved with
hand):

| experiment | result |
|---|---|
| drop the `fx_ok` check | about -0.2 ns, still above hand |
| split the rewrite path into a source function `reopen_text` | the inline policy marks the single-caller function `#[inline(always)]` and folds it back; worse, 1.05/1.09; reverted |
| hand-edited generated Rust: `reopen` `#[inline(always)]` | worse, about 17 ns |
| hand-edited generated Rust: `reopen_text` `#[cold] #[inline(never)]` | about base, 13.0-13.5 vs hand 12.2-13.9; does not reach 1.0 reliably |

Source has no cold/no-inline control, and `codegen.rs` inlines every function with one caller
(`calls <= 1`, `pruvc-rs/crates/pruv-core/src/codegen.rs:4778`). This is recorded for the queued inline-policy split
(T5) and the part is stopped here; the source keeps the single-body `reopen`.

## Appendix P21 (B/bud_tools.pruv + key helpers: stored hash, dedup, commit at end)

Status: done on the Rust and Python compilers (2 of the 4 pairs; LLVM waits for P17a-c), except the forget cell
against oaw and one peak-RSS cell, queued below (P21a, P13e). Commits a23b9ff (step 1), 570c635 (step 2, audit fixes
and perf split), on top of 85dd936. Changed: `bud_tools.pruv`, `bud_map.pruv` (additions at the end only, plus one
comment), `m8_test/` (root, driver, three hand lanes, TS lane, runner). No compiler, `SPEC.md`, `tests/run_all_rows*`,
`bud_store.pruv`, `bud_lifecycle.pruv`, `bud_clock.pruv` or `bud_charge.pruv` change. Machine: macOS arm64, shared
(load average 5-9 during the final run). Raw logs in `work/p21/` (not committed).

### P21.1 What changed

- noteTool is split in a read-only `seen()` and a writing `note_new()`. `seen()` hashes each key once (`seek_w`) and
  keeps the hash, generation and slot that an insert would take; `note_new()` reuses them (`room_w`, `put_seek_w`),
  so a new activity hashes its key once instead of twice (lookup, then insert), and a dup hit stops after one hash.
- Commit at end (P20.7 carry-over): every refusal of `note_new()` (Grow from `room_w`, `room_w`'s invalid answer, the
  new `bud_map::alloc_ok`, the owner liveness test in `put_seek_w`) comes before the first key, entry or link write
  on a store whose header agrees with its tables. `alloc_ok` mirrors `entry_alloc` (free-list head, then `top < cap`,
  the second allocation after the first) and runs after `room_w`, so a full but consistent table still answers Grow.
  Scoped, not made atomic: two paths need a buffer whose index or arena contradicts its header beyond what `valid()`
  and `alloc_ok` read (no free slot after a rehash; a reused entry's key region not fitting); only `room_w`'s index
  rebuild (same key set) can precede a 2 there. The root's op 3 makes the tools-counter write last.
- A missing or stale budget still consumes the dedup key (spec §15 #6): `note_new()` runs whatever CURRENT says.
- root_m8 op 3 fast path only when the record lies inside the arena (`st[9] <= b0`, `b0 + 14 <= st[10]`);
  `load_cv_at` is shared with the fallback, which no longer looks CURRENT up twice.
- Perf: the old toolgrow timing is split into toolnew (ns per new activity) and toolforget (ns per forgetTurn of a
  turn holding N activities) on every lane; toolgrow stays as the instruction and memory item.

### P21.4 Attribution and the cells above 1.0x

- dup: one hash and one probe per key (`seen()`), then the counter path; the stored hash in entry word 6 is compared
  before any key words. 89 instructions fewer than the baseline per call.
- new: the key is hashed once (`seek_w` result reused by `put_seek_w`); about 680 instructions per toolgrow call less
  than the baseline, below oaw.
- forget vs oaw, line by line (hand `hand_m8_oa.rs` `Turns::forget` vs generated `bud_tools::forget_turn` ->
  `bud_map::remove`):

  | step | hand oa | Pruv |
  |---|---|---|
  | find the turn | `find_turn(h, key)`: hash + probe | `find_w(st, 2, key)`: hash + probe (same) |
  | unlink the turn | `slots[slot] = 1` (tombstone), `alive = false` | prev/next relink (entry words 7, 8), owner head/tail (9, 10), owner count (11) |
  | activities | `gen += 1`: all N activities become dead in O(1); their pool slots, slot-table entries and key units stay until a later rebuild (`dead_units`) | walk all N children: free each entry, tombstone its slot, return its arena words (word-14 update batched in `pend`) |
  | key words | `dead_units += key_len` | arena words returned per entry |

  The gap is the algorithm, not codegen: oa forgets lazily by generation (O(1) per forget, cost moved to the next
  rebuild and to memory: oaw toolgrow holds 23325-63790 allocations against Pruv's 40-44), Pruv frees eagerly
  (O(activities), 3.0 ns per activity, the bound `forget_turn` documents). An O(1) forget needs generation-tagged
  children in `bud_map` (entry layout and every child walk), outside P21's bounds (bud_map additions only). Queued as
  P21a.
- tooldup RSS at M (1.03x oaw, 80 KiB): not attributed in this package. Candidates: the 20-word entry (P13e) and the
  slack of the Pruv-sized grow (`bud_store::need`, N >= 2*len). Added to P13e.

### P21.5 Checks the proofs removed

- `put_seek_w` takes the slot and hash from `seen()` and does not probe again: the slot's emptiness and the key's
  absence are carried by `Seen` (a stale `Seen` can only mis-index, still total and `kept`).
- `room_w` answers fit once for both entries and the key words of both keys; `alloc_ok` and the inserts index the
  header and entry words without rechecks (from `kept(st, old(st))` and `valid()`).
- op 3 fast path: one arena-bounds test admits plain indexing of record words `b0 .. b0 + 14`.

## Appendix P21a (B/bud_map.pruv, bud_tools.pruv: O(1) forgetTurn by generation)

Status: forget gate met on the Rust and Python compilers (gates on both; perf from `run_m8.py perf`'s own build). toolnew at M = 500 is 1.08x oaw by median with overlapping distributions (noise by the rule) and the new + forget cycle costs 1.05-1.08x oaw in instructions; the reclaim cost is queued as P21b. Rust and Python compilers (2 of the 4 pairs; LLVM waits for P17a-c). On top of 46db894. Changed:
`bud_map.pruv`, `bud_tools.pruv`, `bud_admit.pruv`, `bud_store.pruv` (comments only), `m8_test/` (root, driver, the
two oa/u16 hand lanes, `corrupt_resident.py`), `M8_NOTES.md`, `m34_test/CONTRACT.md`. No compiler, `SPEC.md`,
`tests/run_all_rows*`, `bud_clock.pruv`, `bud_charge.pruv`, `bud_lifecycle.pruv` or M7/M9/M10 root change (P22 works
on those in parallel). Raw logs in `work/p21a/` (not committed).

### P21a.1 What changed

- forgetTurn (`bud_tools::forget_turn` -> `bud_map::forget_turn_entry`): finds the turn, unlinks it from root 2, takes
  its child count off word 12 (`uncount_children`) and frees the turn entry (`drop_entry`, which bumps its
  generation). The activities are not walked: each keeps state 1 with an owner that is now free and an owner
  generation (field 2) that no longer equals the owner's generation (field 3). Cost O(probe length + turn key),
  independent of the number of activities (was O(activities), P21.4).
- Reclaim where it lands: `put_at` first runs `reclaim_head`. While the free-list head f is a free entry whose head
  child c is pending dead (`reclaimable`: state 1, owner f, og != gen(f), field row writable), c is detached from f's
  list, its key and blob words come off word 14, it is freed (generation bumped) and pushed on the free list, where
  `entry_alloc` takes it. f itself stays on the free list until its list is empty, so a freed turn is never reused
  while it still owns pending children. If c has children of its own, they are uncounted and the loop continues
  (fuel top + 1, so a malformed child list ends the loop). Dead children keep their index slots until the next
  rehash; lookups compare the stored hash, owner and key, so a stale slot can only cost a probe step.
- `alloc_ok` mirrors the reclaim (a reclaimable head child of the free head counts as the second entry) and now runs
  before `room_w`: when the top and free list cannot supply the entries, `note_new` answers Grow before any write
  (`allocation_grow`: the count-based `need()` size if it already asks for growth, else `need(cap + 1)`). This closes
  the P21.7 counterexample (entry top = cap - 1, low live count) with a Grow instead of 2.
- `rehash` reinserts only entries in state 1 whose owner is a root or live, so pending dead children leave the index
  at a rehash and used <= live holds on a store whose word 12 counts its live entries.
- `remove` (M4 eager delete, unchanged walk) returns early on a pending dead child, which is already off word 12.
- Admission (`bud_admit::entry_ok`): a state-1 entry whose owner is free, with og != gen(owner) and the owner still
  holding a child list (head in range, count > 0), is classed dead (2). `admit` counts dead entries separately and
  checks free + live + dead == top and word 12 == live. A live child redirected to an unrelated free leaf stays an
  owner error (-4, M34 admission case 16).
- root_m8 op 3 (P21.7 fix-check medium): the counters are updated in place only when the record lies inside the arena
  below the arena top; the cv fallback runs only for a record entirely beyond `st` (`b0 >= len(st)`); an offset
  inside `st` but outside the arena (e.g. into the header) answers 2 before any write. The old revision wrote the
  copied counters back over the header (for `b0 = 1`, the arena top).
- Bench drivers: the perf checksum is taken after the forget; the driver gains an `hdr` command (header words 4..14)
  so `corrupt_resident.py` can tell a Grow from an in-place answer.

forget (toolgrow) RSS and allocations are below oaw and hand16w at S and M. tooldup RSS at M stays above oaw (1.02x,

Attribution of the toolnew cost at M: P21's toolnew was the insert alone, with each activity freed later by the eager
forget walk (about 3 ns per activity, inside toolforget). P21a moves that work into the insert: `reclaim_head` at
every `put_at` (free head, its head child, `reclaimable`'s field address, then the detach, word-14 update, free and
push) and `alloc_ok`'s second-entry test with the same reads, now ahead of `room_w`. Net: +10-12 ns per toolnew and +180
instructions per toolgrow cycle, so the lazy reclaim costs more per activity than P21's eager free did. oa pays its
deferred cost at a rebuild instead (23852-66323 allocations against Pruv's 40-45). Candidate fixes, not tried here
(build budget used): fold `reclaim_head` into `entry_alloc` so the free head is read once; skip the reclaim test when
word 8 is -1 or its head child is -1 (one load); reclaim a whole pending list per free-list visit.

### P21a.4 Checks the proofs removed or changed

- `entry_ok` now returns 2 (dead) as well as 0 and 1; `admit`'s loop invariant carries live + dead <= e, and the
  header check is word 12 == live with free + live + dead == top.
- `alloc_ok` is no longer proved equivalent to two `entry_alloc` calls (it was not machine-checked in P21 either); it
  mirrors `reclaim_head` + `entry_alloc` and is covered by the a-high-top and c-reuse controls and the Q2/controls
  gates. A wrong `alloc_ok` can only turn an insert into Grow (before any write) or reach the existing 2 paths.
- used <= live after `rehash` is a comment premise (a store with a valid layout, cap = slots/2 as `bud_store::valid`
  checks, whose word 12 counts its live entries), not a proved postcondition; on other buffers a Grow can follow the
  rehash (same key set), as `room_w` states.
- `reclaim_head` and `forget_turn_entry` keep `kept(st, old(st))` and entry top; the reclaim loop is total by fuel.

### P21a.5 Audit

One package audit (static, Codex gpt-6.2-astra; the first attempt was stopped by the engine's content filter and
rerun as a plain code review) and one fix-check.

- taken: `remove` on a pending dead child (reachable through a stale index slot) took it off word 12 a second
  time. Fixed by the early return in `remove`.
- taken: `rehash` reinserts live entries only and reads an entry's owner after its state (a free row's owner
  word is no longer loaded).
- taken: the P21a controls could not tell a Grow from an in-place answer; added the driver `hdr` command and
  the header checks above.
- taken: the `room_w` comment claimed used <= live on any buffer; scoped to a valid layout with an exact word 12.
- scoped, not changed (pre-existing, same as 46db894): ops 1/2 (charge) write a record in place when its offset
  points into the header of a corrupt buffer; guarding it adds arena-bound loads to the charge hot path. Queued.
- scoped: op 3 assumes a record inside the arena does not overlap other live arena regions (arena-internal overlap is
  a broken buffer, not checked).
- advisory: completeness of a pending child list (every dead child reachable from its former owner) is I2 and not
  checked by admission; an unreachable dead entry is leaked until the host rebuilds the store, never reused while
  linked.
- Fix-check: the `remove` and `rehash` fixes are correct, the `hdr` controls separate Grow from in place; the comment
  and one control name were narrowed as asked. New, recorded (medium, pre-existing): admission does not check
  og == gen(owner) when the owner is live, so a child with a stale owner generation under a live owner is admitted
  as live, while `remove` now skips it. Fixing it changes admission results and the m34 expectations; queued.

## Appendix P21b (B/bud_map.pruv: the reclaim cost of the lazy forget)

Status: gate met on the Rust and Python compilers (gates on both; perf from `run_m8.py perf`'s own build). toolnew is
0.87 / 0.97x oaw at S / M by median, with Pruv's max below oaw's min at both sizes, and the toolgrow cycle is 0.93 /
0.98x oaw in instructions. On top of 2b04d95 (P21a). Changed: `bud_map.pruv`, `M8_NOTES.md` and the load-policy paragraph of `m34_test/CONTRACT.md`. `bud_store.pruv`,
`bud_tools.pruv`, the m8 drivers and roots, `bud_clock.pruv`, M7/M9/M10 and compiler sources are unchanged. Raw logs
are in `work/p21b/` (not committed).

### P21b.1 Cause, in the order data representation -> language gap -> codegen

- Data representation (the M cell). The P21b header dump at M = 500 (words 4..14) reads 4096 slots, cap 2048,
  1505 live entries and 2502 used slots. `room()` rehashed early only when `live + ents <= slots / 4` (1024). With
  1505 live entries that never held, so tombstones built up until the `used > slots * 3 / 4` grow-or-rehash point.
  The index ran between 0.37 and 0.75 load, and every new activity's unsuccessful probe got longer. At S (305 live
  in 1024 slots) the bound held, which is why only M was above oaw.
- Language gap: none. The fixes use existing Pruv features: direct row writes proved with
  `kept(st, old(st))` (`len` equal, header shape and `dyn_ok` kept), and the `eb(st, e)` fast base.
- Codegen (both sizes). P21a's `reclaim_head` freed the dead child, pushed it on the free list, and then
  `entry_alloc` popped it back. Each step re-read the free head and recomputed the row bases through `field_addr`.
  `put_at` also recomputed the entry base for the key store and for the link.

### P21b.2 What changed (`bud_map.pruv`)

- `alloc_entry(st, owner, og)` replaces `reclaim_head; entry_alloc`.
  - Fast path. The free head f is a free row whose head child c is pending dead: state 1, owner f, og != gen(f), and
    no children of its own. Both rows must have a fast base. In that case c is detached from f's list
    (`detach_fast`), its key and blob words come off word 14, and c is filled in place as the new entry (`fill_fast`,
    generation + 1). Word 12 gains one. There is no free-list push or pop, and the free head stays f.
  - Any other case takes the old `reclaim_head; entry_alloc` path.
  - The audit proved the two paths equal on every input (P21b.6).
- `put_at`:
  - It computes `be = eb(st, e)` once.
  - On a fast base it stores the key with `put_key_fast`: it reuses the old key region when the key fits, else it
    calls `arena_put` and `set_key_region`. Otherwise it uses `put_units` as before.
  - The same `be` is passed to `link_fast`.
- `rehash`:
  - It clears the slot range on direct words when `16 <= sb` and `sb + slots <= len(st)`, else through `wr16` as
    before.
  - `rehash_hash` reads state, owner, the owner's state and the stored hash on direct words and returns -1 for an
    entry that is not reinserted. When the stored hash itself is -1, the caller asks `reinsert` (the old `gf`
    test), so the reinserted set is unchanged.
- `room()`'s early tombstone rehash now runs when `used + ents > slots / 2` and `live + ents <= slots * 3 / 8`.
  - It was `slots / 4`.
  - Amortization still holds: after the rehash, used = live <= 3/8 of the slots, so the next early rehash is at
    least slots/8 inserts away.
  - The grow point and the rehash-before-grow rule are unchanged.
  - After the early rehash `need()` is asked again, as the 3/4 branch already did (audit pass 2, P21b.6). On a valid
    store it is 0; on a buffer with wrong counters a Grow can now follow the rehash instead of a false fit.
  - The `room()` and `make_room` comments say so.

### P21b.5 Checks the proofs removed or changed

- `detach_fast`, `fill_fast`, `set_key_region` and `alloc_entry` carry `ensures kept(st, old(st))`. Their direct
  writes are proved inside the row (`16 <= b`, `b + 20 <= len(st)` from `eb`). The `fields_ok`/`dyn_ok` header facts
  are re-established by `assert len(st) == len(old(st)) && hdr_same(st, old(st), -1); reveal dyn_ok`.
- The rehash slot clear proves each `sb + i` inside `[16, len(st))` from the branch guard. Slots outside it still go
  through `wr16`.
- `alloc_entry`'s equivalence to `reclaim_head; entry_alloc` is a static audit result (P21b.6), not a machine-checked
  postcondition. Like `alloc_ok` in P21a.4, it is covered by the c-reuse control and the Q2/controls gates.
- `room()`'s amortization is a comment premise (a valid layout whose word 12 counts its live entries), as `room_w`
  states in P21a.4.

### P21b.6 Audit

Static review, Codex gpt-6.2-astra (ultra), in two passes.
- Pass 1 (`alloc_entry`, `detach_fast` and the first `put_at` change): no must-fix and no should-fix findings.
  - `alloc_entry` returns the same value and leaves every store word identical to `reclaim_head; entry_alloc` on
    every input, including corrupted stores.
  - The guards imply both rows lie past the header and below cap; f != c.
  - The old path's loop ends on its first turn for the same c.
  - Words 8, 12 and 14 and the generation (`wrapping_add`) end equal.
  - The key-word sum stays below 2^41.
- Pass 2 (`fill_fast`, `put_key_fast` / `set_key_region`, base reuse, `rehash_hash` / `reinsert` and the direct slot
  clear, the `slots * 3 / 8` bound): items 1-4 equal to the paths they replace on every input; one must-fix in item 5.
  - taken (must-fix): the early branch returned "rehashed, fits" without asking `need()` again. On a corrupted store
    (rows in state 1 not counted in word 12, e.g. 16 slots, live 5, used 9, 16 reinsertable rows) the rehash fills
    the index and the insert then fails with 2. Under the old `slots / 4` bound the same shape needed a smaller live
    count, so the gap predates P21b but the wider bound reaches more buffers. Fixed: `need()` again after the rehash,
    Grow if it fails (P21b.2). Gates and perf rerun (P21b.3, P21b.4).
  - taken (should-fix): the amortization comment now states its premise (valid layout, exact word 12; the roots are
    not indexed, so used = live - 3) and calls the rehash O(slots) passes with probe lengths that depend on the hash
    spread, not a worst-case time bound.
  - taken (should-fix): `m34_test/CONTRACT.md`'s load policy now states 3/8, the re-ask and slots/8. The other two
    places that cite `slots / 4` are records of earlier packages (PERF_HEADROOM.md, P22's file; the P19.6a / P21a
    appendix text) and stay as written.
  - recorded: on a corrupted store the early rehash can repeat on every call with no insert in between (each call
    ends; frequency is amortized only on a valid store). Same class as the 3/4 branch; not changed.
  - No fix-check pass: the request's audit budget (one audit, one follow-up) was used by passes 1 and 2. The fix
    mirrors the existing 3/4 branch line for line and is covered by the rerun gates.

## Appendix P22 (row P/bud_clock.pruv: runs, refresh, begin, settle, arm; active count; R/timer cycle)

Commits 4b7b3e9 (restructure), 49da4c6 (merge of main with P21a), 5816790 (mutant fix), 09898b8 (audit fixes) and
the commit with this appendix (confirm-audit fixes); base 64aee24. Changed files: `bench/l3/budget/bud_clock.pruv`,
`bench/l3/budget/m9_test/{driver_m9.rs,root_m9.pruv,run_m9.py,mut_m9.py}`, `bench/l3/budget/{M9_NOTES.md,PERF_HEADROOM.md}`.
No compiler file, `bud_map`, `bud_store`, `m8_test`, `bud_lifecycle.pruv` or `bud_halt.pruv` change. Raw logs:
`work/p22/` (not committed).

### P22.1 Change

- Clock and run fields are read through one `bud_store::eb` base per entry (`16 <= ca && ca + 20 <= len(st)`) and
  then by proven direct indexing `st[ca + f]` (fields 11 child count, 14 since-present, 15 since ms, 16 armed,
  17 active count), as P18/P19 did for the session and lifecycle paths.
- I2 (clock word 17 = number of its runs with word 14 != 1) is not a proof premise. Every change of word 17 goes
  through `add_active`, whose ensures state the exact +-1 update and that no other word changes; `runs` reads
  word 17 instead of walking the run list. I2 is checked at run time: `root_m9::t_i2` recomputes the count of every
  clock from its run list, and the q driver (`World<true>`) calls it after every `t_call` and every `t_put`, exit 3
  on a mismatch. `mut_m9.py` builds four mutants of the update sites and requires each to be killed.
- Audit fixes (09898b8):
  - C1: `limit_ms` clamps timeMinutes into +-1.5e14 (product within +-9e18), so every safe-integer delay equals the
    source's (a q case gave 59009 vs TS 119009 before; pre-existing clamp, not P22's).
  - C2: every public entry taking `bv` tests `len(bv) >= 7` before any write and returns 0 with nothing changed
    (`run_waiting`, `run_ended`, `close` wrote part of a short frame before).
  - C3/P1: `arm_at`, `refresh_at`, `fire_at` return 3 without fx room (`fx_ok`) before any write; `refresh_at` tests
    CURRENT before the entry base. `settle_at`/`drop_at` keep the caller's `fx_ok` (bud_lifecycle and the by-key
    entries make it), stated in a comment.
  - H1-H5 (harness): `t_i2` fails a list still going after `walk_limit` and a clock walk that does not end; the driver
    checks I2 after every `t_put`, fails after 4 Grow retries and skips puts after a halt; `run_m9` restores
    activeSince from the last put before the first non-run call; `waiting_no_dec` drops only the decrement.

- Confirm-audit fixes (comparator and notes only, no Pruv change):
  - `run_m9.py` classifies an oracle record holding a number outside the safe integral range (`{num}`) as
    known-difference KD-M6-1 (excluded domain, spec §8.4) instead of comparing it (a `%d` on `{num}` raised
    TypeError; a settled activeMs above 2^53 made B halt where the clock re-arms).
  - `compare_final` turns both activeSince sides into text, so a lone-surrogate `{u16}` record compares equal (H1).
  - The halt-state check is skipped when the script stores the halted session again after its first call: the
    oracle's final state is then not the one at the halt (H2; no corpus case has such a put).
  - `M9_NOTES.md`: the clamp text, status 3 of `refresh_at`/`arm_at`/`fire_at`, the caller's `fx_ok` for
    `settle_at`/`drop_at`, the short-`bv` rule.

## Appendix P19c (both codegens: foreign call wrapper, cross-rlib inlining)

### P19c.1 Change

Every `trusted rust fn` wrapper (`pruvc/foreign_codegen.py` `trusted_helper`, `pruvc-rs/.../codegen.rs`
`trusted_text`) emitted

```rust
let result: T = match ::std::panic::catch_unwind(::std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| path(args))) {
    Ok(pruv_r) => pruv_r,
    Err(_) => panic!("pruv: foreign panic: NAME"),
};
```

It now emits a local drop guard and no unwind frame:

```rust
struct pruv_ForeignGuard;
impl ::std::ops::Drop for pruv_ForeignGuard { #[cold] fn drop(&mut self) { let m: &str = "pruv: foreign panic: NAME\u{a}"; #[cfg(unix)] { if let Ok(mut f) = ::std::fs::OpenOptions::new().append(true).open("/dev/stderr") { let _ = ::std::io::Write::write_all(&mut f, m.as_bytes()); return; } } let _ = ::std::io::Write::write_all(&mut ::std::io::stderr(), m.as_bytes()); } }
let pruv_fg = pruv_ForeignGuard;
let result: T = path(args);
::std::mem::forget(pruv_fg);
```

The guard type and binding use the reserved `pruv_` prefix (`pruvc/codegen.py:22`: user identifiers may not start
with `pruv_` or contain `__`), and `Drop` is written by path, so a user type named `Drop` or a parameter named
`PruvForeignGuard` cannot clash (`tests/runtime/g6_guard_names`: both, plus two trusted calls in one fn). Each
wrapper is its own fn, so the item is local to it and two trusted calls never share a scope.

The checks before and after the call (G6_SPEC 12.3 `requires`/`ensures`, owned-result checks) are unchanged.
On unix the guard writes the line through a fresh `/dev/stderr` handle, not through `std::io::stderr()`: std's
stderr is a lock (reentrant on the same thread), and while another thread holds it, for example a host thread that
keeps a `StderrLock` until this call finishes, a `Drop` through `stderr()` waits on it for ever and the unwind never
ends (found by the confirm audit). A raw `write(2, ...)` was tried first and dropped: it needs `unsafe`, and
`--no-verify` Rust output must contain none (`tests/run_all.py` examples check, `g6_min_clamp`). The handle is opened
with `append`, so a regular file on fd 2 is not overwritten. If the open fails (for example fd 2 is a socket on
Linux, where `/dev/stderr` cannot be reopened) the guard falls back to `std::io::stderr()`, and on non-unix targets it
always uses it; only those cases can still wait on the lock. Checked standalone (`work/p19c/lock/lockcheck.rs`, a
second thread holds the lock until the panicking call has unwound): the old text stays blocked after 3 s; the new
text prints the line and the unwind finishes, with fd 2 on a tty, a pipe and a regular file (prior content kept). The
panic hook itself already writes without that lock.
`docs/G6_SPEC.md:536` describes the new form, and G6_SPEC 13.2 now says the LLVM adapter guard is a separate
path and that the helper's `Drop`, not the adapter, prints the trusted-panic line. Both compilers emit the same text (diff_rust, diff_compilers).

### P19c.2 Soundness

What the old wrapper gave, and how each is kept:

| property | old (`catch_unwind` + `panic!`) | new (drop guard) |
|---|---|---|
| a foreign panic never returns a value to Pruv code | the `Err` arm panics again | the unwind continues through the wrapper; `result` is never bound |
| the process prints `pruv: foreign panic: NAME` | message of the second panic | the guard's `Drop` runs during the unwind and writes the line (`tests/runtime/g6_liar_panic.json`: exit 101, stderr contains the line) |
| exit status of a standalone program | 101 (panic out of `main`) | 101 (same unwind out of `main`) |
| Rust backend: P09 `PruvStore::with` poison | the flag is set before the call and cleared only on a normal return; an unwind (second panic) leaves it set | the same flag, the same code; the original panic unwinds through `with` and leaves it set |
| P10 C adapter (`llvmgen.py` `guard`, status 3 `PRUV_PANICKED`) | emitted only in LLVM bindings; a foreign panic never reaches it (the G6 shim adapter exits first, next row), and the Rust backend has no adapter on this path | unchanged: the same, it plays no part in a foreign panic |
| LLVM backend: G6 trusted calls (`foreign_shim.py` `pruv_g6_guard`, G6_SPEC 13.2) | the shim adapter catches the second panic, `fflush(NULL)`, exit 101 | the helper's guard prints the line, then the same adapter catches the original panic, `fflush(NULL)`, exit 101; this path never reaches a P10 adapter |
| `panic = abort` crates | abort in the foreign fn (no unwind to catch) | the same abort |
| unwind safety (`AssertUnwindSafe`) | asserted by the wrapper | not needed: nothing is caught here, so no state is observed after a panic in this frame |

Differences, none observable by Pruv code: the panic payload is the foreign one, not the Pruv message. The
adapters and the poison flag never read the payload (any panic maps to status 3, exit 101 or a set flag). One
tool did: the bench/g6 grader (`bench/g6/run.py`) catches the panic in the generated Rust grader and exits 0, and
`foreign_panic()` in `bench/g6/mutate_ops.py` looked for the Pruv string in the payload, so mutant m60 would have
been graded `wrong_but_verified` on the Rust backend. The grader now keeps the last `pruv: foreign` stderr line as
`foreign_stderr` whatever the exit code, and `foreign_panic()`/`brief()` read it (self-test case added). The panic
hook prints the foreign message before the guard line (both on stderr; the runtime tests check containment). A
panic inside the guard's `Drop` during an unwind would abort; the open and `write_all` return errors instead of
panicking, the result is discarded, and on unix the normal case takes no lock. `mem::forget` of a zero-sized value on the normal path emits no code.
Checked standalone (`work/p19c`): unwind exits 101 with the line, an outer `catch_unwind` catches it,
`panic = abort` exits 134 as before.

What the change removes and what it keeps: `__rust_try` and the catch frame (the closure, the `Result` match and
the re-panic) are gone from every trusted call. A cleanup landing pad remains (the guard's `Drop` call and
`_Unwind_Resume`), off the normal path in the unwind tables; there is no instruction for it on the normal path.

`LocalKey::with` (P19.4): `maybe_close` has one `bl` to `LocalKey::with` (the `bud_facts::answer` closure over
`ANSWERS`, reached through `is_quiet`) in `cur`, `guard` and `direct` (a plain call with no wrapper at all), and 0
in hand16. In `inl` it is 0 in `maybe_close` and appears in its 8 callers instead. The `direct` control shows it
does not depend on the wrapper: it is LLVM's inline decision for the generated caller, not the foreign call path.
A control, `hand_bl` (hand16 with the whole `is_quiet` host call outlined behind an `#[inline(never)]` fn,
`work/p19c/exp/hand_bl.rs`, experiment only), 21 interleaved rounds at S 100, ns/call median [min-max]:
closereopen 14.10 [13.40-40.90] vs hand16 14.10 [13.60-41.40]; attach 12.50 vs 12.30 and reopenmiss 13.80 vs 14.00
(neither reaches `is_quiet`). No difference was detected in this control; it outlines a different call than the
generated one, so it does not bound the cost of the generated `LocalKey::with` `bl`. `bud_facts.rs` is the host and
is not changed.

The guard is kept although its time effect is within spread (P19c.3): it removes `__rust_try` and the catch frame
from every trusted call, and needs no `AssertUnwindSafe`.

(`gen_guard.rs` is byte-identical to `pruvc.py` output): `cur` = the old `catch_unwind` wrapper put back, `guard` =
this change, `direct` = a plain `let result = path(args);` with no wrapper at all (control), `inl` = guard plus

(experiment only, not emitted). Lane order rotates every round and sizes alternate; load 7-11 (other sessions were

divided by 2 x reps, so a close/reopen pair costs twice the closereopen value (guard 31.20 ns per pair). Median
[min-max]:

| closereopen | 500 | 15.60 [15.10-16.90] | 15.60 [15.10-20.60] | 15.60 [15.20-38.70] | 14.50 [13.70-27.00] | 13.90 [13.60-35.10] | 1.122 | 1.122 | 1.122 | 1.043 |
| reopenmiss | 100 | 13.70 [13.40-32.20] | 13.70 [13.40-24.50] | 13.70 [13.40-27.40] | 13.30 [12.70-44.50] | 13.00 [12.70-38.00] | 1.054 | 1.054 | 1.054 | 1.023 |
| reopenmiss | 500 | 13.60 [13.40-14.90] | 13.70 [13.20-23.10] | 13.70 [13.40-50.00] | 13.50 [12.70-19.20] | 12.70 [12.50-20.60] | 1.071 | 1.079 | 1.079 | 1.063 |

On closereopen, the only item that runs the trusted call, `guard` equals `direct` (no wrapper) within 0.1 ns at both
sizes; on attach and reopenmiss, which never execute the wrapper, guard and direct differ by up to 0.2 ns (attach S 100)
with overlapping ranges, which is layout. What is left of the foreign call path costs nothing measurable, so nothing
in it can close the gap to hand16. An earlier 31-round run at load 5-8 (pre-merge)
gave guard 1.11-1.13 and inl 1.01-1.03 on attach/closereopen, the same picture with smaller inl residue.

Instructions per iteration (`boundary 100 R item C`, (instr(5R) - instr(R)) / 4R, R = 20000; an attach or
reopenmiss iteration is one call, a closereopen iteration is a close/reopen pair, two calls). Only closereopen runs
the trusted `is_quiet` call (in `maybe_close`); attach and reopenmiss never execute the wrapper, so their cur/guard
difference is layout, not the wrapper:

| item | unit | cur | guard | inl |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| attach | call | 567 | 561 | 496 |
| closereopen | pair | 1217 | 1221 | 1127 |
| reopenmiss | call | 534 | 523 | 454 |

The instruction counts are from the pre-merge source (P21a); the merge changes no compiler code and no
lifecycle path these items run except through `bud_map` (P21b), so they are kept as the per-path split, and the
timing above is the final evidence.

Observed wrapper difference: closereopen guard - cur = 0.0 ns per call in the final run (15.60 both sizes) and
-0.5 ns per call in the earlier run, with overlapping ranges, so no time gain is claimed beyond the removed `__rust_try`;
attach and reopenmiss differences (0.0-0.1 ns) are layout noise (no wrapper on their path).

| line | hand16 | generated | instr | class | owner |

`room`, `put_at`, `settle_at` are not on these paths (0).

### P19c.5 Queued

- **T5 (inline policy):** with `find_w` and the three lifecycle bodies `#[inline(always)]`, attach goes 1.13 -> 1.04-1.05x
  (1.02-1.03x in the quieter pre-merge run) and closereopen 1.11-1.12 -> 1.04x (1.01-1.03x), the ranges overlapping
  hand16; 65 fewer instructions per attach call and 94 per close/reopen pair (47 per call). Evidence that it is not
  the foreign path: `guard` = `direct`, so the gap is the same with no foreign wrapper at all.
  The policy is shared by both compilers (`pruvc/data/inline_policy.json`, text-size rule) and changes every program,
  so it is T5's, not the foreign call path's; measure the policy change against the M4/M7/M8/M10 lanes there.
- **P18b:** `reopenmiss` 1.02-1.06x with inl (hypothesis: the status + out-buffer result vs a register return), the `attach` id copy and the
  empty-clock count, with the register-return isolating measurement of that row.

(main, P21b + P22; unchanged, no merge needed). Changed files: `bench/l3/budget/{bud_map.pruv,bud_lifecycle.pruv,ABI.md}`,

q_gate_control.py,lifecycle_controls.py,mutant_quiet.py,cases.exact.json,cases_life.exact.json}`,
`bench/l3/budget/m10_test/{driver_m10.rs,run_m10.py,cases.exact.json,cases_halt.exact.json}`. No compiler file,
`bud_clock.pruv` or `m9_test` change. Raw logs: `work/p19a/` (not committed).

### P19a.1 Change

- R1: `bud_map::room` splits into `room_plan` (decision only, no writes) and `room_apply` (`ensures p != -1 ==>`
  `st` unchanged word for word). `maybe_close` plans before `is_quiet` and rebuilds the slot table only after
  answer 1, before the first `out` write. Answer 0 or an invalid answer (status 2) leaves raw `st` unchanged
  (`docs/REQUEST_BUDGET_SPEC.md:813`). A positive Grow returns before the query.
- R2: `lifecycle_controls.py` adds an attach fixture. The id is declared past the end of its record, a neighbour
  session follows, and the fixture expects status 2 with `st`, `fx` and `out` unchanged.
- R3: `is_quiet(k, ks, kn, fxn)` also takes the effect count so far (`fx[0]`). `bud_facts` logs each query with the
  packed session key, its length and the effect count, on both the Pruv and hand16 sides. `mutant_quiet.py` builds
  three mutants: effect before the query, wrong (empty) key, and rehash before the query.
- R4: the M7 and M10 drivers check each attempt over a forced Grow.
  - The first attempt must return a negative status with 0 queries and `st/fx/out` unchanged.
  - The retry with answer 0, 1 or 2 must make exactly 1 query and give the exact result and effects. With answer 2
    the `out` marker must also be kept.
- R5: `q_gate.py` pins the required exact case ids to the corpus sha256 in `*.exact.json`. Q fails when every
  case is not-implemented, and it also fails when the expected request order is reversed. `q_gate_control.py`
  checks both runners.
- R6: a standalone CLOSE lane on both sides. The reset runs outside timing, and both sides consume the same
  `(status, tag)` per call.
- O1: `ABI.md` describes `isQuiet` as a synchronous host call (`op[2]` is reserved 0) and states the packed key
  span, status 2 on an invalid answer, and the effect count in the query log.
- Package-audit fixes (this commit; harness and spec only, no Pruv change):
  - R5 manifest: a missing manifest for a canonical corpus (`cases`, `cases_life`, `cases_halt`) is a failure
    (`FAIL Q ... required-id manifest ... is missing`). Before, it meant "no required ids", so 1 exact and 299
    not-implemented passed. Other corpora still get an empty set.
  - R5 reproducibility: §M10 now states the exact generator command (`--families Q4,Q5 --per-family 150`; the
    sha256 of `--count 300` differs because it interleaves the two families) and says that `run_m10.py derive`
    makes `cases_halt.jsonl` from that file. Regenerated corpora match all four manifests (sha `c0bec614...` for
    M10).
  - R6 count: CLOSE `prep` and `observe` now run exactly `reps` ops, cycling `k % size`, and are divided by `reps`
    like A and C. Before, they ran `reps x size` ops.
  - R6 restore: the instruction counts of `perf` and `boundary` skip `close` (`NO_INSTR_ITEMS`; boundary prints `-`). The per-batch restore is
    outside the ns timer but inside the process instruction counter, and it differs by side: Pruv copies raw
    `st`, while hand16 calls `put(rec.clone())` for each session. The time asymmetry is measured in P19a.3.
  - R6 key: hand16 wire passes the verified packed key span of the original op (`op[12..sk_end]`) straight to
    `is_quiet`, as Pruv does. The typed path packs the key into a 64-word stack buffer, with a heap fallback above
    256 units. No bench key reaches the heap path.
  - R6 self-check: `run_boundary` steps the reference world and the candidate world in lockstep and compares
    `(out, fx, bv, st)` after each call, in linear space. Before, it kept a snapshot of every call (quadratic).

### P19a.3 Time (Rust backend, ns per op, interleaved rounds, floor 1.0x)

Rounds alternate the four lanes (`work/p19a/close_ab.py`, `item_ab.py`). A difference counts as noise only when
the interquartile ranges overlap.

| cell | Pruv (IQR) | hand16 (IQR) | ratio | verdict |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| close wire, size 100, 21 rounds | 57.9 (57.2-59.1) | 57.4 (56.5-58.5) | 1.009 | overlap, noise |
| close typed, size 100, 21 rounds | 30.3 (29.9-30.6) | 26.8 (26.5-27.4) | 1.131 | no overlap, explained below |
| close typed, size 100, hand with matched restore, 15 rounds | 31.3 (30.5-32.1) | 30.9 (30.2-36.2) | 1.013 | overlap, noise |
| close wire, size 500, 15 rounds | 125.2 (118.1-127.1) | 119.4 (118.3-121.6) | 1.049 | overlap, noise |
| close typed, size 500, 15 rounds | 30.9 | 30.6 | 1.010 | overlap, noise |
| current typed, size 100, 15 rounds | 13.1 (12.8-13.2) | 12.6 (12.5-13.0) | 1.040 | overlap, noise |
| current wire, size 100 / 500 | - | - | 0.647 / 0.640 | below 1.0x |
| current typed, size 500 | - | - | 1.008 | overlap, noise |

Close typed at size 100 explained line by line (`work/p19a/close_evict.log`):

- Before each batch of `size` calls, outside the ns span, the lane restores the state.
  - Pruv copies raw `st`: 32768 words (256 KiB) at size 100, 131072 words at size 500.
  - hand16 rewrites only its few small session records.
  - So Pruv evicts the cache lines that the next batch reads, and hand16 does not.
- Matched control: hand16 copies a 32768-word buffer on each restore (`EVW=32768`). Alternated with Pruv, it gives
  30.9 vs 31.3 (1.013, overlap).
- Without the copy, hand16 itself also rises from 26.8 (size 100) to 30.6 (size 500), while Pruv stays flat. The
  gap is the harness restore, not the close path.
- The close path itself does one `room_plan`, one `is_quiet` and, on answer 1, `room_apply`, with no allocation.

The P19 cells attach, closereopen and reopenmiss are not touched by P19a. Their earlier measurements stay as P19
records them.

### P19a.4 Hand vs generated

The two sides make the same host call. hand16 wire passes the original packed key span as Pruv does, and typed
hand16 packs onto the stack. Pruv's close runs on the flat store, with one span check per entry and the write-free
plan. hand16 uses a hash map of structs. The two close paths are within noise of each other once the restore
traffic is matched.

### P19a.5 RSS and allocations

Allocations: close is 0 per call on every Pruv variant and on hand16 (boundary log, hand count), and close does
not grow `st`.

Peak RSS in bytes (`/usr/bin/time -l`). The earlier note of 950272 B came from a different setup, could not be
reproduced this way, and is replaced:

| process | Pruv driver | hand16 |
|---|---:|---:|
| baseline (noop B / perf none) | 2981888 | 1638400 |
| close, size 100, reps 1 | 4046848 | 2097152 |
| close, size 100, reps 200000 | 3309568 (C), 3768320 (A) | 2097152 (typed), 2179072 (wire) |
| close, size 500, reps 200000 | 6864896 | 3375104 |

- The excess is flat in reps.
- It grows with the session count, because the store layout keeps one i64 per UTF-16 unit and a power-of-two
  arena: at 100 sessions, `st` is 256 KiB for about 112 KiB of live data.
- Every M7 lane shares this layout, so it is not new in P19a. The driver also has a higher fixed baseline, which
  is code size (P13d).
- Queued (P19a.7).

## Appendix P16/P17a (both verifiers: eq_range content and frames; both LLVM emitters: eq_range lowering)

### P16/P17a.1 Verifier encoding (P16)

`pruvc/verify.py` and `pruvc-rs/crates/pruv-proof/src/symbolic.rs`, the `eq_range` call:

- The five bounds obligations stay as they were, in order: `0 <= i`, `0 <= j`, `0 <= n`, `i + n <= len(a)`,
  `j + n <= len(b)` (`index_oob`, same messages).
- Then a fresh bool `r` (`eq_range!N`) and a fresh bound variable `k` (`eq_range!q<N>`), and on the call's path
  `assume r == ForAll k. (0 <= k && k < n) ==> a[i+k] == b[j+k]`.
- `a` and `b` are the array terms at the call, so a later write to either array does not change `r` (frame). `r` is
  fresh, so the assumption is a definition and cannot make the path inconsistent.
- The quantifier has the shape of a contract `forall k in 0..n: a[i+k] == b[j+k]`, so user contracts in that form
  match it directly. No patterns are given; both z3 bindings pick the same default triggers.

Tests: `tests/l3/proof/eq_range_content.pruv` (both directions for `[i64]` and `[u8]`, a point fact in the true
branch, empty range, same array at the same start, a constant array against itself shifted, frame after a store
outside the range; default and `--infer` rows). Must reject (both compilers, same code and position):
`l3_eq_range_false_true` (bounds alone do not make it true), `l3_eq_range_empty_false` (`n == 0` is true),
`l3_eq_range_alias_shift` (a shifted self-compare is not always true), `l3_eq_range_frame` (a store inside the
compared range after the call), `l3_eq_range_one_elem` (one equal element is not two), `l3_eq_range_past_end`
(nothing is known about `a[n]`). The existing bounds negatives (`l3_eq_range_i`, `_ia`, `_j`, `_jb`, `_n`, `_mixed`,
`_bool`, `_contract`, `l3_cx_calls_eq_range`) are unchanged.

### P16/P17a.2 Solver cost (P16)

flags (the proof cache is opt-in, so every run verifies from scratch), 5 interleaved rounds with alternating order,
wall seconds p10 / p50 / p90 and peak RSS. Another package was measuring on the same machine at the same time, so
single p90 values carry outliers (m8 `py_new` 36.6 s, `rs_old` 28.3 s); judge by the overlap of p10..p50.

| workload | py old p10/p50/p90 | py new | rs old | rs new | RSS MB py old/new, rs old/new |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| m8 budget root | 12.46 / 13.26 / 24.75 | 11.68 / 13.47 / 36.60 | 6.72 / 7.84 / 28.29 | 6.65 / 7.63 / 8.65 | 132 / 131, 126 / 127 |
| m9 budget root | 11.60 / 12.89 / 13.80 | 12.01 / 13.77 / 14.85 | 6.54 / 7.29 / 7.82 | 6.54 / 7.36 / 7.58 | 128 / 140, 135 / 133 |

| `l3_rt_eq_range` | 0.098 / 0.105 / 0.114 | 0.098 / 0.104 / 0.107 | 0.030 / 0.047 / 0.111 | 0.030 / 0.034 / 0.127 | 55 / 55, 46 / 46 |
| `l3_rt_eq_range_edges` | 0.130 / 0.136 / 0.139 | 0.130 / 0.142 / 0.164 | 0.044 / 0.050 / 0.058 | 0.046 / 0.047 / 0.052 | 55 / 56, 47 / 47 |
| `eq_range_content` | rejected (rc 1) | 0.145 / 0.157 / 0.209 | rejected (rc 1) | 0.073 / 0.080 / 0.084 | 57 / 57, 48 / 49 |
