### P16/P17a.3 LLVM lowering (P17a)

`pruvc/llvmgen.py` and `pruvc-rs/crates/pruv-core/src/llvmgen.rs` emit byte-identical IR (checked on
`l3_rt_eq_range`, `l3_rt_eq_range_edges`, `eq_range_content` and the perf module, default and `--no-verify`).

- Arguments are evaluated left to right. Under `--no-verify` one combined check (`0 <= i`, `0 <= j`, `0 <= n`,
  `i + n <= len a`, `j + n <= len b`) calls `pruv_panic_oob(i, len a)`.
- Layout guard: both operands `[u8]` bytes, or both 64-bit element storage. Anything else is `codegen` error
  `unsupported_type` ("eq_range is not supported by the llvm codegen layer for this array layout yet"; a non-array
  operand: "... for this operand yet"). A `[u8]` operand is stored as bytes, and the storage plan keeps an `[i64]`
  operand as 64-bit elements even when it is refined, so a `[i64 | lo..=hi]` operand takes the i64 path (`same_nw` in
  the edges test) and the guard is not reached today.
- Literal `n == 0`: `true`, with no compare (after the `--no-verify` check). `alloc(0)` may give a null data pointer,
  and `memcmp(null, null, 0)` is undefined behaviour. A dynamic `n == 0` takes the loop, which does no loads.
- Literal `n > 0`: `memcmp(pa, pb, n * sz) == 0` with a constant size (LLVM expands small constant sizes into wide loads).
- Dynamic `n`: `n >= 4` (`EQR_LOOP_MAX`) branches to `memcmp`, else an inline early-exit element loop; a phi joins
  them. The `memcmp` block is the taken successor of the branch.
- `tests/llvm_pending.txt` no longer lists `l3_rt_eq_range`; `tests/runtime/l3_rt_eq_range_edges` (empty range at the
  end, full range, first/last element differs, same array, overlapping shift, 100-byte and 40-element ranges, literal
  3/64, refined against plain) runs on both backends, both compilers, default and `--no-verify`.
- `tests/runtime/l3_rt_eq_range_order` (each argument prints a tag: the five arguments are evaluated once each, in
  source order, on both backends; a literal 0 over empty `[i64]` and `[u8]` arrays is true) and
  `tests/runtime/l3_rt_eq_range_nv_oob` (`--no-verify`, `i` near i64 max so `i + n` would overflow: `pruv_oob`).
- The Rust source backend (`pruvc/codegen.py`, `pruvc-rs/crates/pruv-core/src/codegen.rs`) used to bind `i, j, n`
  before the arrays, and its `--no-verify` form repeated the array expressions; it now binds `a, i, b, j, n` once each,
  in source order (`let pruv_ea = ...; let pruv_i = ...; ...`).

### P16/P17a.4 Perf against hand Rust (P17a)

`work/p16/perf/` (not committed): a pruv search-count loop (`eq_range(h, p, nd, 0, n)` at every position of a 4096
haystack) compiled with `--backend llvm`, linked into a Rust driver against the same loop over hand Rust
`h[p..p+n] == nd[..n]`; 41 interleaved rounds, median and p10/p90 in ns per position, random and all-equal data.
Arm64, `clang -O2 -mcpu=native`, `rustc -C opt-level=3 -C target-cpu=native`.

| case | pruv/hand (median) | distributions |
|---|---|---|
| `[u8]` dynamic n = 1, 2 | 0.27-0.39 | pruv faster |
| `[i64]` dynamic n = 1, 2, 3 | 0.36-0.90 | pruv faster |
| `[u8]` dynamic n = 4 .. 256 | 1.000-1.009 | overlap |
| `[i64]` dynamic n = 4, 8, 32 | 0.997-1.027 | overlap |
| literal `[u8]` 8, 64; literal `[i64]` 2 | 0.977-1.000 | overlap |

Peak RSS of the two drivers: pruv 14270464 / 14286848 bytes, hand 14254080 / 14270464 bytes (at most one 16 KiB page
apart, inside the run-to-run spread of either driver).

Threshold history (why 4 elements, not the planned 32 bytes):
- A 32-byte threshold with a loop for literal counts: literal loops 5-6x hand, `[u8]` dynamic 8-24 bytes on
  all-equal data up to 5.7x hand (a byte loop against a wide-load compare). So literal counts always use `memcmp`, and
  the loop is kept only below 4 elements, where it beats hand Rust's `memcmp` call.
- With the loop block as the taken successor, the dynamic `memcmp` path measured 1.2x hand; making `memcmp` the
  taken target removes it (all n >= 4 cells overlap).
- Apple clang does not turn `memcmp` into `bcmp`; hand Rust also calls `_memcmp` on this target.

- §3.1/§6 text that says LLVM rejects `eq_range` is history from before P17a.
- `SPEC.md` eq_range bullet updated (verifier result, LLVM lowering).

The commit with this appendix; base 82be91b (main, P19a), main a7f7e68 (P16/P17a) merged before the final gates.

and `bench/l3/budget/M9_NOTES.md`. No compiler file, `bud_clock.pruv`, `bud_map.pruv` or `bud_lifecycle.pruv`
change: the FIRE, DROP and CLOSE paths P22 left in `bud_clock.pruv` already met the row once it was tested. Raw
logs: `work/p23/` (not committed).

### P23.1 Change

- `root_m9::t_live` returns the store's live-entry total (header word 12), so the harness can count reclaimed
  entries.
- `run_m9.py`:
  - `derive --family q4` builds a clock-only Q4 set (raise/charge calls removed, TS oracle rerun).
  - `dc` runs 300 random build/DROP/CLOSE programs (R = 0..12) and 13 reclaim programs (20 build/DROP cycles each).
    At each checkpoint it compares budget, clocks, timers and C/F events with a Python model. It also checks that
    DROP/CLOSE reclaim exactly R + 1 entries, that capacity does not grow over the cycles, and that a FIRE after
    DROP or CLOSE does nothing.
  - `q` fails when a non-empty case set ran no I2 check.
  - `--out` puts the generated Rust and binaries in a chosen directory. A `--budlib` build without `--out` gets a
    fresh directory under `work/m9/budlib`.

    fails on a missing item, and prints `HOLD` and fails for a median above 1.0x hand whose distributions do not
    overlap.
- `gen_stale.py`: 300 seeded FIRE scenarios (budget replaced, unlimited, halted, closed, null session, waiting,
  ended, mixed) with the TS oracle.
- `mut_m9.py`: six new timer mutants (m5-m10) besides the four I2 mutants. `--jobs N` runs mutants in parallel.
  Each campaign gets a fresh directory under `work/m9/mut`, and each mutant its own lib copy and build directory
  inside it, so neither parallel mutants nor concurrent campaigns share a binary (P22.7 H6).
- `driver_m9.rs`:
  - a timer captures its FIRE op (code 4, sessionId record, budgetId record) and its bid bytes when it is set;
  - delivery, including a stale delivery, replays that op with the stored bid. It no longer decodes and re-encodes
    keys per callback, and the captured ids are the ones from set time, as in B;
  - the drop/close perf rows time only the DROP or CLOSE call, with a time limit under the host timer cap; the fire
    row uses a time limit over the cap so no rep count spends the budget (P23.6a).

### P23.4 Hand vs generated

DROP and CLOSE are faster than hand Rust. Hand Rust frees R `String` run keys from per-clock maps one at a time,
while Pruv's `bud_map::remove` frees the entries inside one flat store. fire and cycle keep the P22 gap.

Stale FIRE, line by line (P23 71.4 vs hand 63.0 ns):
- Boundary. Hand Rust has none: its arguments are typed `&str`. `t_call` checks `valid(st)` (header and dynamic
  part), `rec_end` + `slice_ok` for 3 records, `fx_ok` and `len(bv)`. About 4 ns.
- CURRENT. Hand Rust does `sessions.get` and a `budget_id` compare. `load_bv` does the same find and unit compare,
  plus field-address checks.
- Effects. Hand Rust has no effect step. The host reads the fx frame (Grow retry loop, fx scan, scratch key
  take/restore, halt log). About 5 ns.
- Timer map. Both sides do the same `by_bid.remove` (SipHash), about 24 ns.

Pruv cannot emit the hand code without a typed entry: the boundary check is what makes the flat `[i64]` op safe to
index. Queued (P23.7).

## Appendix P13d (row both codegens: generated code size of the M4 driver)

### P13d.1 Result

No compiler change; the row's size target is not met and is queued. No inline policy alone brings the M4 Pruv
binary's resident `__TEXT` to hand's 240 KiB: the smallest (budget 0) reaches 272 and only reaches 240 with the
driver's `q` adapter also removed. Every smaller policy costs time: +10-16% instructions and +9-16% cycles on
sessions (ia1500 to b0), up to +11% on tools and clocks, so it breaks "time not worse than P13c"; the shipped
binary is below hand in cycles on all nine cells, but already above hand in sessions instructions (186 vs 182 M),
and b0 adds 14% more there. The shipped policy (R-7-3, `incl<=8 | sites<=1 |
incl*(sites-1)<=1500`) is the best point measured for time; its size cost is written down below and queued (P13h).
Base: main 22332cd. Raw logs and tools: `work/p13d/` (not committed). Binaries are the M4 driver plus generated code
(`driver_m4.rs` + `root_m4`), and `m4_hand.rs`, each with a 4 s pause hook after the result line for `vmmap`,
all built with `rustc -C opt-level=3 --edition 2021` (no other flag on either side).

### P13d.2 What resident `__TEXT` measures

`vmmap` resident `__TEXT` was the same on all three cells measured (sessions 100, tools 1000, clocks 100), so it
does not depend on the workload. The linker lays out own code (driver, generated module, and in hand the hashbrown
monomorphs) first in `__text`, then std. The own-code pages are nearly all touched; the std pages touched are about
the same set on both sides. So resident `__TEXT` = (own-code size rounded to 16 KiB pages) + a fixed std part:

| binary | own code KiB | `__text` B | resident `__TEXT` KiB |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| hand (`m4_hand.rs`: `selftest` 10.9, `main` 6.3, `State::exec` 2.4, hashbrown about 10) | 37.3 | 282,620 | 240 |
| Pruv shipped (b1500; `World::exec` 53.3, `main` with q mode 9.7, `import_check` 7.5, `put_at` 6.1, `remove` 4.8, `observe` 4.5, `new` 3.4) | 91.6 | 339,516 | 304 |
| Pruv shipped, q-mode body replaced by `exit(9)` (b1500noq, test only) | | | 288 |
| policy `incl` counts all non-recursive callees, budget 1500 (ia1500) | | 319,612 | 288 |
| same, budget 300 (ia300) | | 303,548 | 272 |
| budget 0 (b0: only `incl<=8` and single-site fns forced) | 57.6 | 304,700 | 272 |
| budget 0, no q mode (b0noq, test only) | 40.8 | | 240 |

The `mincore` page map is not usable on macOS for this (it reports page-cache residency, every page shows resident).

| cell | hand | shipped | ia1500 | ia300 | b300 | b0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| sessions 100 | 181.98 | 186.39 | 205.87 | 217.04 | 206.24 | 213.27 |
| sessions 1000 | 186.27 | 194.71 | 214.14 | 225.78 | 214.23 | 221.54 |
| tools 100 | 823.37 | 521.00 | 530.39 | 562.33 | 562.75 | 577.05 |

### P13d.5 Why Pruv does not emit hand's code size (line by line)

1. Hash map logic is Pruv code, not a shared std/hashbrown monomorph. Hand's `State::exec` is 2.4 KB and calls
   hashbrown (about 10 KB of reserve/rehash/find monomorphs) and std's SipHash (in the std part counted on both sides).
   Pruv's map (`bud_map.pruv`: slot probe, `put_at`, `remove`, `rehash`, `room_plan`/`room_apply`, `put_key_h`)
   and store (`bud_store.pruv`, `bud_world.pruv`: `put_blob`, `copy_node`) are generated into the binary; with no
   inlining at all beyond the size-8 rule (b0) this is about 27 KB of `sol` plus a 14 KB `exec`. This is the P13e
   layout and library question, not a codegen defect.
2. Inlining duplicates that logic per op. The shipped policy puts `make_room` (with `room` -> `room_plan`,
   `room_apply`, `rehash`, `need`), `put_blob`, `add_w`, `put_key_h`, `del_key` and `copy_node` into each op arm of
   `World::exec` (53 KB vs 14 KB at b0). This is what makes Pruv faster than hand in cycles on all nine cells
   (P13d.3). Hand Rust gets the same speed without the duplication because hashbrown's hot path is a few small
   inlined probes and the cold `reserve_rehash` stays one out-of-line copy; Rust attributes are per function, so
   Pruv cannot say "inline at the hot call sites only" without a call-site attribute or a split into hot and cold
   bodies, and LLVM does not do that split here (no profile, MachO has no machine function splitter by default).
3. Total accessors are explicit code. `ent_u16::rd`/`wr`/`clamp` (and `c32`/`c40`, `hw`/`hd` built on them) are
   defined total by the library ("defence in depth", `bench/l3/lib/ent_u16.pruv:1-19,182-191`): each inlined use is
   a compare and a branch or select (in shipped `exec`: 640 `b.hs`, 515 `csel` of 13,300 lines). Where the verifier
   proves the index in range at the call, that check is dead, but the codegen has no channel from a call-site proof to
   the callee's body today; P13h below.
4. Test adapter in the measured binary. The Pruv driver carries `q` mode (`import_check` 7.5 KB, the `q_mode` loop
   inlined into `main`, word parsing), never run in perf, 16 KiB resident; hand carries `selftest` (10.9 KB),
   also never run. Both are in the own-code pages, so the comparison already includes an adapter on each side; this is
   not removed with a Pruv-only flag (`driver_m4.rs` belongs to P13f).

| driver | Pruv own code KiB | hand own code KiB | Pruv `__text` B | hand `__text` B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| M7 (`root` + `driver_m7.rs`; hand `hand_m7.rs` / `hand_m7_u16.rs`) | 151.5 | 14.2 / 59.4 | 405,180 | 253,692 / 311,484 |

### T5.1 Change

  M4, M7, M8 and M10 is byte-identical between the pre-move Python compiler, the new Python compiler and the new Rust
  compiler.

  thresholds (8/9 lines, budget 1500/1501), written with the spec values and not read from the JSON, were added to
  `tests/check_generated.py` (Python) and `inline_policy_thresholds` (pruvc-rs). This closes TIDY_SPEC section 4 item 12
  for the inline thresholds; the `MAX_TYPE_APPS`/`MAX_TYPE_NODES` pairs of that item are not part of T5.
- Generated output is unchanged on every root, so `tests/g8/compatibility.json` keeps its hashes. M4, M8 and M10
  binaries are the same as before T5 and were not re-timed.

### T5.2 Why no rule ships (M7, `work/t5/s2/`)

Every rule that makes the P19c bodies inline buys instructions with code pages. The AGENTS.md section 5 rule
(2026-11-19) forbids trading a large loss on one axis for a small gain on the other, so none of these ships.

Variants were built from the shipped M7 output by flipping `#[inline]` to `#[inline(always)]` on the named fns:
- `f` = find_w.
- `a` = attach.
- `fa` = find_w + attach.
- `r` = reopen + maybe_close.
- `inl` = the four P19c fns.
- `cand` = a rule experiment that replaced call sites with "the most copies one entry fn (a `pub fn` or a fn that is
  not `#[inline]`) can hold through inline paths". It promoted maybe_close, reopen and replace. It did not promote
  attach (3 copies, incl 964) or find_w (23 copies).

Instructions per op are `(I(5R) - I(R)) / 4R`, with R = 20000, S = 100, median of 3 runs. They come from
`/usr/bin/time -l`, on `driver boundary 100 R ITEM C` and on `hand_m7_u16 perf 100 R ITEM typed`. The hand column
includes no driver variant loop, so compare across Pruv columns only. `__text` is from `size -m`.

| item | base | f | a | fa | r | inl | hand16 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| current | 1297 | 1270 | 1301 | 1260 | 1300 | 1264 | 333 |
| ishalted | 498 | 469 | 498 | 465 | 498 | 465 | 338 |
| attach | 620 | 626 | 575 | 541 | 623 | 543 | 320 |
| close | 1256 | 1258 | 1259 | 1258 | 1252 | 1232 | 2435 |
| closereopen | 1378 | 1354 | 1382 | 1356 | 1339 | 1285 | 890 |
| reopenmiss | 553 | 526 | 555 | 525 | 520 | 482 | 334 |
| replace | 3028 | 2991 | 3043 | 2969 | 3033 | 2975 | 3064 |
| `__text` B | 405,180 | 434,876 | 508,284 | 568,764 | 651,324 | 873,660 | 311,484 |

How each rule trades:
- `cand` (the per-entry copies rule) gives 1-6 % fewer instructions for 759,100 B of `__text`.
- `f` is the cheapest point: 2-6 % fewer instructions on lookups for +29.7 KB (+7 %).
- The attach saving (−13 %) needs `fa`: +40 % text.
- `inl` costs +116 % text.

Resident text is fixed-share memory (code pages, independent of data size, P13d.2). The M7 Pruv binary is already
above hand16 there: 405 vs 311 KB of `__text`. Peak RSS (`perf 100 100000`, 3 runs) is 4.9-5.4 MB for base, f, fa and
inl alike, against 2.7 MB for hand16. So the proportional share, state, is the larger excess (P13e). The inline
variants do not change it beyond the spread.

Wall-clock timing was too noisy to read (load average about 10, ranges overlapping on every item; raw run in
`work/t5/s2/m7_run1.txt`). Only instructions and sizes are used above.

### T5.3 What remains of the P19c gap

The gap to hand16 is mostly not inlining. Even with `inl`, attach is 543 against 320, and P19c's attribution names
other sources:
- entry and length checks;
- record re-validation;
- id copies;
- the closereopen field walk.

The find_w share comes from its always callees (own body 3 lines, incl 440). Inlining find_w copies those 440 lines
again into each caller. A no-loss fix has to cut that body, for example the P13h call-site specialization or a
hot/cold split, rather than add copies. Queued as row T5a.

## Appendix P25 (row B/bud_card.pruv: card validation and projection on JB packets)

The commit with this appendix; base 22332cd (main, P19c). Main did not move during P25. Changed files:
`bench/l3/budget/bud_card.pruv` and `bench/l3/budget/m11_test/{root.pruv,harness.rs,hand.rs,run_m11.py}`. No compiler
file, `bud_halt.pruv`, `m10_test` or `bud_map`/`bud_store`/`bud_world`/`bud_admit` layout change. Raw logs: `work/p25/`
(not committed).

### P25.1 Change

- `bud_card.pruv` reads the card, `lang` and `by` arguments of setCard as JB byte packets (`[u8]`, big-endian: tags
  1-4, 7 + f64, 6 + u32 + WTF-8, 8 + u32 count, 9 + u32 count + (u32 klen, key, value); depth <= 32; empty = absent).
  The stored budget, `ref` and the result stay in the old V-word ABI.
  - `j_ok` admits the whole packet once (structure, depth, canonical WTF-8 per string; a lead surrogate directly
    followed by a trail surrogate is rejected). `card_at` scans the card object once (last duplicate key wins, as
    `JSON.parse`) and `validate` judges the fields in the B order (kinds 1-6).
  - Text fields use ECMAScript trim (`ws_at`/`ws_before`: TAB-CR, SP, NBSP, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+2028/2029, U+202F,
    U+205F, U+3000, BOM) and `1 <= units <= 300` UTF-16 units after the trim. `targets.note` uses the raw, untrimmed
    length `<= 300` (spec line 96). Counts are JS Numbers: finite, integral, >= 0, `-0` accepted; `safe_int` projects
    a safe integer, the rest keep the raw bits.
  - `units(b, s, e, cap)` counts UTF-16 units by lead bytes (+1 for c < 128 or c >= 192, +1 more for c >= 240) and stops
    once the count passes `cap`, so a bound failure short-circuits. `text_ok` does not trim first: `cut(b, ts, e, 300)`
    returns the first unit start `q` where the count would pass 300; the text is too long iff `q < e` and a
    non-whitespace byte follows `q` (`tr_s(b, q, e) < e`), else valid iff `tr_e(b, ts, q) > ts`. A long text with a
    long whitespace tail is refused after 301 units and one more character, not after the whole tail (audit item 3). `put_units` writes exactly `u` words (surrogate
    pairs for 4-byte sequences, lone surrogates as themselves).
  - `build` runs a size pass into an empty array and a write pass into `zeros(size)`: one allocation per card.
  - ASCII fast paths: `ascii8` (one 8-byte load and a `0x80..80` mask) and `ascii32` (four loads OR-ed, one test) in
    `wtf8_ok`; `ascii8` in both `units` loops and in `put_units` (eight word stores per step). Each inner loop carries
    `i0 <= i` (the entry position) so the outer `decreases e - i` still proves.
  - Types: `[u8]` packets, `i64` UTF-16 words in the V output; no per-unit `i64` packet and no flat record arrays.
- `m11_test/root.pruv`: `m11_set_card`, `m11_perf_card` and `m11_perf_chain` take `[u8]` packets and admit them with
  `j_ok` before any judgment. `by` is admitted with `j_ok_at(by, 4)`: it is stored at V depth 4 inside the setCard
  result (`{ok, budget}` 1, budget 2, card 3, `by` 4), so its packet depth is at most 29; a deeper `by` is refused
  (status 2) before any state change (audit item 1). The error result `{ok: false, error}` needs `5 + 14 + n` words,
  not `5 + 15 + n` (audit item 2, present since 22332cd).
- `m11_test/run_m11.py`: `to_b`/`from_b` JB codec (WTF-8 of JS strings, lone surrogates kept), `--selftest-b`;
  `judge` reports a result V that does not end at its last word.
- `m11_test/hand.rs`: the hand Rust baseline on JB packets (`admit`, `validate`, `build`, `put_card`, `Store::set_card`)
  with `is_ascii` fast paths; `harness.rs`: JB argument lines, perf items A/B/C on packets, and an `hdiff` command
  (hand vs Pruv on one card, kind and output words).

### P25.3 Time (Rust backend, ns per call, 15 interleaved rounds base/P25/hand, one process per measurement)

`work/p25/perf.py 15`, log `work/p25/perf_final.log`, load average 6-7; A and C re-measured after the audit fixes
(`perf.py 15 AC`, `work/p25/perf_audit.log`): new `text_ok`, and C with the hand card admitted once outside the loop
like the Pruv side, outside the timer (audit item 4 and its confirm). The C rows are the confirm run
(`perf.py 21 C`, `work/p25/perf_confirm2.log`) under load average 18-22, so both ranges are wide. A = admit + validate + build of one card
(deliverable and 5 done lines of `"  " + "a" * U + "  "`), U = 1000 is the > 300 refusal; B = n successive setCard
calls through the store; C = the bud_card part of B (set_card + put_card on one in-memory budget). Overlap compares the
P25 and hand min-max ranges.

| cell | base | P25 | hand | P25/hand median | P25/hand min | overlap |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| A U = 100 | 421.4 | 478.3 | 750.6 | 0.64 | 0.62 | yes (one P25 outlier 972) |
| A U = 300 | 573.3 | 822.3 | 1628.1 | 0.51 | 0.50 | no (Pruv faster) |
| A U = 1000 | 17.8 | 133.7 | 227.7 | 0.59 | 0.58 | no (Pruv faster) |
| B n = 100 | 634.2 | 578.2 | 659.9 | 0.88 | 0.87 | no (Pruv faster) |
| B n = 500 | 669.1 | 613.8 | 688.7 | 0.89 | 0.89 | no (Pruv faster) |
| B n = 1000 | 634.8 | 583.4 | 657.3 | 0.89 | 0.89 | no (Pruv faster) |
| C n = 100 | 496.2 | 481.4 | 626.5 | 0.77 | 0.74 | yes (load 18-22, both ranges wide) |
| C n = 1000 | 648.1 | 488.7 | 637.8 | 0.77 | 0.72 | yes (load 18-22, both ranges wide) |

- Base reads V words whose strings already carry their UTF-16 length, so its A cells skip admission and its U = 1000
  refusal reads one length word (15.6 ns). P25 and hand take bytes and must admit the whole ~6 KB packet first
  (canonical WTF-8), so A grows over base by the O(V) admission and the unit count; both sides pay it, P25 at
  0.49-0.60x hand.
- Before the ASCII fast paths (`work/p25/perf1.log`, 9 rounds) A was 1.43x / 1.92x / 8.08x hand: `wtf8_ok` and
  `units` went byte by byte where hand calls `is_ascii`. With `ascii8` only (`perf2.log`) A U = 1000 was still
  1.28x; `ascii32` in `wtf8_ok` brought it to 0.60x.
- Cost bound: setCard = the P19c cost + O(V + U). `j_ok` visits each packet byte once (strings by word, keys once),
  `card_at` scans each object's keys once, `validate` counts units with `cap = 300` (early exit; a > 300 text field
  stops after 300 units and one more character, whatever its whitespace tail), `build` is two passes over the kept fields (size, write). A bound failure
  returns at the first failing field in the B order.

### P25.4 Hand vs generated

All cells are under 1.0x (medians 0.51-0.89x); in the overlapping cells (A U = 100, C n = 100 and 1000) the overlap
comes from outlier rounds on both sides, while the P25 median and minimum stay below hand. The hand baseline still trims before counting (O(tail) on an over-long text); the cost bound is for
the generated code, the baseline is kept as the obvious hand version. Where P25 gains:
- Admission: hand calls `is_ascii` per string; P25 `ascii32` tests 32 bytes per step.
- Validation: hand `trim` re-matches slice patterns per code point then `units_upto` counts per byte; P25 finds the
  trim bounds by index and counts 8 ASCII bytes per step with the cap.
- Build: hand pushes into `Vec::with_capacity` with per-push capacity checks; P25 sizes exactly and writes with
  proven indexes (`get_unchecked`), 8 words per step on ASCII.
- Runtime checks left in the generated card code: none on indexes; the 8-byte loads keep a
  `TryFrom<&[u8]> for [u8; 8]` `unwrap()` on a constant-length slice, which LLVM folds. No further check for the proofs
  to remove was found.

Confirm audit ddb8e411 (Codex gpt-6.2-astra ultra, read-only, on the fixed tree): items 1, 2, 6 and 7 fixed; 3, 4 and
5 partial:
- 3: validity is correct (astral pair across 300, lone surrogate 1 unit, whitespace-only tail accepted, non-whitespace
  after `q` refused), but `"a" * 300 + " " * N + "b"` still reads the N spaces before refusing. Intent: deciding
  that text is over-long needs a non-whitespace byte after unit 300, and a whitespace run may hide one anywhere, so an
  exact trim judgment cannot have a constant bound there. The bound kept is: no byte after the first deciding
  non-whitespace character is read, and a text whose unit 301 is non-whitespace stops at it.
- 4: the hand card was admitted once per round inside the timer, the Pruv chain not at all. Fixed: the hand admission
  moved before the timer; C re-measured (P25.3).
- 5: an empty card still returned early in `hand_diff` on the `-102` kind, so its setCard path was not compared.

## Appendix P24 (row B/bud_halt.pruv + m10_test: synchronous halt and its effects)

The commit with this appendix; base 00aa88e (main, P23); main 22332cd (P19c) merged as cb3d79c and main 06ef5a8
(P13d, T5) merged as 59f6487 before the final gates (neither touches a `bench/l3/budget` file; T5 moves the inline
policy into its own module in both compilers with the rule unchanged). Changed files: `bench/l3/budget/bud_halt.pruv`,
`bench/l3/budget/m10_test/{driver_m10.rs,hand_m10.rs,mutant_halt.py,root_m10.pruv,run_m10.py}`,
`bench/l3/budget/m7_test/bud_facts.rs` (the `running_ids` host fact), `bench/l3/budget/{M10_NOTES.md,ABI.md}`. No
compiler file and no `bud_lifecycle.pruv` change. Raw logs: `work/p24/` (not committed).

### P24.1 Change

- `bud_halt::halt` asks `runningDelegationIds` itself, synchronously, after SETTLE (KD-M10-1 retired: the op no longer
  carries a prefetched answer and the `[30]` marker is gone). Order inside one call:
  1. record frame check (`rec_ok_in`), then `reserve(halt_words)` with `halt_words = blob_n + 8 + QUERY_ROOM`
     (QUERY_ROOM = 256 words); a shortfall returns -N Grow with no effect and no query;
  2. re-read the record offset and re-check its frame (`blob_n` unchanged, `rec_ok_in`), view, clock, `settle_at`
     (may push 13 timerClear);
  3. `running_ids` (trusted Rust host fact in `bud_facts.rs`), answer size `iw`; a malformed answer returns 2 with
     only SETTLE's effects; an answer that does not fit fx (`fx[0] + 8 + 2D`) or the store returns 6;
  4. the second `reserve(n + 8 + iw)` (inside QUERY_ROOM it can only rehash in place; any other result returns 6),
     re-read and re-check the record, then `halted` writes the halted record in place and the effects 31, 32,
     [33, i]..., 34, 35, 36, 20, 37 follow.
- Status 6 (terminal): halt's answer does not fit fx or the store room. fx is valid on every status >= 0.
- Every return after SETTLE goes through `fail_settled`, which first calls `keep_settled`: SETTLE's record change is
  stored even when halt then fails (words 8 activeMs / 16 activeSince kind / 17 since from the view, and, when SETTLE
  ended an active clock (`k0 == 1`, view kind no longer 1), the record is rewritten without the activeSince string, as
  `root_m10::run_op` does). So on 2 / 6 the store and SETTLE's timerClear in fx agree. A failed keep returns 2.
- Store offsets are 40-bit (`c40`): `rec_ok_in` ensures `off <= 2^40`, `halted`/`put_vec`/`copy_in` take offsets up to
  2^40 (`copy_in` falls back to word puts above 2^32). The record copies (`copy_in`, `bud_lifecycle::copy_words`) move
  at most 2^30 words per string, so halt returns 6 before any write when the record has more than 2^30 words (this
  also keeps `halt_words` below 2^32, which `reserve` truncates to), 6 when `n + 8 + iw` exceeds 2^32, and 3 when the
  view has fewer than 7 words.
- `halted(st, base, ...)` reads the old record in place from `st` (`copy_in` block copy for the 24-word head, then
  words 0/8/16/17, `put_key`/`put` from `st`, the id list, the tail via `copy_in`); no intermediate record copy.
  `str_pos` walks the record's strings from `c40(base + 24)` with `bud_lifecycle::str_words`.
- `root_m10`: the op is `[code, now, 0, what x10, flag, sessionId, budgetId, runKey]` (no answer); `run_op` reserves
  halt's room without the id list and checks only the fixed fx part; status 6 is passed through. A run op whose SETTLE
  ended a text activeSince rewrites the record (string 2 dropped) before a nested halt, and reserves that rewrite's
  words with halt's room, so a nested halt that fails after its own SETTLE keeps a consistent record.
- `bud_facts.rs::running_ids`: the host's queue head as `n, (len, words)*`; the query record keeps the answer actually
  returned. The driver logs each query as an `rdi` event at its effect position with that answer, preceded by
  `X armed` when the budget's timer is still armed at query time (a query before SETTLE); q fails on `X armed`.
- `driver_m10.rs` effect 33 resolves each stopped id from the answer (id start positions built in one pass), so the
  perf lane names every stop as the hand lane does (`black_box(id)` when silent).
- `run_m10.py`:
  - q compares the query itself: `runningDelegationIds` must come after SETTLE's timerClear with the ref's sessionId and
    budgetId, and the stops must carry that answer; `halts` counts queries;
  - `build --budlib/--out` (mutant library and its own build directory);
  - `perf` interleaves Pruv and `hand_m10.rs` per round and D, rejects rounds/reps < 1 and fails with `HOLD` for a
    median above 1.0x hand without overlap.
- `driver_m10.rs`: borrows sid/bid (no per-call key clone), silent arm for the perf loop.
- `hand_m10.rs` (new): hand Rust halt and put-back, perf lane only.
- `mutant_halt.py` (new): control, 12 mutants and the G fixtures (G1 answer order with 2 and 0 ids, G2 malformed answer,
  G3 answer too big for fx, G3b too big for the store room, G4 a forced Grow before the query). G2/G3/G3b check the
  exact terminal log (`clear`, `rdi`, `X s`), that the session is not halted and that the record's words
  (0, 8, 16, 17) equal the settled values of the control's halt (the fixture asserts SETTLE changed them). G4 fills the
  arena so the first call returns -N with 0 queries and `st`/fx unchanged; the retry returns 0 with exactly one query.
  `query_before_settle` must build and be killed by q with a reason naming `X armed` or `runningDelegationIds` (not
  only by G, and not by an unrelated failure); a mutant that fails rustc counts as BROKEN.
- The `X armed` check is replayed host-side after the call (effects up to fxn), so it checks the host-visible order of
  the query against SETTLE's timerClear, not Pruv's in-call store write order (the host contract treats fx[1..fxn) as
  performed when it answers).

### P24.4 Hand vs generated

- halt at D = 10 is within noise of hand Rust (the ranges overlap).
- At D = 50/100 Pruv is about 1.6-2x faster:
  - Hand Rust gets the host answer as D owned `String` ids and pushes each into the stopped list and the effects.
  - Pruv writes the answer's packed words once into the flat store and the fx frame.
- Answer preparation differs:
  - The hand lane's per-rep `host.answer = ids.clone()` clones D `String`s. This is the host side of the query, as
    `running_ids` is for Pruv, and it is counted in the hand time.
  - Pruv's host moves a prebuilt word vector out and back.
- putback:
  - Hand Rust clones the open `Budget` struct (its `String` fields) back into the map.
  - Pruv puts the open record back into the flat store without allocating.

## Appendix T5a (M7 lookup and lifecycle gap without code growth)

Result: no change ships. Every product fix found within the package lowers instructions only by adding `__text`
above the T5 base (405,180 B), which row T5a forbids. The generated Rust, the binaries, `__text` and peak RSS stay as
in T5. The remaining gap is split by line below and queued (T5a.5).

### T5a.1 Method

- Instructions per op are `(I(5R) - I(R)) / 4R`, with S = 100, R = 20000, median of 3, from `/usr/bin/time -l`.
  Load average was 4-10, so instructions lead; cycles were read as a cross-check only.
- The Pruv lane is the driver's typed lane (`driver_m7.rs` `perf`), filtered to one item. hand16 is
  `hand_m7_u16 perf 100 R ITEM typed`.
- Variants were built from the shipped M7 output (`work/t5a/m7.base.rs`, identical to the T5 base) by editing the
  generated Rust. `__text` is from `size -m` on the work build (base 406,268 B there; same flags for every variant).

### T5a.2 Cells and harness floor

The raw typed-lane cells are not a like-for-like comparison:
- the hand16 timed loop is a bare method call (`black_box(w.current(..))` for current);
- the Pruv typed loop goes through a `step` closure that rustc does not inline (its own symbol with a 6 register-pair
  prologue), a match on the prep code, `w.fx[0] = 0`, the 2^40 length guards of the `c_*` entries and an `out[0]`
  read.

The Pruv floor was measured with the `c_*` bodies emptied (`m7.emptyall.rs`; `c_replace` is kept, it is not a
target cell). The hand floor was measured only for current (`hand_empty.rs`, current returns `None`). The hand
attach and reopenmiss loops also run `fx.clear()`, and closereopen makes two calls per iteration
(`hand_m7_u16.rs` perf loops), so the hand floor of the other cells is not measured and no floor-subtracted gap is
claimed for them.

| cell | base | hand16 | raw ratio | Pruv floor (bodies empty) | hand floor |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| isHalted | 405 | 339 | 1.19 | 66 | not measured |
| current | 403 | 335 | 1.20 | 73 | ~19 |
| attach | 457 | 319 | 1.43 | 92 | not measured |
| reopenmiss | 456 | 339 | 1.35 | 80 | not measured |
| closereopen (pair) | 1151 | 889 | 1.29 | 128 | not measured |

- For current, floor-subtracted work is about 330 (Pruv) against about 316 (hand): +14, about 1.04x.
- If the current hand floor of about 19 per call held for the pair, closereopen would be about 1023 against 851
  (+172). That is an estimate, not a measurement.
- The step closure alone: with the current body emptied in both, the Pruv floor is 73 with the closure lane and 50
  with an inline loop (`T5A_INL`; the `emptyI` build empties only current). With the shipped body and the inline loop,
  current goes from 407 to 372. Neither changes product code.

### T5a.3 Experiments (product code)

rsplita and mc were measured in the same run as base, so their delta uses that run's base.

| variant | change | same-run base | variant | delta | `__text` B | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---:|---|
| rsplit | reopen slow tail (session_of, blob_copy, rewrite, reserve, store) moved to `#[cold] #[inline(never)] reopen_slow`, reopen stays `#[inline]` | reopenmiss 456, closereopen 1151 (T5a.2 table, not same run) | 461, 1157 | +5, +6 | not measured | worse |
| rsplita | rsplit plus reopen `#[inline(always)]` | reopenmiss 452, closereopen 1146 | 420, 1111 | -32, -35 | 417,212 (+10.9 KB) | not shippable (text rule); not expressible today (T5a.4) |
| mc | maybe_close: `eb` plus one span check, then direct state read and in-place header writes; old path kept as the fallback for buffers outside the premise | closereopen 1149 | 1140 | -9 | 408,508 (+2.2 KB) | gain under 1 %, text grows; not shipped |

- Work build base `__text` is 406,268 B.
- current under rsplita was read as unchanged. current under rsplit, and every cell under mc other than
  closereopen, were not measured.
- `str_pos_in` is still in mc.

Removing the fallback in `mc` would cut text. But for an entry whose record span is not in `st`, maybe_close today
still reads the record through total accessors. A `found_at` style check returns -2 there, and maybe_close would
then answer "not open". That is a behaviour change outside the T5a scope, so it was not taken.

### T5a.4 Line-level reasons for each remaining cell

- **current, isHalted** (current +14 after the floor; isHalted's hand floor not measured):
  - Generated: find_w → `gf(owner, 3)`, `hash_words`, `find_h_w`.
  - Generated: on each tag-matching probe, `entry_matches_w` re-reads `st[5]`/`st[6]` through `field_addr → ea`, with
    clamps.
  - Generated: found_at does one `eb`, one span check, the `id_at` memcmp and the state check.
  - Hand: one SipHash `HashMap::get` and a `Box<[u16]>` compare.
  - Why Pruv cannot emit it: the per-probe re-validation is the total accessor on an unproved buffer. A caller-proved
    base would remove it, which is the P13h call-site specialization. Inlining find_w is ruled out by T5.2
    (+29.7 KB).
- **reopenmiss**:
  - reopen is `#[inline]` and out of line, and its single body holds the slow path (blob_copy Vec, rewrite, store).
  - The miss path therefore pays the slow path's frame: `sub sp, sp, #0x160` (352 B) in this build, with saved
    registers (P18.4 measured 320 B).
  - The split that removes this (rsplita) needs a cold, never-inlined tail. Pruv source has no cold or no-inline
    marker, and the inline policy folds a single-caller fn back into its caller (P18.4), so neither compiler can emit
    it. Even then it costs +10.9 KB of text.
  - The miss share without the frame is not separated.
- **closereopen**:
  - The reopen share is as above.
  - Per pair, find_w runs twice: maybe_close's `session_of`, and reopen's `current_at`. `clock_in` answers -1 on the
    empty clock map without hashing.
  - maybe_close re-validates the entry with total accessors: `entry_addr`, `at_off`/`at_n`, `state_of`,
    `str_pos_in`, and an `ent_u16::wr` per in-place header write. Proving the entry and header part away measured -9
    (mc).
  - Hand also calls `is_quiet` and records `Changed` on both calls, so those are not a Pruv-only cost.
  - The cause of the rest of the pair gap is not determined by these experiments. A per-function attribution is
    queued with T5b.
- **attach**:
  - On an open budget, Pruv copies the stored budget id into `out` (`put_key`, `bud_lifecycle.pruv` attach ref path).
    Hand returns a reference to the stored id (`Res::Ref(&b.id, ..)`).
  - Pruv also re-validates the entry (eb, span check, id length inside the record).
  - The copy follows from the `out` buffer result ABI, not the entry layout. It belongs with P18b's result-path
    question, not P13e.
  - Inlining is ruled out: T5.2's `fa` variant (find_w + attach inlined together) gives -13 % for +40 % text.

### T5a.5 Queued rows

- T5b (new): a cold-tail rule in both codegens, for example an attribute or a proof-free rule on a branch that ends in
  an `! alloc` call chain, chosen so the M4 put path is not marked cold. Target: reopenmiss and closereopen, with
  `__text` not above the T5 base. rsplita is the upper bound it must beat in text.
- T5c (new): M7 typed-lane harness parity in `driver_m7.rs`. The timed loop calls the `c_*` entry the way hand16 calls
  its method (no non-inlined step closure, no prep match per op), and is reported next to the current lane. This is
  measurement only; it moves no product number.
- P13h keeps the find_w probe re-validation. P18b keeps the result path, including the attach id copy into `out` (T5a.4).

### T5a.6 Gates, audit and delegation

- No product file changed: the generated output is identical to T5, so `tests/g8/compatibility.json`, the budget roots
  and the M4 cells are as at T5 and were not re-run.
- `work/t5a/` holds the variants, `mk.py`, `instr.py` and `diag.md`; it is not committed.
- Step 1 went over its 1-hour cap. The package was split as row T5a.5 says, rather than shipping a text-growing
  change.
- Audit (Codex gpt-6.2-astra, ultra, review): it found that the no-ship verdict holds. It made four required findings,
  all fixed above:
  1. The harness floor was stated per cell, but it was measured only for current.
  2. The deltas mixed bases.
  3. The reopen frame is 352 B in this build; closereopen runs find_w twice per pair, and hand also calls is_quiet and
     logs `Changed`.
  4. attach copies the stored id into `out`; it is not a key copy into the record.
- One optional finding is left unmeasured: reopen's slow path could reuse the already validated `off`/`n` instead of a
  second `session_of` and state re-check. It is folded into T5b.

## Appendix T5c (M7 typed-lane harness parity and floors)

Result: with a typed lane shaped like hand16's typed loop, isHalted is below hand16 at S and M (0.98-0.99x
instructions, no overlap). current is 1.02x. attach (1.29-1.30x), closereopen (1.18x) and reopenmiss (1.15-1.16x)
stay above 1.0x. Each remaining gap is split by line below and points to T5b, P13h or P18b; no new row. Measurement
only: no `.pruv` file or compiler changed, the generated Rust is as at T5a (rs and py output byte-identical), and the
existing typed lane is unchanged.

### T5c.1 Lanes and floors

- **Existing typed lane (`t`, `rchk_t`, unchanged):** the `step` closure (not inlined), the `c_direct` match on the prep
  code, `w.fx[0] = 0` per op, the Grow fallback. Its closure's disassembly is identical to the T5a driver on the same
  `gen.rs` (same symbol, same address, md5 of the address-stripped listing equal).
- **Fair typed lane (`f`, `rchk_f`, new, `driver_m7.rs` `fair_loop`):** the match on the item is outside the loop; the
  loop calls `fair_one::<C>` (`#[inline(always)]`, const-generic code), which calls the `c_*` entry directly and then
  `black_box((r, w.out[0]))`, the same observation as the existing lane.
  - fx is reset only where hand16 clears fx: attach, reopen and maybe_close (hand `fx.clear()`); current and
    isHalted reset nothing, as hand16 does not.
  - No Grow fallback: none of the five cells grows a buffer, and `fair_rchk` asserts `r >= 0` for every op.
  - Arguments are the same pre-decoded words as the existing lane (`FArgs` from `Prep`), read through `black_box`,
    as hand16 reads its keys through `black_box`.
  - closereopen runs maybe_close then reopen per rep (2 calls), as hand16 does.
- `driver_m7 perf S reps <item> <t|f>` runs one lane of one item (setup, warm-up 1000, timed loop, `rchk_*` pass);
  `run_m7.py perf` parses `f` / `rchk_f` as lane `pruv_f` and adds the fair columns and their instructions.
- **Floors (`t5c_floor.py`):**
  - Pruv: the shipped `gen.rs` with the five typed `c_*` bodies (current, is_halted, attach, reopen, maybe_close)
    replaced by `out[0]=0; return 0;`, as T5a's `m7.emptyall.rs`. The entry length guards stay. `c_replace` and the
    wire path are kept, so setup is unchanged.
  - hand16: `hand_m7_u16.rs` built with `--cfg t5c_empty`; current, is_halted, attach, reopen and maybe_close return
    at once. The default build is unchanged: its `__text` is 311,484 B before and after, and the otool listing md5 is
    equal. The floor build is 304,380 B.
- Driver `__text` (rs output, this flags set): 405,180 B before, 413,756 B with the fair lane. The growth is the
  harness binary only, but row T5a's text rule reads this binary, so T5b and later rows must re-measure their base on
  this driver (or on the old driver) and compare like with like.

### T5c.2 Method

- Instructions and cycles per call are `(X(5R) - X(R)) / (4R x calls)` from `/usr/bin/time -l`, R = 20,000, with
  calls = 2 for closereopen. Setup, warm-up and the rchk pass (min(R, 2000) ops) are equal in both runs and cancel.
- 5 interleaved rounds: each round runs every (size, cell, lane) once, and the lane order rotates per round. Six
  lanes: Pruv t, Pruv f, hand16, and the three floors (t0, f0, hand0). Sizes S = 100 and M = 500.
- Load was high, so instructions lead; cycles are reported, but their ranges overlap in most cells.
- Ratios use medians: raw = t / hand, fair = f / hand, floor-subtracted = (f - f0) / (hand - hand0).
- Overlap is whether the [min, max] ranges of f and hand intersect over the 5 rounds.
- rchk_f equals rchk and rchk_t for every cell, on the rs-built and the py-built driver.

## Appendix P26 (row Same+m11_test: resident setCard/hasCard)

The commit with this appendix; base 03cda63 (main, P25); main a6fb98e (T5a-T5c, P24 fixes) merged before the
final gates (P26.5). Changed files: `bench/l3/budget/bud_card.pruv` and
`bench/l3/budget/m11_test/{root.pruv,hand.rs,harness.rs,run_m11.py}`. No compiler file, `bud_map`, `bud_lifecycle`,
`bud_halt`, `m7_test` or `m10_test` change. Raw logs: `work/p26/` (not committed).

### P26.1 Change

- The budget stays in its `st` blob `[o, o+n)`; nothing is copied out to decide.
  - `bud_card::budget_pos(v, at, end) -> BudgetPos {ok, id, state, card, card_end}`: one walk of the top-level pairs
    of the object at `v[at]` (last pair wins, as `obj_get`), ASCII key match for `id`, `state`, `card`; `ok` iff tag 9,
    every value well formed (`v_end_d` from depth 3: a field value of the stored budget sits at depth 3 of the
    `{ok, budget}` result) and the walk ends exactly at `end`.
  - `bud_card::v_stored_end(v, at)` (`v_end_u` from depth 2, with the unit range 0..65535 of every string and key):
    `m11_load` refuses (status 2) a blob unless it is exactly one such V, so a stored budget is always a valid V that
    still fits the 32-level limit inside the setCard result (audit fixes, P26.8).
  - `root::cur(st, rf, sid) -> Cur {e, o, n, state, card, card_end}`: session entry, blob offset/length, `budget_pos`
    bounded by `o + n`, and `str_eq` of the budget id with `ref_budget_id(rf)` (last `budgetId` pair wins). `e = -1`
    when there is no current budget (no session, empty blob, id mismatch, malformed blob).
  - `bud_card::judge(found, closed, card, at, lang) -> Judged {kind, used_now, f, error}` is `set_card` without the
    build; `set_card` = `judge` + `build` (kept for perf items A/C).
  - `put_card_words(inout o, p0, ...)` is `pub` with a start position (`requires 0 <= p0 <= 2^40`): the setCard path
    writes the card straight into `out` at the budget's place. `build` keeps a private `p0 = 0` copy
    (`put_card_words0`): with the `p0` form alone, A/C were 2-6 % slower on median than base (61 rounds; the
    constant start lets the writer positions fold). Same words for `p0 = 0`; the generated `build`, `m11_perf_card` and
    `put_card_words0` are now the base code token for token.
- `m11_set_card`: `judge`; on error the old error result. On success: one dry size pass for the card (`cs`);
  `nbn = n + 5 + cs` (append `"card"`) or `n - (card_end - card) + cs` (replace); `need2 = 18 + nbn`; out too small
  -> 3; `nbn > 2^32` -> 2; `words = 0` if `blob_fits`, `make_room(st, 0, words)` -> Grow 1 with `st` unchanged; a
  moved blob after `make_room` -> 2 (unreachable, `make_room` rehashes the index only). Then the 18-word header,
  `st[o..card)`, the card words in place, `st[card_end..o+n)` (append: all of the budget, count + 1 at `out[19]`,
  key `"card"`, the card), and `set_blob(st, e, out, 18, nbn)`. The returned budget and the stored budget are the
  same words (identity by construction).
- `m11_query` drops `! alloc`: op 1 (`current`) copies `st[o..o+n)` once; op 2 (`isHalted`) `is_halted` (literal-free
  6-unit test); op 3 (`hasCard`) `card >= 0 && truthy(st, card)`.
- `hand.rs`: the error path (P25.8 queued row): `card_error(kind, en)` with the Korean and English texts,
  `emit_card_error`; `Store::current_budget`, `current` (`bool`), `has_card` (`Option<bool>`), both validating `rf`
  and `sid`; a strict `v_end` (depth limit, counts checked); `iso` with the signed 6-digit year outside 0..=9999. `harness.rs`: perf items R/H/I (P26.3) and
  `hand_diff` compares the full error words. `run_m11.py`: a `dump` follows every `set` (strict framing,
  `parse_dump`), and `judge` checks after every successful setCard, halted or not, that the returned budget words
  equal the dumped blob of that session (identity oracle).
- Types: `[u8]` card packets, `i64` V words in `st`/`out`, structs for positions; no flat record arrays.

### P26.2 Cost bound per path (B = budget words, V + U = card packet, K = top-level budget pairs)

| path | P25 | P26 bound |
|---|---|---|
| setCard ok | H + 4 walks + O(V+U) + 4 O(B) copies, 4 allocations | H + 1 walk O(K) + O(V+U) + 2 O(card) + 2 O(B) copies (st->out, out->st), 1 allocation (iso) |
| setCard missing/closed | H + O(B) copy + 2 walks + allocation | H + 1 walk, no copy, the error text only |
| setCard field error | as ok up to the failing field | H + 1 walk + the validation prefix (short-circuit) |
| setCard Grow / out small | after O(B) work | before any `st` write; `st` unchanged |
| hasCard | H + O(B) copy + 2 walks + allocation | H + 1 walk + O(1) truthiness, no allocation |
| current | H + O(B) copy + walk + allocation + copy | H + 1 walk + 1 O(B) copy, no allocation |
| isHalted | H + O(B) copy + 2 walks | H + 1 walk, no allocation |

The walk is O(K + sizes of nested containers) (`v_end` of a string is O(1)). Confirmed by perf (P26.3): B/R/I fall
to 0.57-0.61 of base and H to 0.36; allocations per call (P26.4) B/R 4 -> 1, H 2 -> 0, I 6 -> 1, all flat in n.

on one in-memory budget, R = setCard alternating a full card with `state` and a minimal card (optional replacement),

### P26.6 Mutants (`work/p26/mut.py`, hdiff + oracle over Q6 + K + qx)

Control: exact 295, prefix-ok 87; hdiff 0 of 10,711. 14 of 18 caught (hdiff, the oracle or both; an oracle crash on malformed words
counts as caught). Rerun after the audit fixes (per-setCard identity oracle): the same 14 of 18, the same 4 not
caught:

| # | mutant | class |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `budget_pos`: first `card` pair wins | equivalent in domain: stored budgets come from JSON (`m11_load`) or setCard, both with unique keys |
| 4 | `budget_pos`: tail not checked (`pos > end`) | equivalent in domain: the blob is always exactly one V (`m11_load` checks `v_stored_end`, setCard writes one V) |
| 14 | `ref`: first `budgetId` wins | unreachable: the driver builds `ref` as a JS object before it is encoded, so a repeated key is collapsed (last wins) before Pruv sees it; the two qx refs with a repeated key (`other` then the id, and the reverse) give the same words to both forms |
| 18 | `judge`: missing reported as kind 1 | equivalent: the root reads `kind` only by sign (`kind >= 0` = error) and takes the text from `error`, which stays `card_error(0, lang)`; `used_now` is false in both |

Before `qx.py` the `isHalted` and `hasCard` mutants were missed (Q6 has no query on a closed budget or a falsy card);
`qx.py` closes both.

### P26.7 Classification

| behaviour | class | how it is kept |
|---|---|---|
| setCard returns the same budget object it stores | intent (TS identity) | by construction (one set of words); the oracle compares every returned budget with the dumped blob |
| an optional field absent from the new card is not kept from the old card | intent (TS replaces `budget.card`) | the card V is replaced whole; Q6 + perf R |
| hasCard = `Boolean(card)` | intent | `truthy` on the resident words; qx 12 card kinds |
| a malformed resident blob reads as "no current" (missing) instead of status 2 at put_card | accident, unreachable | `m11_load` checks `v_stored_end`, setCard writes one V; recorded here, not observable by Q |
| a budget at depth 32 (or with a unit outside 0..65535) is refused at load (status 2) | intent (ABI V limits) | the setCard result `{ok, budget}` adds one level; `v_stored_end` counts from depth 2; `audfix.py` |
| a repeated `budgetId` in `ref`: last pair wins | intent (JS object semantics) | `ref_budget_id`; not producible by the driver (mutant 14) |

### P26.8 Audit

Package audit (Codex gpt-6.2-astra ultra): 5 required, 1 optional; all fixed.

| # | finding | fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the identity oracle compared only the last setCard of a session with the final dump | `run_m11.py`: a `dump` after every `set`; every successful setCard (halted or not) is compared word for word with the dumped blob |
| 2 | `budget_pos` / `v_end` did not check the unit range and restarted the depth at the fields | `v_stored_end` at `m11_load` (units 0..65535, depth from 2); `budget_pos` walks field values from depth 3 |
| 3 | a depth-32 budget became depth 33 inside the `{ok, budget}` result | the same load check counts from depth 2 (ABI limit 32); a depth-32 budget is refused, depth 31 loads (`audfix.py`) |
| 4 | `hand.rs` queries did not validate `ref`; negative counts passed its `v_end` | strict hand `v_end` (depth, counts); `current` -> `bool`, `has_card` -> `Option<bool>`, both validate `ref` and `sid` |
| 5 | hand `iso` lacked the signed 6-digit year | fixed (`-000001`, `+010000`) |
| 6 (optional) | loose dump framing | `parse_dump` (strict counts, lengths, tail) |

Confirm audit (same model): 1-5 confirmed fixed, H/I perf calls measure the same work. One required regression: a
halted replay no longer checked its final dump (`err 2` there classed `prefix-ok`); and (optional) a dump key unit
out of range raised `struct.error` past the `ValueError` handler. Fixed: every dump after a `set` and the final dump
must parse (only the final comparison is skipped on halt), and `parse_dump` refuses key units outside 0..65535.
Rechecked: `judge` on a halted case with `err 2` -> `prefix-fail`; `parse_dump([1, 1, 65536, 0])` -> `ValueError`;
Q6 213/87, K 10/10, qx 72/72 on rs and py.

- P26a: peak RSS above hand by fixed shares only: A +2 pages (code layout of the larger m11 binary, A code = base)
  and H +3 pages (harness `World` buffers vs the hand lane's untouched capacity). Proportional share: none.
- P25.8 JB `ref`/result row stays queued (outside this row).

## Appendix P18b (M7 entry/result path: length guards, out store, id copy, peak RSS)

Base: main a6fb98e (T5c). Lane: the T5c fair typed lane (`driver_m7 perf S R item f`) against hand16 typed, S = 100,
M = 500 sessions. Per call = (X(5R) - X(R)) / (4R calls), X from `/usr/bin/time -l`, R = 20000, 7 interleaved rounds
with the lane order rotated per round; medians, [min..max] over rounds. Instructions are the primary metric. Every
run's rchk value is equal across base, P18b and hand.

### P18b.1 Isolating measurement (instructions per call, S = 500)

Variants of the T5c `gen.rs` / driver, built from one compiler output (measurement only, not shipped):
- `ng`: the 2^40 length-guard `if` removed from the five typed `c_*` entries.
- `lo`: the driver passes a local `[i64; 64]` as `out` and observes `lo[0]`. It stands in for a register result,
  because every body here is inlined and LLVM may keep `out[0]` in a register.
- `noid`: attach's ref-path `put_key` (the stored budget id copied into `out`) replaced by a 2-word view.
- `*0`: the five typed bodies emptied (floors).

| item | base | ng | noid | proven prototype | hand | base0 | proven prototype0 | hand0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| current | 341.0 | 334.2 | 341.1 | 336.6 | 334.0 | 11.2 | 7.1 | 7.0 |
| attach | 391.1 | 379.1 | 355.1 | 377.9 | 303.3 | 15.0 | 8.0 | 5.0 |

`lo` was measured in a separate interleaved run with `ng` beside it, on current at S = 500: `ng` 334.3, `nglo` 327.2,
and base 341.0 against `lo` 332.1.

Shares per call:
- Length guard: -6.8 on current and -12.0 on attach (`ng`); in the floors, 11-15 -> 6-8.
- `out` store + reload: -7..-9 on current (`lo`).
- attach's id copy: -36 (`noid`).
- The proven prototype (twins hand-added to the T5c output) matches the shipped `--proven-entries` result in P18b.3.

### P18b.2 The three causes

1. **2^40 guards, fixed by proof.** New opt-in `--proven-entries` (Rust backend, both compilers, SPEC.md "Length
   bound at host boundaries"). The generated file adds two types, `PruvArr<T>` (`#[repr(transparent)]` over `[T]`)
   and `PruvStr`. Each has a private field in a private module, and its only constructors (`new`, `new_mut`) run the
   T0 check with T0's message. `get` / `get_mut` pass the bound to LLVM through `assert_unchecked`.
   - `pruv_proven::f` is a twin of each checked entry `f`. It takes these types, rebinds them to slices, then runs
     the same representation checks, `requires` and body.
   - The checked entries are byte-identical with and without the flag. Without the flag the whole output is
     unchanged: root_m4 and m7 root are identical to the a6fb98e compiler's output.
   - Safe host code cannot build an unchecked `PruvArr`. `tests/l3/abi/check_proven_entries.py` asserts this through
     E0616 on `include!` at crate root, and also checks the 2^40 and 2^40+1 boundary and the `requires` panic. So
     T0's guarantee holds for untrusted callers: they pay the check once when they wrap the resident state, not on
     every call.
   - `raw_entries = "crate"` is not used.
   - `driver_m7.rs`'s fair lane now wraps `st`/`out`/`bv`/`fx` once (`FBuf`) and the keys once (`FArgs`).
   - `run_m7.py` compiles with `--proven-entries`. The step lane, `q`, and the checked entries are unchanged.
2. **`out` store + reload: no fix in this row; it needs a new ABI → P18c.**
   - Hand: `World::current` is out of line and returns `Option<&Budget>` in x0, which costs 1 `str` (black_box).
   - Pruv: `current` inlines into the loop, and the hit tail writes the host's `out`
     (`stp x9,x14,[x27]; str x15,[x27,#0x10]` = `[4, n, off]`). The host then reloads `out[0]` (`ldr x9,[x27]`).
   - That is 2 stores + 1 load against hand's 1 store, about +3 per call. The empty-body floors show it too: the
     emptied body still writes `out[0] = 0`, which accounts for the +1.4..+3.1 left in pv0 - hand0 on
     attach/closereopen/reopenmiss.
   - `out` is `&mut [i64]` owned by the host, so the stores are visible to the host and LLVM must keep them. Pruv
     cannot emit a register result under the current entry ABI: every array result goes through a host buffer.
   - Fix: an entry form that returns a small fixed-shape result by value (registers). That is a language/ABI change,
     so it is opened as P18c, not done here.
3. **attach's id copy: needs `bud_lifecycle.pruv`, so it is not done here (P13e owns that file).**
   - `put_key` copies the stored budget id into `out`. Hand returns `Res::Ref` (a pointer into the store).
   - `noid` measures -36 per call. A layout that returns a view (`[il, off+25]`, as `noid` does) is a `.pruv` change in
     the entry layout P13e owns. It is reported to P13e.

### P18b.4 Peak RSS attribution (P18b vs hand16, both drivers keep two worlds alive)

- The linear fit gives about 0.74 KB per session proportional plus about 254 KB fixed.
- The proportional share is the store headroom. `bud_store::need` keeps `N >= 2 * len` with power-of-two growth, so
  `st` is up to 4x its live words. That is `bud_store.pruv` (P13e), not a compiler or host share.

    find_w probe → P13h.

  - entry +2.1 / +1.8 → P18c;
  - body +75 / +76: the reopen cold tail → T5b; maybe_close header re-validation and find_w twice per pair → P13h.
- **reopenmiss (1.15):**
  - entry +1.4 / +1.8 → P18c;
  - body +49 / +47: the reopen slow-tail frame → T5b; re-validation → P13h.

New row P18c: a by-value small-result entry (fixed-shape result returned in registers instead of through a host
`&mut [i64]`), in both compilers, with the `--proven-entries` twins as the host surface.

Audit (Codex gpt-6.2-astra ultra), required findings:

   edition (E0433). Fixed: both compilers emit `::std::hint::assert_unchecked`; the proven-entries test now builds
   its default-flags host without `--edition`.

   default Rust compiler is now this checkout's `pruvc-rs/target/release/pruvc`.
3. A crate-root `include!` reaches the private, safe, unchecked `f__pruv_body` functions directly. This predates
   P18b (a6fb98e) and P18b does not widen it; fixing it moves every body into a private child module, which changes
   every generated file. Not fixed here: SPEC now states the guarantee covers `#[path] mod` hosts, and the fix is
   left for a new row.

the clash is on the generated Rust name (a private or specialized `PruvArr` is mangled and does not clash), now
stated in SPEC.
Not taken: moving the `FBuf` checks out of the timed region (one check per timed call, not per iteration).

## Appendix T5b: cold-tail rule, state at the step cap

Base: main `f0c5932` (after P18b), worktree `pruvc-rs` release build, M7 driver built by
`run_m7.py` flags (`-C opt-level=3 --edition 2021`). Driver `__text` 413,244 B, the P18b base.
The variants were hand edits of the generated `gen.rs` only (no source and no compiler change):
reopen is cut at `let se = session_of(..)` into a fast part that ends in a tail call and a tail
function `reopen__pruv_tail(st, sk, ss, sn, fx, out)`.

### T5b.1 Variants and numbers

Fair lane (`driver_m7 perf 500 R item f`, hand16 `typed`), instructions per call from
`(X(5R)-X(R))/(4R*calls)`, R=20000, 3 interleaved rounds, median [min..max]. Peak RSS is the
median `peak memory footprint`. Machine load was high; cycles are listed but not used.

| variant | fast part | tail | `__text` (B) | reopenmiss instr | closereopen instr | peak (B) |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base (P18b) | `#[inline]` | (whole fn) | 413,244 | 386.8 [368.8..388.9] | 521.6 [521.2..528.4] | 3,817,808-3,834,192 |
| cold | `#[inline]` | `#[cold] #[inline(never)]` | 418,876 | 390.0 [377.3..393.0] | 525.2 [523.7..525.8] | 3,834,192 |
| never | `#[inline]` | `#[inline(never)]` | 418,876 | 391.3 [372.4..395.3] | 525.7 [525.6..525.7] | 3,834,192-3,883,344 |
| coldA | `#[inline(always)]` | `#[cold] #[inline(never)]` | 426,940 | 352.8 [332.4..359.2] | 497.7 [496.2..498.3] | 3,817,808-3,834,192 |
| hand16 | | | (own binary) | 334.0 [322.1..334.6] | 445.9 [442.7..458.3] | 3,195,216 |

`rchk` is equal for every variant (reopenmiss 7239146844012164864, closereopen
16571789882858190432). cold and never overlap base on reopenmiss and are 3-4 instructions worse
on closereopen; only coldA separates from base (-34 / -24), and it is still 1.06x / 1.12x hand16.

### T5b.2 Why the tail split alone does not help (line level)

The miss path of base `reopen` is: frame `sub sp, sp, #0x160`, six `stp` of x19-x30, the
length/`out` guards, five `mov` to keep `ss, sn, bk, bs, bn` in callee-saved registers, two
spills (`str x6`, `stp x1, x0`), `bl find_w`, then the miss exit and six `ldp`. In the cold
variant the fast part is 948 B and its frame drops to `#0x90`, but it still saves all six pairs
and spills argument words to the stack (`stp x10, x6`, `str x7` and three stack-argument copies): the nine arguments (`st`, `sk`, `ss`, `sn`, `bk`, `bs`, `bn`,
`fx`, `out`, as slices 14 words) stay live across `bl find_w` because the hit path needs them for
the tail call. The cost on the miss path is the register-save set, and it is set by what is live
across the lookup call, not by the size of the slow tail. A smaller frame changes one `sub`
immediate. hand16 does not pay it because its `reopen` is inlined into the timed loop, where the
values are already in registers.

So the only measured win (coldA) is the fast part inlined into its callers. The `reopen` call
sites in the driver binary are the wire dispatch and every driver function that inlines
`c_reopen` (`fair_loop`, `raw_call`, `c_call`, `one`, `run_perf` and two of its closures,
`World::call`): +628 to +1,476 B each.

### T5b.3 `__text` is partly a CGU artifact

With identical call graphs (same `bl` targets per function, checked from `otool -tvV`), the cold
variant's `put_at` grows 5,468 to 11,668 B (`memcpy` calls 4 to 8) and `find_w` 1,020 to 2,024 B
(`memcmp` 1 to 2): LLVM duplicated code inside them. Built with `-C codegen-units=1` (diagnosis
only, not the bench flags): base 413,884, cold 411,964 (-1,920), coldA 420,732 (+6,848). So
under the default 16 CGUs a gen change that removes code can still grow `__text` by about 6 KB
from partitioning. The `__text` gate stays on the bench flags; this is reported so a later row
does not read the +5.6 KB of cold as the rule's own cost.

Decision (main, 2026-11-19): the `__text` gate keeps reading the bench-flag build, because that is the
binary that ships and pays the code pages. A row whose `__text` grows also reports the
`-C codegen-units=1` number next to it; growth that disappears at one CGU is written as partition
noise in that row, but it still counts against the gate (no exemption). Whether the bench profile
itself should move to one CGU for both hand and generated code is measured in row T5d.

### T5b.4 Split

- T5b1 (measurement, this appendix): done. No compiler change ships; the cold attribute alone
  does not meet the row (no instruction gain, `__text` +5.6 KB under bench flags).
- T5b2 (row T5b2, open): cut the miss path's live set across `find_w` instead of the tail. Either
  the reopen fast part takes the session record as one view (P18b result path / P13h
  specialization), or the cold-tail rule is paired with a `__text` cut of at least 13.7 KB
  (bench flags) elsewhere so the coldA inline fits the P18b base. Still to do there: the
  five-cell S/M re-baseline table, the closereopen per-function attribution, M4 cells, gates,
  and the audit.

### T5b2.2 The fix attempt (variant A, not shipped)

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| base afe3732 | 464,700 | 377.4 / 392.3 / 391.1 | 533.8 / 548.4 / 549.3 |

reopenmiss drops 19 at M and L and stays 1.11x; closereopen does not move (its reopen hits, so it pays the
change path either way). The inlined `reopen_b` still saves six callee-saved pairs, still
stores hoisted invariants before the probe loop and still spills about 11 registers around the key `memcmp`.
`__text` grows by 10 KB, so variant A fails the `__text` gate as well as the 1.0x gate; it is reverted (no source
or compiler change ships from this row) and the cgu1 number was not taken for a build that does not ship.

### T5b2.3 Per-function attribution (lldb single step, one call or pair at M)

Method: `lldb` breakpoint on the entry function after 50 warm calls (`perf 500 200 <item> f` for Pruv, `typed` for
hand16), then `StepInstruction` until the same entry is hit again; every retired instruction is attributed to the
symbol that holds its pc. The counts match the counter medians (Pruv pair 1,097 vs 548.4 x 2; hand pair 890 vs
445.0 x 2; Pruv reopenmiss 392; hand 336). Traces: `work/t5b2/attr/` (not committed).

closereopen pair (close half = from `maybe_close` entry to its return; reopen half = the rest of the iteration):

| part | Pruv | hand16 | Pruv - hand |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| maybe_close own code (Pruv: includes its inlined hash) | 465 | 214 + 168 SipHash = 382 | +83 |
| maybe_close host facts (`bud_facts::calls`, `is_quiet`, `answer`, TLS) | 133 | 98 | +35 |
| maybe_close `memcmp` | 14 | 33 | -19 |
| reopen (hit) own code (Pruv: includes its inlined hash) | 377 | 117 + 168 SipHash = 285 | +92 |
| reopen `memcmp` (key and 9-word id) | 67 | 86 | -19 |
| loop / harness (`fair_loop` by-value copy vs hand closure) | 40 | 5 | +35 |
| pair total | 1,096 | 889 | +207 |

The host-facts row is the same harness function (`bud_facts::is_quiet`) on both sides; hand's build inlines
`answer` into `maybe_close`, the Pruv build calls it through `LocalKey::with` (harness inlining, not generated
code). The loop row is mostly in the floors (`pruv_f0` 5.1 vs `hand0` 4.6 per call at M); the floor-subtracted
ratio stays 1.23.

reopenmiss at M, Pruv 392 = own code 305 + `memcmp` 67 + `fair_loop` 20; hand16 336 = closure 76 + loop 5 +
SipHash 168 + `memcmp` 86. The Pruv own code by source line:

| Pruv source part | instr | of which stack loads/stores | `bic`/`csel` clamps |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| frame prologue (six callee-saved pairs, `sub sp, #0x1f0`) | 8 | 6 | 0 |
| `fx_ok(fx)`, `len(out)` guards | 15 | 3 | 2 |
| `og = gf(st, owner, 3)` | 17 | 0 | 2 |
| `hash_words` (2 words) | 34 | 0 | 2 |
| `find_h_w` setup and invariants hoisted out of the probe loop | 51 | 11 | 6 |
| probe loop (2 probes) | 27 | 0 | 0 |
| `entry_matches_w` field tests (kind, owner, owner gen, hash, length) | 47 | 6 | 3 |
| key compare call: argument moves and spills around `bl memcmp` | 24 | 18 | 0 |
| `id_at` record tests and the 9-word id compare call | 71 | 15 | 1 |
| miss exit and epilogue | 11 | 6 | 0 |
| total | 305 | 65 | 16 |

So hand16's own code is 81 instructions plus a 168-instruction library hash; Pruv's hash is 34, but its own code
around it is 271. Line-level cause of the +56 (M) gap:

1. Register pressure: `reopen_b`'s nine arguments (14 words as slices) plus the hoisted invariants stay live
   across the two `memcmp` calls, so the miss path pays 65 stack loads/stores (six callee-saved pairs, 11
   hoisted-invariant stores, 18 and 15 spill/reload words around the two calls). hand16's `reopen` is inlined into
   its loop with `sessions.get_mut(sid)` live state in registers. Variant A (inline the fast part) removed only 19
   of these.
2. Record checks on the flat `[i64]` store: `c32` clamps of stored counts (16 `bic`/`csel`), the owner generation
   read, `entry_matches_w`'s five field tests and `id_at`'s range tests (together about 100 instructions with the
   guards). hand16's `HashMap<Box<[u16]>, Session>` has typed fields and does none of them.

### T5b2.4 Gates and what did not change

No source or compiler change ships, so codegen parity, the test groups, M4 cells, `__text` (464,700 B) and peak
RSS are those of `afe3732` (M4 not re-measured: no file it builds from changed). reopenmiss and closereopen stay
1.17x / 1.23x hand16 at M and L in instructions (0.85-0.89x in cycles) and move to debt D14.

Proposed next row (for main to open): the session store as typed records (struct or `[u8]` entries with typed
count fields) for the reopen / maybe_close lookup, which removes the `c32` clamps and the field tests by
representation, per the §7.5 data representation rule; and either the inline policy taking `reopen_b` with a
`__text` cut elsewhere or a language form that passes the session record as one view so fewer values are live
across the compare calls.

### P13e.2 Split: fixed and proportional share of the excess

Fixed share = the excess at n = 1 (code pages, the 4096-word start buffer): +64 (tools, clocks) to +96 (sessions)
KiB; this is the P13d/P13h term. Proportional share = excess(n) - excess(1):

| axis | n=100 | n=500 | n=1000 | n=2000 | slope Pruv / hand (KiB per entry, n 100..2000) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| sessions | -32 | -48 | -64 | -80 | 0.296 / 0.319 |
| tools | +32 | +48 | +96 | +176 | 0.328 / 0.253 |
| clocks | +16 | -160 | -320 | -608 | 0.227 / 0.555 |

Only tools has a proportional share above hand. Per activity Pruv touches one 20-word entry (160 B), two i64 slots
(16 B) and one packed key word (8 B), 184 B; hand's `HashSet<Box<[u16]>>` is a 16 B bucket plus a control byte at
load 7/8 or less and a 16 B key block, about 56 B at n = 1000 (2048 buckets) and 115 B per added activity between
1000 and 2000 (a doubling to 4096). Sessions and clocks are below hand proportionally (hand's per-entry `Vec` /
nested `HashMap`), so their excess is the fixed share alone.

### P13e.3 Why the layout step stopped

The entry fields 11..17 (child count, blob offset and length, v0..v3) and the bound `16 <= a && a + 20 <= len(st)`
are a word ABI outside this row's files:

- `bud_clock.pruv`: `st[ca + 11..17]`, `st[ra + 14]`, `requires 16 <= ca && ca + 20 <= len(st)` (P22 proven indexing).
- `bud_lifecycle.pruv`: `st[a + 12]`, `st[a + 13]`, `found_at` ensures `result + 20 <= len(st)`.
- `m9_test/root_m9.pruv` (fields 12, 13, 14, 17) and `m8_test/root_m8.pruv` (12, 13) through `field_addr`.

Inside the row's files the most that can shrink is fields 0..10, 18, 19 (bits: state 1, owner/prev/next/head/tail
32 each, key off 40, key len 31, key cap 28, blob cap 40, plus three full words gen, owner gen, hash), packed in
front of the seven fixed words with `eb` returning a virtual base: 15 words per entry. Tools then touches about
144 B per activity, still above hand's 56-115 B (n = 1000: about +55 KiB proportional left). Reaching hand needs a
per-kind layout: a small base entry for map members (state, owner, generations, hash, links, key; about 6-7 words,
short keys inline) and an extension record only for entries with children, blobs or scalars, reached through
accessors. That changes `bud_clock.pruv`, `bud_lifecycle.pruv`, `m9_test/root_m9.pruv` and `m8_test/root_m8.pruv`,
which the package brief forbids; decision requested from the main session:

1. allow those four files (accessor-based fields; proofs re-done there), then the per-kind layout; or
2. ship the in-boundary 15-word layout now (tools proportional share shrinks but stays above hand), and queue the
   per-kind layout as a new row.

Generation width stays 64 bits in both options: a 32-bit generation makes a stale child match its reused owner after
2^32 reuses of one entry, which the tools churn (one turn forgotten per rep) reaches in hours.

Decision (main session): option 1, with `bud_clock.pruv`, `bud_lifecycle.pruv`, `m9_test/root_m9.pruv`,
`m8_test/root_m8.pruv` and the layout constants in `m34_test/run.py` added to the boundary; generation stays 64-bit.

### P13e.4 Step 2a: accessors (2d877e8)

Fixed offsets 11..17 and the `a + 20 <= len(st)` bounds outside `bud_store` go through `xa` / `xb` / `xbm` /
`field_at`; the layout is unchanged and every gate output is identical to c3ec58d.

### P13e.5 Step 2b: layout (b231319)

The buffer keeps 20 cap words of entry space, split in two arrays:

- Base, 10 words at `E + 10e`: 0 state, 1 owner, 2 owner gen, 3 gen, 4 key offset, 5 key length, 6 hash, 7 prev,
  8 next, 9 `xk = 2 * key cap + flag` (flag = extension present).
- Extension, 10 words at `E + 10 cap + 10e`: 0 child count, 1 blob offset, 2 blob length, 3..6 v0..v3, 7 child head,
  8 child tail, 9 blob cap. Written only when an entry gets children, a blob or a nonzero value (`xbm` sets the
  flag and the defaults). Without it reads give head/tail -1 and 0 otherwise.

Pure map members (all tools activities) touch 10 words plus slot and key; the extension half of their entries is never
written, and buffers of 64 KiB and up are host-mapped (P13c), so those pages stay non-resident. Admission
(`ent_i1` / `ent_w` / `entry_ok`) checks the base, and the extension only when the flag is set; no new
`admit` / `assume` / `opaque`. Deviation from the brief's 6-7 word base: generation, owner generation and hash stay
full words and the base is not bit-packed, because packing added decode instructions on every lookup (the
instructions and time come first). `copy_node` / `set_blob` write the extension directly (`set_vals`, `wr16`) instead
of the generic field path; without that sessions and clocks lost about 1M instructions (+4 %) at n = 2000 (grow
copies).

Layout-forced changes outside the row files: `m8_test/driver_m8.rs` (import fixture offsets),
`m8_test/corrupt_resident.py` (field addresses; `--old-rev HEAD` passes, the default `c4d3a63^` fails as before for a
pre-existing format reason), `m34_test/CONTRACT.md` (layout text), and after the audit `m9_test/mut_m9.py` (P13e.10).

## Appendix P18c: by-value result forms

### P18c.1 Surface (SPEC "By-value results")

With `--proven-entries`, every `pruv_proven` twin whose last parameter is the `inout` `[i64]` result buffer also
gets `pruv_proven::val::<name>::<const PRUV__K: usize>(other twin parameters) -> (RT, [i64; PRUV__K])`. The body
makes a fresh `[0i64; PRUV__K]`, calls the twin with `PruvArr::new_mut(&mut buf)` and returns `(status, buf)`, so it
means exactly the twin called on a new zeroed buffer of length K; the twin's own `requires` (for example
`len(out) >= 2`) still apply in checked builds, and under `--trust-callers` the host must meet them for the zeroed
buffer. `K > 2^40` is a `const` assertion (a compile error E0080, `pruv: by-value result longer than 2^40`). No form
is emitted for another element type, for a non-`inout` result or when the buffer is not last. The form is
`#[inline(always)]` and generic: an unused form emits no code, and `val` is a module, so an entry named `val` does not
clash. The const generic is named `PRUV__K` because `__` names are reserved in Pruv (`vparser.py`), so no Pruv
parameter can shadow it (the first cut named it `K`, and a parameter named `K` broke the generated Rust; audit
finding, P18c.6). SPEC fixes the meaning only; where the result words live after optimization is rustc's choice, so a
host picks `val` or the `out` twin per call site by measurement (P18c.2).

Both compilers emit the same text (M7 root, `--proven-entries`: 117 added lines, Python = Rust byte for byte).
Without the flag the output is byte-identical to the base (M7 root, m34 root_m4, m11 root checked against the
base compiler); the guarded `c_*` entries and the P18b twins are unchanged.

Tests (`tests/l3/abi/check_proven_entries.py`): host calls `val::pair::<2>` = `(7, [5, 6])`,
`val::copy_first::<3>` = `(42, [42, 0, 0])`, `val::named_k::<2>(9)` = `(9, [9, 0])` (a Pruv parameter named `K`),
`val::only_out::<1>()` = `(4, [3])` (the result buffer is the only parameter), `val::pair::<1>` panics with
`requires violated`; must-reject: `K = 2^40 + 1` (E0080 with our const message), a result buffer that is not last,
and a `[u8]` result (no `val` form, E0603).

### P18c.2 Prototype: where the by-value form wins

Isolating measurement before the compiler change: a `val` module added by script to the shipped M7 gen and the fair
lane switched cell by cell (lanes `f` = P18b fair lane, `v` = by-value; per call = (X(5R) - X(R)) / (4R x calls),
R = 20000, `/usr/bin/time -l`, interleaved rounds; instructions per call, medians).

| cell | f | v | hand16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| current S / M | 336.7 / 335.3 | 325.7 / 323.8 | 332.9 / 333.9 |
| isHalted S / M | 328.0 / 329.8 | 325.1 / 324.7 | 340.0 / 340.4 |
| attach S / M (K = 11) | 380.6 / 378.3 | 380.6 / 381.5 | |
| closereopen S / M | 521.4 / 520.1 | 523.8 / 524.2 | |
| reopenmiss S / M | 385.7 / 386.2 | 385.7 / 387.2 | |

- current and isHalted: the twin body inlines into the caller, the `[i64; K]` lives in registers and the `out`
  store + reload (P18b.2 item 2) is gone: -11 instructions per call.
- attach, reopen and maybeClose: their bodies (`bud_lifecycle` attach/reopen/maybe_close) are calls, not inlined.
  The by-value form then adds per call a zero store of the stack array, the length constant and the array's stack
  address (from `otool -tvV`), and the result is still stored and reloaded through memory: +0 to +4. The zeroing
  cannot be dropped: the body may read `out`, and a `&mut [i64]` over uninitialized memory is undefined behaviour.
  attach also needs K >= 11 to keep the same per-op checksum; K = 4 changes `rchk_f`.

Decision: the M7 fair lane uses `val` for current (K = 3, `[4, n, off]` on a hit) and isHalted (K = 1) only;
attach, reopen and maybeClose keep the `out` twins (`fair_out`, the P18b shape), so no cell gives back a P18b gain.
