### P18c.4 Not met here: the `out` write of call-shaped bodies

The by-value result only stays in registers when the twin body inlines into the caller. attach, reopen and
maybeClose call non-inlined `bud_lifecycle` functions that take the result buffer as `&mut [i64]` (pointer and
length) and write through it. A by-value form at the entry cannot remove that store; it only moves the buffer to
the host's stack and adds the zeroing. Removing it needs the result to travel by value through the call chain: the
callee returns its result words (a small tuple or `[i64; K]` in registers, Rust's aggregate return) instead of
writing a caller buffer, which is a codegen change for every function that writes an `inout` result, plus a proof
of the shape (K fixed per function, all words written on every path). Proposed new row (for main to open):

- P18d, both codegens: by-value results through non-inlined calls. An internal function whose `inout [i64]`
  result has a statically fixed written prefix returns it by value; attach / closereopen / reopenmiss floors
  without the `out` write, those cells not above P18b, `__text` and peak RSS not above the P18b base; output parity
  on both compilers. Runs with or before T5b2 (same reopen path).

### P18c.6 Audit

Review delegation (Codex gpt-6.2-astra, ultra) over the P18c commits. Required findings, all fixed in b2fb727:
1. The const generic `K` clashed with a Pruv parameter named `K`: renamed `PRUV__K` in both codegens, host test
   `named_k` added.
2. The fair lane's current timing consumed only `o[0]` of the by-value result, so the optimizer could drop the other
   words: `fair_val` now black-boxes the whole `(r, o)` (P18c.3 reports the cost, about 4-5 instructions).
3. SPEC promised where the words live (registers, no store): rewritten to state the meaning only.

Optional: an E0080 must-reject test for `K > 2^40` (added); a unit-return case (Pruv entries cannot return unit, so
an i64 entry whose only parameter is the result buffer, `only_out`, covers the empty-argument form instead); the
attach lane's `uk` black-box differs from the hand lane's (predates P18c, unchanged; noted for the M7 harness owner).
Confirm audit (same reviewer, only the three fix scopes): scopes 1 and 2 FIXED; scope 3 had one required finding,
the SPEC text said a too-small `K` always panics in a checked build, but an entry without a length `requires` (M7
`c_current`) just runs and returns a status (3 for `K = 0`). Fixed: SPEC now says a small `K` gives what the twin
gives, panicking only when a declared `requires` is violated.

## Appendix P18d: fixed-prefix by-value results through calls

### P18d.1 Surface (SPEC "Fixed-prefix internal results")

Only under `--proven-entries` (Rust backend), with no output change otherwise. For an internal, concrete (generic
functions only through their specializations), non-foreign function `NAME` whose last parameter is `inout o: [i64]`,
both compilers (`pruvc/fixed_prefix.py`, `pruvc-rs/crates/pruv-core/src/fixed_prefix.rs`) derive a prefix length K
from the body. Every use of `o` must be one of:

- U1 `o[c] = e` and U2 `o[c]` with a literal `c` (K > c);
- U3 `len(o) OP c` or `c OP len(o)` with a literal `c`, K chosen so the comparison has the same outcome for the
  length L and for `min(L, K)`;
- U4 `inout o` passed as the last argument to another planned function (K >= that function's K).

Anything else (`o` in arithmetic, a slice op, a non-last position, a non-planned callee, a return, recursion, K > 16)
rejects the function, which keeps the buffer form. Planned functions get three Rust items:

- `NAME(args, o: &mut [i64])`, pinned always: `pruv_fn = min(o.len(), K)`, copy `o[..pruv_fn]` into `[0i64; K]`,
  call the core, copy `[..pruv_fn]` back;
- `NAME__pruv_fp(args, pruv_fa: [i64; K], pruv_fn: usize) -> (RT, [i64; K])`, which runs the body on
  `&mut pruv_fa[..pruv_fn]`; for K = 1 it is `(args, pruv_f0: i64, pruv_fn) -> (RT, i64)` (P18d.3);
- `NAME__pruv_fpb`, the original body, pinned always.

The body sees `min(L, K)` words instead of L. Every access is a literal index below K or a length comparison whose
outcome does not change, and unwritten words keep their copied-in value. So the row's "every word written on every
path" proof is not needed. The one difference is a panic between a write and the return: the copy-back is skipped.
plan_fp therefore runs only in a verified build without the G10 runtime, proc, net, ev or par groups. A fixpoint
`may_unwind` drops every function that can reach, through calls, a foreign function, `print` or a G6 catalog
operation (its boundary helper panics on a failed check or an exhausted check budget). The inline policy gives
`__pruv_fp` the base name's call-site count only when the whole triple is present.

M7 (bench/l3/budget): current (K 3), is_halted, reopen, reopen_b (K 1) get twins. maybe_close is a pub entry
(P18c val form); attach's put_key writes a key-length prefix (rejected). `bud_lifecycle.pruv` writes `out[0]` in
reopen_b and maybe_close as a literal index. `driver_m7.rs` now times reopenmiss and closereopen through `fair_val`.

### P18d.3 The one fix attempt: K = 1 scalar return

The first build returned `(RT, [i64; 1])` from the core. Rust returns that pair indirectly, through a hidden result
pointer (`stp x23, x24, [x0]` in reopen_b's core, a store and a reload at each caller). That cost M reopenmiss
407 vs base 393.9 and closereopen 556.0 vs 548.3. For K = 1 both codegens now pass and return the single word as
an `i64` (`(RT, i64)`, a register pair). The cells came back to the base ranges (P18d.2). K > 1 (only current here,
whose val entry inlines) keeps `[i64; K]`. This fix landed after both audits (P18d.6). Its gates are P18d.5.

### P18d.4 Not met: cells above hand16 and `__text`

The by-value core does not lower the cells. The word that was stored through the caller's pointer is now copied
into and out of the adapter's local array. That store left the core but did not leave the call chain, so the
instruction counts overlap the base. Line-level causes, recorded as debt D9 and D10 (§7.5):

- attach (1.27 / 1.25x at M/L): put_key writes a key-length prefix, so attach has no fixed K and keeps the buffer
  form.
- closereopen (1.23x): the maybe_close half is a pub entry. It keeps its P18c val array and writes through it, and
  the reopen half pays the reopenmiss cost below.
- reopenmiss (1.18 / 1.16x): reopen_b has 12 parameters, so the tail is stack-passed, and the core carries a
  run-time `pruv_fn` (the length check stays). The remaining gap is the reopen body (T5b2, unchanged).
- `__text` +3,072 B is a fixed share. The pinned adapters' copy-in and copy-out are inlined into each host caller:
  `raw_call` +952, `run_perf` +596, `c_call` +420, `one` +388, two `run_perf` closures +416 / +376. The core is the
  old body (reopen_b 11,648 -> 11,636). This is the same per-host-copy multiplication as P13k.2.
- S cells (attach 1.21, closereopen 1.13, reopenmiss 1.11 at S = 100) go to D5.

### P18d.6 Audit

Review (Codex gpt-6.2-astra, ultra, read-only) over the uncommitted change before the K = 1 fix:
1. must-fix: a body that panics after writing `o` loses the write under `catch_unwind`, because the adapter copies
   back only on return (reproduced with `--no-verify`). Fixed: twins only in verified builds without the
   G10/proc/net/ev/par groups, and `may_unwind` excludes functions that reach a foreign function or `print`.
2. must-fix: generic functions. Twins are made only for concrete specializations (the candidate filter). SPEC says
   so.
3. should: the inline-policy `__pruv_fp` suffix could match a user function named that way. It now applies only when
   the whole triple is present (tests in `check_generated.py` and `inline_policy.rs`).

Confirm audit (same reviewer, only those scopes): 2 and 3 resolved. 1 was not resolved: the G6 catalog boundary
helper (`string_push_str` under `--foreign-checks all --contract-budget 1`) can panic after a write. Fixed after the
confirm: `may_unwind` also excludes catalog operations in both compilers, with a must-reject test. No new must-fix.
The audit budget (one review plus one confirm) was then spent. The catalog fix and the later K = 1 scalar return
(P18d.3) were not re-audited. They are covered by the P18d.5 gates only.

## Appendix P25.8a (queued P25.8 item: hand error path in hdiff)

Result: the hand error path already existed (P26, Appendix P26.1: `card_error(kind, en)`, `emit_card_error`), and
hdiff already compared full error words, but only with one open budget, so kind 0 (no current budget) was never
reached, and the generator lived in an uncommitted work file. This row moves the generator into `run_m11.py --hdiff`,
adds the kind 0 scenarios and per-kind checks, and changes only the measurement harness: `harness.rs` and
`run_m11.py`. `hand.rs`, `root.pruv`, the `.pruv` sources and both compilers are unchanged. No proof meaning changed.

Base: main a9ac433, release `pruvc-rs` built in the worktree, macOS arm64. Work files in `work/p25_8/` (not committed).

### P25.8a.1 Change

- `harness.rs` `hand_diff(card, lang, by, scen)`: both sides load the same budget `s1 -> b1`; `scen` 1 = the found
  budget is `closed`, 2 = unknown session `s2`, 3 = `ref` budgetId `b2` against `b1`, 4 = no `ref.sessionId` and
  an empty sid. For scen 1..4 the expected kind is 0; for scen 0 it is the validation kind (or ok). Two calls per
  card (the second reads the stored budget). Each call compares the whole hand words with the Pruv words, and in
  addition: the raw Pruv length prefix equals the returned word count (`World::call` clamps it to the buffer), on an
  error `used_now` equals `kind >= 3` on both sides, `saved`/`changed` are 0 on both sides, and the value is exactly
  `{ok:false, error:<string>}` with equal UTF-16 units. A malformed packet must be refused by both (Pruv status 2,
  hand -2). Output: `same err <kind> <en> <used_now>` / `same ok` / `same refused` / `differ ...`. The perf
  functions are byte-identical to the base.
- `run_m11.py --hdiff`: the P26 generator ported unchanged (10,711 items at scen 0, checked equal in order and
  label to `work/p26/p26/hdiff.py`), the same items again at scen 1 (`closed:`), and 770 crafted `kind` items
  (one card per validation kind plus one valid card, 22 cards, x 7 `lang` inputs `en`/`ko`/`EN`/empty/1/null/absent
  x scen 0..4). It fails on any differ, an output line-count mismatch, a `used_now` other than `kind >= 3`, or an
  empty cell in the kind 0..6 x en 0/1 table.

Four of the five extra pages are entry bodies copied into each `World::call` closure (P33: inline attribute of
generated entries; the per-call-site copies are what the closures execute) and the `bud_map` store write
(`put_at`, a file outside this row). Hand's code is 1 page because its set_card path is ~6 KB in one place. A link
order file (`-order_file`) can move these atoms next to touched std pages, but it also moves hand addresses and
is a build-option layout choice, not a code rule; not used (P26a measured it: A +32 / H +16).

The code-placement research (Codex) confirmed the levers: CGU assignment follows the defining module, items in a
CGU are emitted in mangled-name order, ld keeps input-object order per output section; `#[cold]` creates no
separate section on Mach-O, `#[inline]`/item order cannot put generated code on std pages. The only rule-based cut
is fewer executed bytes; P26c is that cut for H.

## Appendix P13i: lifecycle fixed share and the attach id copy

Scope of this package: parts (a) and (b) of row P13i. Part (c) (`bud_store::need` slack and the fixed 254 KB) needs
`bud_store.pruv`, which row P13j owns, so it stays open.

### P13i.1 Attribution of (a)

The lifecycle bodies (`maybe_close`, `replace`, `reopen`, `attach`) already reach records through the direct `xa`/`xb`
paths, so the fix named in the row has nothing left to change. The M7 driver `__text` growth (c3ec58d 413,244 B ->
5832908 457,532 B) comes from P13e giving `bud_store::ef` / `set_ef` an `#[inline]` attribute: with them inlined,
`bud_map::find_w` becomes small enough for LLVM to inline it at every call site. Experiments on hand-edited generated
Rust (M7 driver, fair lane, R = 20000):

| variant | change | `__text` (B) | instructions |
|---|---|---|---|
| base (5832908) | none | 457,532 | reference |
| A | `ef`/`set_ef` `#[inline(always)]` | 458,236 | no gain |
| B | `find_w` `#[inline(never)]` | 421,436 | +12..+25 per call on current, isHalted, reopenmiss, closereopen |
| C | cold fallback paths, `find_w` out of line | 422,268 | same losses as B |
| E | C's cold fallbacks, `find_w` `#[inline(always)]` | 454,140 | wins on every cell (attach 392 -> 376, reopenmiss 383 -> 373, current 322 -> 311, isHalted 319 -> 304) |

No variant restores `__text` without an instruction loss, and every lever (the shape of `bud_map::find_w`, the
`ef`/`set_ef` attributes in `bud_store.pruv`, or the compiler inline policy) is outside this package's files. Peak
RSS is also not restored: c3ec58d attach S 2752-2784 KiB, M 4496-4544 KiB against 2800-2848 / 4608-4656 KiB for
both 5832908 and this package (3 interleaved rounds). Part (a) is handed back. Suggested follow-up: a `bud_map` row
that takes E's cold-fallback split (it pays in instructions on all five cells) together with a size lever that keeps
those gains.

### P13i.2 Design of (b)

`attach` on the ref path used to copy the packed id into `out` (`[3, n, id words]`). It now returns a view of the
stored id, `[6, n, off]`, where the packed id words are `st[off..off + words(n))` inside the stored record, the same
way `current` returns a budget view `[4, n, off]`. The length word is clamped into 0..2^30 as `put_key` does, so the
view's length and the words checked against the record agree. The view is valid until the next change of `st`. Being 3
words, it fits the 4096-word out buffer for any id, so the hand reference (`hand_m7_u16.rs`) drops its out-buffer limit
on this path and `diff_hand_m7.py` expects a value for the 16,377-unit control (OPEN and halted `replace` keep the
limit). The OPEN path keeps `[3, n, id words]` (its id is the caller's
`uk`). The M7 driver reads tag 6 from `st` in egress, `rchk_fold` and `consume`; the consume checksum folds the same
words as the tag-3 form, so result checks are unchanged. No proof annotation changed and no admit, assume or opaque
was added; no compiler change.

Decision: keep the bench flags `-C opt-level=3 --edition 2021` and the T5b.3 reporting rule. `-C codegen-units=1`
loses axes on both sides: Pruv instructions on every M4 cell, hand instructions on every M4 cell and M7 reopenmiss,
Pruv `__text`, and the M7 Pruv peak by a small margin. The row's switch condition is not met. No Pruv/hand ratio
crosses 1.0x under cgu1.

### T5d.1 Method

- Base main a21f8b5, compiler `pruvc-rs/target/release/pruvc` of the main checkout, rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13) of
  `~/.cargo/bin`. Scratch scripts in `work/t5d/` (not committed): `build.py`, `measure.py`,
  `summarize.py`, `alloccount.c`.

## Appendix P13f: M4 bench adapter length bound, paid once outside the timed loop

Row P13f. Base main 9925a2c. No compiler change, no `.pruv` change. Changed files: `bench/l3/budget/state_buf.rs`,
`bench/l3/budget/m34_test/driver_m4.rs`, `bench/l3/budget/m34_test/run.py`, and (audit must, P13f.5)
`driver_m4c.rs`, `driver_m4cb.rs`. All but `state_buf.rs` sit inside P13j's `m34_test/*` area.

### P13f.1 Mechanism: bounded owner types, no proven entries

SPEC "Length bound at host boundaries": a checked pub entry tests `len <= 2^40` (cold `pruv_len_slow`, exit 101
`pruv: invalid representation: N (array length)`) and calls the private `__pruv_body`. The driver never calls
`__pruv_body`. Instead every buffer the driver hands to an entry is an owner type whose constructor refuses a length
above `2^40` and whose `Deref` tells the optimizer so:
- `state_buf.rs`: `STATE_MAX_WORDS = 1 << 40`. `StateBuf::zeroed(n)` returns `None` for `n > STATE_MAX_WORDS`
  before allocating (like an allocator failure); `zeroed_or_abort` panics with "state buffer of N words is too large"
  instead of `handle_alloc_error`. `Deref`/`DerefMut` wrap `from_raw_parts` in
  `std::hint::assert_unchecked(self.len <= STATE_MAX_WORDS)` (sound: `zeroed` is the only constructor).
- `driver_m4.rs`: `struct Words(Vec<i64>)` for the op words and the `out` buffer. `Words::new`, `Words::zeroed` and
  `Words::resize` check the bound once (cold `words_too_long`, the same message and exit 101 as a generated entry);
  `Deref`/`DerefMut` are `#[inline(always)]` with the same `assert_unchecked`. The perf op list (`Vec<Words>`) is
  built before the timed loop, so the check is paid once per op at setup. `out` growth (status 3) is clamped with
  `.min(STATE_MAX_WORDS)`; the import and observe scratch buffers are clamped the same way.
- Result: the entry's inline compare folds away on every lane with no codegen change. `nm` on the new perf binary:
  `m4_op`, `m4_init`, `m4_import` `pruv_len_slow` are gone (dead after folding); only `m4_observe`'s remains, which
  runs outside the timed loop on a plain clamped `Vec`.
- Proven entries (`--proven-entries`, P18b `PruvArr`) were not used: the driver's buffers are owned and grown, so a
  proof wrapper would be rebuilt (`new_mut`) on every call, and the LLVM lanes have no proven twins. The owner type
  carries the same fact in the type without touching either compiler.
- Inlining note: dereferencing `Words` inside the state-call closure left `World::exec::{closure#0}` out of line
  (+5..+20 instr/op). `exec` now derefs `op` and `out` to slices before the closure; the closure inlines as at base.
  `m4c`/`m4cb` replace the World section and take `&Words` through deref coercion (files unchanged).

### P13f.2 Probe

`driver_m4 bound state` checks `StateBuf::zeroed(2^40 + 1)` and `zeroed(usize::MAX / 8 + 1)` return `None` with no
allocation (`ALLOC_COUNT + STATE_MAPS` unchanged): stdout `bound state refused=true allocs=0`.
`driver_m4 bound words` calls `Words::zeroed(2^40 + 1)`: exit 101, empty stdout, stderr
`pruv: invalid representation: 1099511627777 (array length)`. `run.py m4` runs both after every build and fails the
lane on a mismatch ("length bound probe ok").

### P13f.5 Audit (Codex gpt-6.2-astra ultra): does the bound cover every length

No path found on any of the 9 lanes (64-bit) where a slice over `2^40` reaches a Pruv body or an `assert_unchecked`
premise breaks: initial/reinit state via `zeroed_or_abort`, grow only after `StateBuf::zeroed` succeeds, import and
replace move or clone checked buffers, every q/perf op through `Words::new`, `out` doubling clamped.
- must, fixed: `m4c`/`m4cb` keep their own `out` (`out2`) as `Vec<i64>`; `need = max(4096, 4 * len)` was not
  clamped, so a state of `2^38 + 1` words would try a `2^40 + 4` word buffer (the C adapter would still refuse it
  before the body). `driver_m4c.rs:116`, `driver_m4cb.rs:147,181` now clamp `need` to `STATE_MAX_WORDS`;
  `run.py m4c`/`m4cb` 300/300, probe ok, after the fix. The q gate rows in P13f.3 for these lanes are this rerun.
- should, open: `1 << 40` as `usize` does not compile for a 32-bit target (the bench is 64-bit only); the probe's
  `allocs=0` counts successful maps only (the source refuses before the map call); the probe does not exercise
  `Words::new`/`resize` or the C lanes' `out`. nit, open: the header says `Words::new` checks before allocating; it
  checks an already collected `Vec`.

## Appendix P13f2: P13f audit should/nits (bound constant width, refused-length probe, `Words::new` comment)

Base main b29259c. Files: `bench/l3/budget/state_buf.rs`, `m34_test/driver_m4.rs`, `m34_test/run.py`. No `.pruv`, no
compiler change. Notes and scripts in `work/p13f2` (not committed).

### P13f2.1 Changes

- `STATE_MAX_WORDS` is computed from a `u64` `1 << 40`: `BOUND as usize` when `BOUND <= usize::MAX as u64`, else
  `usize::MAX`. On 64-bit it is exactly 2^40 (same constant, same code); on 32-bit no `1 << 40` overflow and no extra
  test (no slice there can exceed 2^40 elements). Checked with a `u32` stand-in of the expression (2^32 - 1 for 32-bit,
  2^40 for 64-bit); no 32-bit Rust target is installed here, the bench stays 64-bit.
- `Words` comments: `zeroed` and `resize` check before allocating; `new` checks an already built `Vec` (it does not
  prevent that allocation); together they guarantee no `Words` is longer than `STATE_MAX_WORDS`, which is what the
  `Deref` `assert_unchecked` needs.
- `driver_m4 bound state` adds an at-bound control: after the two refused lengths (`2^40 + 1` and `usize::MAX / 8 + 1`)
  it makes `StateBuf::zeroed(STATE_MAX_WORDS)`. When built (macOS maps 8 TiB lazily) the count (allocator calls plus
  successful maps) must move by exactly 1; when the OS refuses it, by at most 1. Output
  `bound state refused=true allocs=0 at_bound=built|refused at_bound_ok=true`, checked by `run.py` on every lane.
  So `allocs=0` on the refused lengths is read against a counter shown to see a buffer one word below the cut.
  Mutation: `state_buf.rs` without the `n > STATE_MAX_WORDS` test prints `refused=false allocs=1` (the 2^40 + 1 map
  succeeds lazily on macOS), so the probe fails as it should.

### P13f2.2 Counting map attempts: measured, not taken

The audit's other reading of "a refused length that never allocates" is to count map calls before the call
(`STATE_MAPS` incremented unconditionally), so a regression that calls `mmap` and is refused would also show. Measured
on the 9 M4 cells (5 rounds): +0.5..1.1 instr/op on every cell, distributions not overlapping base (e.g. sessions 1000
base 464.0-464.1, attempts 465.0-465.1). Cause: `StateBuf::zeroed` is inlined into `World::exec`; moving the increment
changes register allocation there (`World::exec` -68 B, spills reordered). Moving the increment into
`state_map::map` costs the same. The constant change alone leaves `World::exec` identical to base. Dropped by the
no-give-back rule; `STATE_MAPS` keeps counting successful maps. Left open: on an OS that refuses an 8 TiB map
(e.g. Linux heuristic overcommit), a regression that calls `mmap` for `2^40 + 1` words would be refused by the OS and
pass the probe; on macOS (this bench) it is caught.

## Appendix P13j (row P13j: store bounds from the P13e audit)

Result: both bounds are proved `ensures` and each has a gate case that fails on a4427ec and passes now. No new
`admit`, `assume` or `opaque`; no compiler change; no layout change (resident format version stays 2). Gates equal
P13e.8. Instructions, peak RSS and allocations are not worse on any M4 / M7 cell. M7 `__text` is 320 B below base;
M4 `__text` is 832 B above base, accepted for the root payload fix; its removal is queued as P13j2 (P13j.4). The final audit's two required findings are fixed (P13j.5).

Base: a4427ec, release `pruvc-rs` (read-only), macOS arm64. Work files in `work/p13j/` (not committed).

### P13j.1 Entry base at the maximum slot count (`bud_store.pruv`, `bud_admit.pruv`)

- Bug: `ea` / `xa` took the entry base as `c32(st[5])`. At s = 2^32 word 5 is 16 + 2^32, the clamp cut it to 2^32,
  and entry 0 sat inside the slot table [16, 16 + 2^32).
- Fix: base = `16 + c32(st[4]) + 10 e` (equal to word 5 on a valid store, since `shape_w` gives w5 = 16 + s). It uses
  the same 2^32 constant as the `c32(st[6])` clamp. A first form `c33(st[5])` (clamp to 2^33) added a second
  materialized constant at every address site: about +4 instructions per op, sessions n = 1000 / 2000 IQR-separated
  above base. It was dropped.
- `ensures` (valid store, 0 <= e < st[6]): `st[3] + st[4] <= result && result + 10 <= st[9]` on `ea` (base and
  extension), `eb`, `xa`, `xb`, `xbm` (on `old(st)`). `ea` also has `(valid(st) && result >= 0) ==> 0 <= e < st[6]`.
- Forced caller change, `bud_admit.pruv`: `ent_i1` and `entry_ok` compute the same base (16 + word 4, word 4 checked
  in [0, 2^32]) so the admission facts name the addresses the store reads. The old 2^32 cut branch is gone.
- Gate: `driver_admit.rs` prints `maxslot` (`entry_addr` = `field_at(st, e, 0)` on a header-only buffer with
  s = 2^32, w5 = 2^32 + 16, w6 = 2^31). `run.py admit` expects 4294967312 / 4294967322 (>= the slot table end).
  a4427ec: 4294967296 / 4294967306 (MISMATCH). New: pass.

### P13j.2 Root payload through grow (`bud_map.pruv`)

- Bug: `grow_copy` copied each root's children but not the root's own payload (values v0..v3, blob); a fresh root in
  `nxt` read as defaults.
- Fix: `copy_node` = `put_node` (key) + `copy_pay` (blob and values). `copy_kids` runs one extra first loop step that
  calls `copy_pay(pr -> nr)` without a budget step, so the root payload goes through the same `copy_pay` site as each
  child's (no third inlined `set_blob` site; a separate `carry_root` call cost about +2.2 KB of `__text` in
  `World::exec`).
- `grow_copy` `ensures result == 0 ==> forall r in 0..3: root_carried(prev, nxt, r) && blob words equal`. The
  writers keep `valid(nxt)` (`kept`) but do not give a frame over the arena, so the property is closed by a compare
  loop over the three roots at the end (`blob_same`, `root_carried`; `nxt` is not written after it). A failing compare
  returns 2 (the old state stays valid, as for the live-count check). `root_carried` reads the base and extension at
  w5 + 10 r (+ 10 w6) of each buffer, the addresses `ef` / `blob_len` read on a valid store; a missing extension
  reads as the defaults.
- Gate: admit case 24 = case 19 with a blob (2 units) and v0..v3 on roots 0..2; `root_pay_diff` compares values,
  blob length and units through the public accessors after `admit_grow`. a4427ec: pay_diff 1 (MISMATCH). New: 0.

### P13j.5 Final audit (Codex gpt-6.2-astra ultra)

- Required 1, empty root blob with a free offset: admission does not check the offset of an empty blob (`span_w`
  with cap 0 is true), so an admitted root may hold blob length 0 with offset -1 or past the buffer. `copy_pay`
  passed that offset to `set_blob` (rejects `s0 > len(src)`) and `root_carried` required `po >= 0`, so grow failed
  on an admitted store (regression of P13j.2). Fix: `copy_pay` passes offset 0 when the length is 0; `root_carried`
  returns true for n = 0 (an empty blob reads nothing). Gate: admit cases 25 / 26 = case 19 with v0..v3 on root 0 and
  blob offset `len(st) + 1` / -1. Before the fix: grow [2, 7, 3, 1] / [2, 7, 7, 0]; now 0, live 7 -> 7, pay_diff 0
  (run.py requires `[0, 7, 7, 0]` for cases 24..26).
- Required 2, raw words against clamped reads: the `ensures` compared raw offset / length words while `blob_len` /
  `blob_unit` read `c40(offset) + j` and `c40(length)`. Fix: `root_carried` requires n, po, no in [0, 2^40] when
  n > 0, the range where the raw words equal the clamped reads.
- Optional: the `grow_copy` cost comment now says linear in the summed blob lengths of the three roots.
- Re-gated after the fixes: P13j.3 (rs then py, identical), mut_m9, corrupt_resident, M11, and P13j.4.

## Appendix P13i(c): M7 proportional and fixed peak RSS, attributed (base main 5a82208)

### P13i(c).1 Method

Instrumented scratch copies of the M7 driver (`mincore` resident bytes per store region after setup, `task_info`
resident size after every grow) and of hand16 (a counting global allocator, live and peak heap bytes after each
setup). Peak RSS is `/usr/bin/time -l` maximum resident set size. Single lane: `perf S 5 attach f` (Pruv) against
`perf S 5 attach typed` (hand16), two Worlds alive in each.

### P13i(c).2 `need` slack: one page resident after setup

At S = 1000 the store grows 256 -> 262144 words (s = 8192, cap = 4096, 1003 entries, arena 160,000 words used of
172,016). Resident per World after setup: slots 80 KiB, entry bases 96 KiB, extensions 96 KiB, arena used 1264 KiB,
arena rest 16 KiB (one page past the top). The doubling slack of `bud_store::need` is never written (`init_store`
writes the header, the slot table and the three roots; `grow_copy` appends at the arena top), so after setup at S = 1000 `mincore` shows one 16 KiB page
of it resident (the full run's `close` item copies whole stores, tail included, with
`copy_from_slice`; that is a harness copy, not `need`). `need` is not the source of the proportional share; nothing in bud_store.pruv changes.

### P13i(c).3 Proportional share: the record text encoding

Per World and session, Pruv holds 1.49 KiB resident (the arena record is 160 words = 1.26 KiB), hand16 0.90 KiB of
live heap. The record (driver `rec()`, bud_lifecycle record layout) stores the `rest` text (PERF_REST, 95
UTF-16 units) and the date (24 units) one unit per i64 word; hand16 keeps both as u16 text (`Stamp::Text`), so the text data alone
differs by (95 + 24) x (8 - 2) = 714 B per session. Experiment: the same driver with `PERF_REST = "{}"` uses 67 arena words per session (160 before) and the
single-lane peak RSS slope drops from 4.95 to 2.40 KiB per session (S = 100 -> 1000; hand16 3.56). The excess is the
text words times two Worlds, times the grow transient (old and new store alive during `t_grow`, and libmalloc keeping
the freed large blocks resident: after the last grow at S = 1000 RSS is 4624 KiB for a 1488 KiB store on a 1792 KiB
start). Packing the record text (4 units per word, as keys already are) changes the bud_lifecycle record layout read
by Pruv and the M7 wire; it is outside this package's files and is queued for the main session as a row
("P13i2: pack the M7 record rest/date text 4 units per word in bud_lifecycle and the driver; expected about
-0.6 KiB per session per World").

### P13i(c).4 Full-run peak: a harness asymmetry, fixed in the driver

The full `perf S 5` run kept every item's World alive (`let mut w = setup(0)` shadowing at the top of `run_perf`,
10+ Worlds), while hand16 scopes each item in an `if typed && on(..) { .. }` block. The driver now puts each item (World and
ops, `close` included) in its own block and drops the item World before the typed and fair lanes build theirs; in
`replace` the timed World stays alive during the verification setup, as hand16's shadowed Host does (audit fix).
The single-lane path, the printed values and every timed loop are unchanged.

### P13i(c).5 Fixed share

At S = 1 (single lane) Pruv peaks at 1808 KiB, hand16 at 1632 KiB: +176 KiB. `__text` is 457,916 B against 311,484
(+143 KiB of code, the open P13k size lever), plus the 4096-word out buffer (32 KiB). The 254 KiB intercept of the
full-run fit also carried the extra Worlds of P13i(c).4.

## Appendix P13j2: root-compare loop, not done (split)

The `grow_copy` root payload `ensures` needs, without the compare loop, facts no writer states today: (a) content
`ensures` on `set_blob`/`copy_pay` (the blob words and values of pe land in ne), (b) frame `ensures` on `arena_put`
(words 16 .. old top unchanged) and `xbm` (only its record and flag word written), and (c) a copy order in which no
child write follows a root's payload copy: child linking writes the root's extension words 7/8 and may create it
(`xbm`), `set_ef(18)` rewrites base word 9 (only `has_x` is kept), and `set_blob`'s in-place path writes an old region
whose disjointness from the other roots' blobs is not stated anywhere. Proposed split: P13j2a (a) with admit 24-26,
P13j2b (b), P13j2c copy root payloads after all children through the single `copy_kids` site and drop
`blob_same`/the compare loop, measuring M4 `__text`. Left open in this package (one-hour step cap). Audit preconditions for P13j2c: (1) `grow_copy` checks only `valid(prev)`, so a root
extension with raw blob length -1 and zero scalars passes; `copy_pay` clamps the length with `c32` and copies an
empty payload, and today only the compare loop returns 2; dropping it without checking the raw length (and, for a
non-empty blob, the raw offset and range) breaks the `ensures`. (2) `copy_pay` returns 0 without touching ne when pe
has no extension, and `set_blob` can reach 0 after a failed `xbm` on a general buffer, so the content contract needs
the premise that the destination payload is default, and must cover the four scalars after `set_vals`; the second
pass must show the reused region does not overlap an earlier root's blob. (3) Pass 1's invariant is "root payload
default" (not "no extension": the first child may create it); pass 2 copies roots only, without re-inserting
children or charging budget, and keeps child links and earlier roots' flags, scalars and blob words.

## Appendix P13j2a: content `ensures` on `set_blob` / `copy_pay`

Status: done on the Rust and Python compilers; proof facts only. On top of f5d9891. Changed: `B/bud_map.pruv`
(+158 -1), `B/bud_store.pruv` (+64): `ensures`, loop invariants, `assert` and `reveal` only. No statement changed and
no fn added.

### P13j2a.1 Contracts

Addresses below are written inline: entry base `st[5] + 10 * e`, extension `base + 10 * st[6]`, flag word `base + 9`
read through `has_x`, extension words 1 = blob offset, 2 = blob length, 3..6 = the four scalars. "Payload" is
logical: a missing extension reads as an empty blob and zero scalars, as in `root_carried`.

- bud_store:
  - `has_x`: the negative-key case.
  - `ea`/`eb`/`xa`/`xb`: exact address under `valid` (base, extension, or -1 iff `!has_x`).
  - `xbm`:
    - the result is the extension address;
    - a flag word that was 0 or `has_x` ends `has_x`, and a 0 flag becomes 1;
    - an existing extension's flag is kept;
    - a new extension has word 2 = 0;
    - words from the old top `st[9]` to the end are unchanged.
  - `xfield`: values for f 12/13/19.
  - `ef(12)`: reads extension word 1.
  - `set_ef(12/13/19)` on an existing extension: writes only that word, keeps the flag, frame from old `st[9]`.
  - `set_vals`:
    - words 3..6 are a..d whenever the result has an extension;
    - flag and words 1/2 are kept for an existing extension;
    - a fresh flag becomes 1 when any value is non-zero, and a new extension's word 2 = 0;
    - all-zero values on no extension leave none;
    - frame from old `st[9]`.
  - `arena_put`: `result == old st[10]`, words written, words 16 .. result kept, `result >= old st[9]`.
- bud_map:
  - `gf`/`sf` (f 12/13/19), `fits_region` (range), `write_at` (content and frame), `put_units` (content).
  - `set_blob`:
    - **No extension before** (flag 0, or `!has_x` for length and words): with 0 < n <= 2^32, length n at a new
      region `old st[10]`, the region lies above `st[9]` and inside the buffer, and the words equal `src[s..s+n)`.
      The extension bit itself is proved only from flag 0.
    - **Existing extension**: length n, and for n > 0 and offset >= 0 the words at the stored offset equal
      `src[s..s+n)`.
    - **n = 0 on no extension**: none is created (flag 0 stays 0).
  - `copy_pay`:
    - pe without an extension: nxt is unchanged.
    - pe with an extension and ne ending with one: the four scalars are equal.
    - pe with an extension and a fresh ne (flag 0):
      - 0 < length: ne has an extension, the same length, offset `old nxt[10]`, and the blob words equal;
      - length 0: ne's length is 0, or ne has no extension and pe's scalars are all 0.
    - existing ne extension with offset >= 0: the same length and words.

For a fresh destination with flag word 0, the logical payload of pe (blob length, blob words, scalars) equals ne's
after `copy_pay`. In `grow_copy` this covers the root only: `init_store` sets the root's flag word to 0. A child is
not covered: `put_node` stores the key before `copy_pay`, and `set_key_region` writes `2 * n` into word 9, so a child
with a non-empty key and no extension is in unproved state 1 below (audit finding). `grow_copy`'s root payload `ensures`
and the compare loop are unchanged (P13j2c removes the loop).

For P13j2c: on the existing-extension path `copy_pay` states length and word equality but not that ne's offset and
span stay inside the buffer, which `root_carried` also needs. If P13j2c links children first so that the root already
has an extension, these contracts alone do not justify removing the compare loop (audit, optional).

### P13j2a.2 Unproved destination states (left to P13j2b if P13j2c needs them)

1. Flag word non-zero but `!has_x` (a freed-extension state, and every new child after `put_node` stores its key): that `set_blob` sets the extension bit is not proved.
   The verifier returns `verify_unknown` (timeout) for it, so `copy_pay` states the full payload equality only from
   flag 0.
2. An existing destination extension with a negative stored offset and n > 0 (`set_blob` takes the append path):
   length and word equality are not proved. Stating it fails with `cannot prove postcondition` (counterexample offset
   -1), so it is excluded by the premise `0 <= offset`.

### P13j2a.3 Language finding

The contracts had to be written inline, as raw address arithmetic, for two reasons:

- Every new `fn` is emitted into the generated Rust, even one used only in contracts or `assert`s. A helper
  `pay_def` changed the generated code.
- An i64 fn with an `if` (`xb`, `c32`, `c40`) cannot be called in a contract (`call_in_contract`).

The cost is long repeated premises. A ghost (spec-only, not emitted) fn would remove them. This is a language-gap row
candidate and was not worked around in the compilers.

## Appendix P13i2: M7 record text as bytes (P13i2 split, built in P13i2a)

P13i2 (base main 4747c4b) stopped after the read-and-design step with no source change; P13i2.1-P13i2.4 are that
step. P13i2a built the design (P13i2a.1-P13i2a.6) on top of its own steps 1 (`#[inline]` attributes, 0bf3e5d) and 2
(`copy_range`, 3b4add7, row L-copy-range).

### P13i2.1 Who reads and writes the record text

| place | strings 1-3 (openedAt, activeSince, ended.at text) and 5 (rest) |
|---|---|
| `bud_lifecycle.pruv` | `str_words` stride `1 + len`, `str_at` / `str_pos_in`, `rewrite` (copies 1, 2, 5, writes 3), `rec_bound`, `put_str`; `reopen` tests `str_len_in(3) == 0` |
| `bud_halt.pruv` | `halted()` sizes the record as `30 + .. + l1 + l2 + l3 + .. + rl` and copies strings 1-3 with `put_str` (`l` words each); string 5 becomes a structured halt prefix in words (`-2, reason, kind, at, ids` as framed packed keys) followed by the old rest tail; `prefix_len` and the halt reason read those words |
| `m10_test` (`root_m10.pruv` `str_at`/`rewrite`, `driver_m10.rs` `rec()`, `hand_m10.rs`) | same layout, one unit per word |
| `m7_test` (`driver_m7.rs` `rec()` and egress, `hand_m7_u16.rs` `encode()`) | same layout |

So the rest string is not opaque text in the store: bud_halt writes numbers and packed ids into it. Changing the
layout of strings 1-3 alone (the dates) already breaks `bud_halt::halted()`. Both `bud_halt.pruv` and `m10_test` are
outside row P13i2's files.

### P13i2.2 Representation options

| option | result |
|---|---|
| UTF-16 units 4 per word, or bytes 8 per word, inside the `[i64]` arena | rejected: the project rule keeps strings out of i64 words (the "4 units per word" of P13i(c).3 is withdrawn) |
| a `[u8]` view of the `[i64]` arena | not in the language (SPEC §6b: no `[u8]`/`[i64]` conversion) and bytes-in-words in disguise |
| a typed store `struct { words: [i64], text: [u8] }` changed in place | language gap: buffer fields are read-only views (SPEC §6e) and fields cannot be `inout` places (§6g); §3 of this spec already says not to assume field `inout` |
| a second resident `[u8]` text arena `tx` beside `st` (two `inout` arrays, existing features) | feasible; chosen for P13i2a |

### P13i2.3 Proposed P13i2a

- `tx: [u8]` beside `st`, written by the host at ingress only. The text comes from UTF-16 (JS) and may hold lone
  surrogates, so it is WTF-8 (`[u8]`, never `str`, §2.1 G4), decoded back to units at egress.
- Record strings 1-3 and the rest tail are handles `(byte len, byte off)` into `tx`; the halt prefix stays structured
  words (`rl, -2, reason, kind, at, ids, tail handle`). Lifecycle and halt bodies copy handles and never read bytes,
  so no lifecycle signature takes `tx`; `t_put` checks every span `off + len <= len(tx)` at ingress and egress views
  `[tag, off, len]` are checked against `len(tx)` in Pruv. `reopen`'s ended.at emptiness test reads the byte length.
- Dropped text (OPEN, session delete) is garbage in `tx` until `t_grow` compacts it (a lifecycle-level walk of live
  records, O(live text)); hand16 frees per drop, so the garbage bound (ingress bytes since the last grow) must be
  measured against hand16's peak.
- Size per M7 perf session and World: record 160 words (1280 B) -> 24 + 12 (id) + 3 x 2 + 1 (follows) + 2 (rest) = 45
  words (360 B) plus 119 text bytes, about 479 B; hand16 holds about 0.90 KiB of live heap per session.
- Files: `bud_lifecycle.pruv`, `bud_halt.pruv`, `m7_test/{root.pruv, driver_m7.rs, hand_m7_u16.rs, diff_hand_m7.py}`,
  `m10_test/{root_m10.pruv, driver_m10.rs, hand_m10.rs}`. Roots that import bud_lifecycle through bud_map, bud_clock
  or bud_halt (M4, M8, M9, M11, admit) rebuild without source changes; their generated Rust is a gate.

### P13i2.4 Delegations

| work | by |
|---|---|
| reading, attribution of the text readers, representation decision, this appendix | Claude Opus 5.5, direct (no multi-file sweep was needed past a few greps; no audit, nothing to audit) |

### P13i2a.1 What was built

- `bench/l3/budget/m7_test/bud_tx.pruv` (new, shared by the M7 and M10 roots): the resident WTF-8 arena `tx: [u8]`.
  Bytes 0..7 hold the used length (little-endian, `used`/`set_used`; `[u8]` has no u64 load, so 8 byte ops); text
  starts at 8. `put(inout st, inout tx, op, txt, inout out)` is the ingress: it parses the record's text frame
  (`bud_halt::text_frame`), checks each of the five op spans against `len(txt)` (`soff`), plans store room first so
  a text Grow never follows a store change, copies `txt` to `used` with `copy_range` and rebases the five handles in
  the stored blob to absolute arena offsets. `text` is the checked egress view; `grow(inout st, prev, inout next)`
  compacts (P13i2a.2).
- `bud_lifecycle.pruv`: strings 1, 2, 3 hold `0` or `2, byteLen, byteOff`; string 5 holds `0`, a two-word JSON text
  handle, or the halt prefix followed by an optional text handle. Lifecycle bodies move handles only; no lifecycle
  signature called by bud_map/bud_store changed (`reopen` keeps its signature and calls an `#[inline]` body
  `reopen_b`, an explicit directive against the R-7-3 count promotion that `bud_halt`'s extra `rewrite` call
triggered).
- `bud_halt.pruv`: `halted()` sizes and copies the date handles instead of unit strings and keeps the halt prefix as
  structured words with the at-text as a handle; `text_frame` returns the five handle positions.
- `m7_test/{root.pruv, driver_m7.rs, record_text.rs (new), run_m7.py, lifecycle_controls.py, mutant_quiet.py,
  t5c_floor.py}`, `m10_test/{root_m10.pruv, driver_m10.rs, run_m10.py}`: the host converts UTF-16 to WTF-8 at
  ingress and back at egress (`record_text.rs`); the Q protocol keeps the old unit layout at egress and still
  accepts it for raw-state fixtures, so the Q expectations did not change. `hand_m7_u16.rs`/`hand_m10.rs` unchanged.

### P13i2a.2 Compaction bound

`put` returns 4 with the wanted size `want = max(4096, 8 + 4 * (live + need) + walked)` when the text does not fit
(`live` = live text bytes found by a walk of the records, `need` = incoming bytes, `walked` = walk steps). The host
allocates `next` of that size and calls `grow`, which copies only the live spans into `next` from offset 8 and
rewrites their offsets, then retries the put. After a compaction the arena holds `live + need` bytes and has at
least `3 * (live + need) + walked` free, so the next compaction needs at least `3 * (live + need)` more ingress bytes
and copies at most `live + need` plus those bytes. Copy work per ingress byte is therefore at most 4/3 (amortized
O(1)), and the walk is paid once per compaction. Measured with the earlier `2 *` factor (live M7 perf records, 1,000
overwrites per session): 100 / 500 / 1,000 sessions, 981 / 989 / 991 compactions, copied/written 0.981 / 0.989 /
0.991 (`work/p13i2/perf_report.md`, "아레나 압축"); the `4 *` factor and the 4096 floor only add room between
compactions. Garbage (dropped texts) is bounded by the ingress since the last compaction.

### P13i2a.audit-1 copy_range source-range diagnostic

The package audit (Codex, on the step-2 commit 3b4add7 `copy_range`) found no soundness defect: bounds, post-state,
`[u8]` facts, aliasing, evaluation order, both compilers and the LLVM lowering check out. One should-fix finding:
under `--no-verify` the single combined range check reported the destination pair `(i, len(dst))` to `pruv_oob` even
when the source range (`j`, `n` against `len(src)`) was the bad one. Fixed in all four code generators
(`pruvc/codegen.py`, `pruvc/llvmgen.py`, `pruv-core` `codegen.rs`, `llvmgen.rs`): the check is split into the
destination check `i < 0 || n < 0 || i > len(dst) - n` reporting `(i, len(dst))`, then the source check
`j < 0 || j > len(src) - n` reporting `(j, len(src))`; verified code is unchanged (no check). New runtime row
`tests/runtime/l3_rt_copy_range_nv_oob_src` (bad `j`, expects `index out of bounds: 2 (len 3)`); the row list grows
by 2 (rust and llvm, `--no-verify`), regenerated with the Rust `--list-rows`. Gates: `--only runtime` and
`--only g8_frontend` on both compilers (no full run). No confirm audit: the finding is should-fix only.

## Appendix P13k: `#[cold]` attribute; no bud_map split meets the no-give-back rule

### P13k.1 Lever

Pruv had no way to keep a fn out of line: R-7-3 gives every generated fn `#[inline]` or `#[inline(always)]`. The parent
chose a source attribute (rule (c)): `#[cold]` directly before a private top-level `fn`, emitted as `#[cold]`
`#[inline(never)]` on the fn and its body/wrapper items; no effect on checking or verification; anything else
(`#[hot]`, `#[cold(x)]`, `#[cold] pub fn`, inside a body, before `struct`) is a parse error. SPEC.md R-7-3 supplement and
attribute syntax; both compilers (pruvc/vparser.py, vast.py, mono.py, codegen.py; pruvc-rs lexer, parser, ast, mono,
codegen, bindings, abi, llvmgen); accept/reject tests `tests/spec/r7_3_cold{,_pub,_struct,_unknown}`.
Gates: cargo test ok, diff_rust same (fuzz 20), g8_frontend rs 39/39 and py 27/27, list-rows no diff, spec trace.
Audit (Codex, one pass): a `#[cold]` fn that becomes a `--proven-entries` twin crashed both `proven_module`s (the
attribute map knew only `#[inline]`/`#[inline(always)]`); fixed identically, the twin keeps `#[cold]` `#[inline(never)]`,
checked in tests/l3/abi/check_proven_entries.py. Rejecting `#[cold] pub fn` is by design. Reject tests added for
`#[cold()]`, a repeated `#[cold]` and `#[cold]` inside a body; spec trace 252/252 on both compilers, l3_abi 3/3.

### P13k.2 Variants (M7 driver `__text`, base 458,300 B)

All variants were built from source with the new compiler; the generated Rust of the unchanged base sources is
byte-identical to main's. Counters in the M7 build show none of the cold fns runs in any M7 perf item.

Q8 helper replay 136/136. No m6 helper cell is above hand. m11 output is unchanged and the A-lane peak RSS stays at or

  and under `codegen-units=1` the same cells are at or below base. Layout-owned.

`106ae5a`), built with the same `pruvc-rs` as new. Changed files: `bench/l3/budget/{bud_card,bud_date,bud_text}.pruv`,
`bench/l3/budget/m11_test/root.pruv`, `bench/l3/budget/m6_test/{gen_text.py,harness.rs,hand.rs,node_ref.mjs,root.pruv,run_m6.py}`,

### P27.1 Intent, bug, accident (original: `reference/backend-request-budget.ts` + JS built-ins)

| Flow | Intent (kept exactly) | Bug | Accident | Chosen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| limitText | unlimited -> no-limit text, else `String(limit)` | - | `String(n)` of a double; equal to the decimal for safe ints | intent; inputs are safe ints |
| amountText | `used/limit`, time used = `floor(activeMs/60000)` | - | `Math.floor(ms/60000)` is double division; near 2^53 it can differ from the exact floor | exact floor (known difference K-min; run_m6 counts it as `ts_inexact_minutes`) |
| refusal / continueText | template(counter name, amount) per lang | - | lang other than `ko`/`en` falls back to ko via `entry[language] ?? entry.ko`; `Object.prototype` names return a non-string (outside the typed domain) | intent: en only for exact `en`; prototype names excluded (`lang_excluded`) |
| refusalWire | key `budget.refusal.<reason>`, args {used (time in minutes), limit} | - | args are doubles | intent with i64 args; key is ASCII bytes |
| cardMissing / card errors | fixed text per lang | - | - | intent |
| budgetUnitOf | absent setting -> DEFAULT_BUDGET + defaultUnlimited | - | - | intent (`bud_num::unit_of`, no text) |
| ISO date | `Date#toISOString` for `|ms| <= 8.64e15`: `YYYY` / `+YYYYYY` / `-YYYYYY` | - | - | intent |
| card text length | ECMAScript trim, 1..300 UTF-16 units; raw note <= 300 units | - | - | intent; inputs stay UTF-16 units (they are compared in units) |

### P27.2 Representation and contracts

- Every text output is `[u8]` UTF-8 source bytes (G4), allocated once with its length computed first: never F1,
  never UTF-16 unit payloads, never flat `[i64]` records.
- Bounds are contracts. `int_text` has `len(result) <= 17`. `iso` and `iso_parts` have length exactly 24 or 27 (the
  empty case is gone: every caller passes `|ms| <= 8.64e15`). Templates are bounded by their fixed size plus two int
  texts, and `card_error` by its longest message. `gen_text.py` writes and checks each bound.
- Template constants are written by straight-line byte writers that `m6_test/gen_text.py` generates from the template
  comments. `run_m6.py` runs it with `--check`. Each writer is one bounds guard, then byte stores: no per-call literal
  decode, no `cat`.
- State stays state. The stored card V words remain `[i64]` UTF-16 units (m11 format), so `bud_date` keeps the
  `[i64]` `put_iso`/`put_iso_prefix` used by `bud_card` and adds the byte writer for the date output.
- `card_error` is `[u8]`, and so are `bud_card::Judged.error` and `SetCard.error`.
  - m11 converts at the V-word emit. The error branch of `m11_set_card` takes the UTF-16 length from
    `bud_text::card_error_units(kind, lang)`, a constant per (kind, lang) generated next to `card_error`, so there is
    no count loop over the bytes.
  - The two-site `emit_utf8` writes the units (one unit per lead byte, the high surrogate only for a 4-byte lead).
    The hand does the same from a `&'static str`.
- `set_card` keeps `copy(j.error)` on its reject path. Two alternatives were measured over 7 rounds and dropped:
  calling `card_error` there (with no `Judged.error`), and a `check_card` split. Both outlined `card_error` and cost
  the success path of the only caller (m11 lane C) +0.9 % instructions vs base, with non-overlapping distributions.
  A plain move of `j.error` is not legal (`array_alias`: an array value comes from `alloc()`, `copy()` or a call).
- Complexity per flow:
  - O(output): limit, amount, refusal, continue and card texts.
  - O(1) plus the key bytes: `refusal_wire`.
  - O(digits): int text.
  - O(1): ISO, `unit_of`, `count_class`, `card_error_units`.
  - O(n) without allocation: length checks.

### P27.3 Oracle and gates (compiler rs first, then py)

What `run_m6.py` checks, besides the 300 generated cases:
- N fixture replay. Each helper step of fixture group N is turned into m6 words (`replay_words`): the language word,
  safe ints, the unlimited word, and `card_error_kind`, which projects the fixture's first validation failure onto
  the typed error code. It is then compared with the recorded output. `N10/r1` (`runStarted`) is excluded and listed
  in the report, because it needs stateful budget execution outside M6.
- Q8 helper replay. The standalone helper steps of 40 Q8 scenarios from `q_gen` are replayed the same way. Stateful
  compatibility calls interleaved in Q8 are skipped by name (`HELPER_ENTRIES`).
- UTF-16 to UTF-8 at the boundary. `node_ref.mjs` returns each oracle text both as UTF-8 bytes (`w`, compared with
  Pruv) and as UTF-16 units (`u`, used for the unit counts). The conversion happens once, in the oracle, and is
  compared exactly. The card-error oracle runs the real `RequestBudgets.setCard` with `budgetUnitOf()` defaults.
- `t_unit` (m6 root, harness op `unit`) transports `bud_num::unit_of` / `unit_default` so `budgetUnitOf` is
  compared too.
- Fixture group K (`setCard`: trim, UTF-16 length boundaries, lone surrogates, stored fields) is stateful, so m6 does
  not replay it. Its `setCard` calls are items of the m11 hand diff (`run_m11.py`, label `K`), which compares every
  item against the hand: 0 differ. Its raw numbers also feed the m6 number inputs.
- The perf checksums (P27.4, P27.5) are guards that each lane computed the same thing. They read the length and the
  parity of the first, middle and last byte. Exactness is the job of the gates above, not of the checksums.
  Allocations per call are not counted; peak RSS is reported instead.

### P27.5 Given back: `p_int` (compiler-owned, queued) and the PERF_HEADROOM rows

Why `p_int` is slower:
- Base `int_text -> [i64]` met `docs/SMALL_RESULT_SPEC.md` eligibility (rule 1: result `[i64]`, `ensures
  len(result) <= 17`). So `p_int` called `int_text__pruv_small(&mut [i64; 17], x)` with no heap.
- `int_text -> [u8]` fails rule 1 and allocates on every call.
- In the m6 grid that is still below the hand (which allocates a `Vec<u8>`): 0.83-0.86x.
- In the PERF_HEADROOM compiler root it is above hand, because there the best hand is the stack variant `p_int_u`.

PERF_HEADROOM compiler root (which also runs `perf_extra.pruv`), 7 alternating rounds, base a9664a9 vs new. Values
are ns per call, min..max (median):

| op n | base py | base rs | new py | new rs | best hand (new runs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| p_int 100 | 13.75..14.17 (13.75) | 13.75..37.08 (14.16) | 25.42..70.41 (27.92) | 24.58..70.00 (30.00) | 12.9 |
| p_int 500 | 13.67..13.92 (13.67) | 13.58..15.00 (13.67) | 24.00..26.00 (24.08) | 24.08..29.50 (26.17) | 12.7 |
| p_int 1000 | 13.67..37.00 (14.58) | 13.58..37.17 (13.75) | 23.96..30.42 (26.62) | 24.42..35.17 (25.25) | 12.8 |

The other PERF_HEADROOM rows did not get worse (checksums equal between base and new, except p_ref):
- p_amt is faster on every cell (median 28.4..32.5 -> 22.6..25.8 ns). It is non-overlapping better on 4 of 6 cells.
- p_ref is faster on every cell (ratio to hand 1.31..1.46 -> 0.64..0.77). It is non-overlapping better on 5 of 6
  cells. Its checksum moves from 9800/49000/98000 to 22800/114000/228000 (bytes vs units). The PERF_HEADROOM best
  hand for p_ref still writes UTF-16 units (checksum 9800). The like-for-like comparison is the m6 grid, whose hand
  writes UTF-8 (22800): new is 0.62-0.68x there.
- p_iso and p_wr overlap base on every cell.

The fix needs both codegens, and TIDY 4.13 owns them, so it is not made here. Exact change, proposed as a TIDY row:
- SMALL_RESULT_SPEC rule 1 accepts `[u8]` results, with plain `u8` storage for both the result and the local `o`.
- The caller buffer is `[u8; K]`, with K taken from the same `ensures len(result) <= K` (K <= 64).
- Rules 2-5 and the call-site rules are unchanged.

Expected effect: p_int returns to the base 13-15 ns. The other short byte texts (`no_limit`, `reason_name`,
`counter_name`, ISO) also come off the heap wherever their callers only read them.

Done (P27.5 package, base 9248379 = P27 + P13i2a). Both codegens accept `[u8]` in rule 1 with a `[u8; K]` caller
buffer (`[0u8; K]`, `alloc` fill cast `as u8`); the 4096-byte cap counts `K` bytes for `u8`. Accept tests:
`tests/runtime/kd_m6_small_result_u8` and `tests/spec/r7_2_small_result_u8`. py and rs generated Rust is identical
on m6 and m11. m6 emits 6 small functions and two stack sites, `[u8; 17]` (`int_text` in the `p_int` loop) and
`[u8; 35]` (`amount_text` in `p_amount`); m11 has no stack site (its call sites are unchanged).

## Appendix PR1: proof reuse across roots (module proof records)

Problem: every bench root re-proved the shared library modules (bud_map, bud_store, bud_keys, ...), which are about
98% of a root's proof time (M10 py: 33.0 s of FnVerifier, root_m10 itself 0.69 s). The query cache (G4b-3) cannot hit
across roots: sort and symbol names carry program-wide indices, and a hit still pays the encoding.

Route: a per-module proof record behind `--module-cache DIR` (off by default; full rule docs/G4B_SPEC.md section 7.8,
SPEC.md proof cache section). The obligations are the same; only the run of a module's function verifiers is skipped
when the same inputs were already proved with no error. True modular proof with exported interface facts was
rejected: it changes what a module's proof may assume.

Key inputs: compiler identity (py: `pruvc/*.py`, `pruvc/data/*`, `stdlib/*`; rs: the running executable on Linux, a build-time hash of all compiler inputs elsewhere), full Z3
version, explicit mode, `--infer`, the G9 metadata restricted to the closure, the module, and for each module of its
reference closure the file digest and rdigest (the digest of what its names resolved to). Edges come from resolved
identities before expansion, so callees of callees, types, constructors and template sources are all in the closure.
Not in the key (does not enter a module's proof): caller contracts, `--trust-callers`, `--proven-entries`,
`--foreign-checks`, `--budget`, rust-extern bodies, whole-program index order (renaming only).

Adversarial review of the design (Codex gpt-6.2-astra), fixed before the gates: swapped package aliases kept the key
(fixed: rdigest); `pruvc/data/builtin_types.json` was outside the py identity (fixed); py identity hashed after the
checker passes (now hashed at the start of `main`).

Gates (both compilers): `tests/g4b/check_module_cache.py` 50/50 (56/56 after the audit fixes); full py `run_all --compare-rows` 3190/3190, 0
missing/extra/failed; rs `g4b_proof` and `g4b_frontend` rows; `cargo test --release`; diff_rust fuzz 20 all same;
M7 Q 113 exact and M10 Q 78 exact on rs and `--py`; M4 run rc 0 on both; L3 lib tests (json a0..a5, mcp, qwen,
supervisor a0..a3) all pass; spec_trace 380/380. Generated `.rs` of the ten bench roots is byte-identical between
HEAD, the new compiler without the flag and with the flag, on both compilers (40 comparisons).

Timing, wall seconds, compile with verify of the ten bench roots in order (m3, keys, admit, m4, m6, m7, m8, m9, m10,
m11); the new compiler runs them as one chain sharing one cache directory ("cold": empty at the start), "warm" is the
same chain again. Noisy machine (load about 12); py rows are the second of two runs.

| compiler | f5d9891 (pre-P13j2a) | HEAD 24d28ac | PR1 cold chain | PR1 warm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| rs | 63.91 | 110.59 | 38.42 | 1.67 |
| py | 129.80 | 222.91 | 84.29 | 11.36 |
| rs, after audit fixes | | | 43.84 | 1.80 |
| py, after audit fixes | | | 100.66 | 11.64 |

Per root, rs: f5 1.47 3.03 7.33 7.44 2.80 8.04 7.49 7.47 9.27 9.56; HEAD 0.55 4.24 13.07 12.37 2.80 15.38 14.84
13.11 18.39 15.84; cold 0.53 3.10 9.07 1.49 2.77 3.10 1.02 0.38 2.57 14.39. py: f5 0.72 3.54 17.21 16.14 4.26 16.91
15.42 15.32 20.06 20.22; HEAD 0.70 3.49 31.67 28.88 3.70 32.27 27.64 29.00 33.72 31.84; cold 0.72 3.24 27.55 2.39
3.59 7.31 2.53 1.91 3.44 31.61.

Reading: the chain total is under f5d9891 on both compilers. The first root that loads the heavy shared modules
(admit) still pays their full proof, and m11 owns its own modules (py 31.6 vs f5 20.2, rs 14.4 vs f5 9.6), so a single
root compiled with an empty cache costs what HEAD costs; the P13j2a proof-time growth itself is not reduced, only paid
once per input set.

Code audit (Codex gpt-6.2-astra, one round, verdict must-fix). Must-fix, all fixed in the same commit: (1) Rust edges
missed identities nested in a type key string (`option<crate::types::Flag>`), so a module named only as a generic
argument was outside the closure and a changed enum reused the stale record; the Python resolver already recursed into
type arguments. Fixed by splitting quoted strings on the type-key separators; the new `nested` case fails on the old
code and passes now. (2) A Rust `ModulePlan` passed through `VerifyOptions` to a second program with the same function
count used the first program's keys (library API only); a plan is now used once. (3) Rust hashed the executable late,
so a binary replaced after start could label the old verifier's results; it is now hashed first in `main`, and the
cache is off if the file was modified after start or changed while hashed. (4) Python ignored an unreadable source
directory and hashed a partial set; any OS error now turns the cache off. Should-fix taken: bounded record reads and
exclusive temporary files on both compilers. Deferred (performance only): the Rust rdigest is the `Debug` text of
resolved items, which carries program-wide indices and file tags, so the same module loaded by two roots can get two
keys (a miss, never a wrong hit); the measured roots still reuse across the chain. Note documented in G4B 7.8 rule 6:
under `--infer` a hit skips inference attempts, so the guarantee is proof validity, not identical diagnostics.
Re-check (Codex gpt-6.2-astra, the second and last audit round, verdict must-fix): (1), (4), bounded reads and
exclusive temporaries confirmed fixed, and no new wrong-accept path in the fix diff. Two remained, fixed after the
re-check and not audited again: the Rust plan was consumed only when records were on, so a call with a trace or report
left it for a later program (now consumed whenever it is passed); off Linux the executable was re-opened by path, which
can be replaced by an older-mtime binary before the first stat (now a build-time identity, `build.rs`, see G4B 7.8 rule
2; verified that adding a file under `crates/` changes the id and removing it restores it). Python now uses `os.stat`
in the identity walk so a stat error also turns the cache off. Gates after these fixes: `check_module_cache.py` 56/56,
rs `g4b_proof` 2/2, `cargo test --release`, M10 rs output byte-identical without the flag, cold and warm (11 records,
warm 0.08 s).

## Appendix P13g: the M8 CURRENT lookup inlined; the rest of the hand16 gap, by line

Base main 04b43b6. Files: `bench/l3/budget/m8_test/root_m8.pruv` only. No compiler change, no verifier change. Notes,
variants and scripts in `work/p13g` (not committed).

### P13g.1 What blocked inlining

At base `bud_map::find_w` already gets `#[inline(always)]`. The helper that stayed out of line on the hot path was
`cur_off` (root_m8): four textual call sites (charge, noteFailure, noteTool, and the one inside `load_cv`), inclusive
size 562 lines (own body 47 plus the inlined `find_w` chain, 415), so `incl * (sites - 1)` = 1,686 exceeded
`INLINE_BUDGET` (1,500) and the policy left it `#[inline]`; rustc did not inline it. The policy itself is right here (more copies of a large body grow `__text`); the
shape was the cause, so the fix is in the source:

- The code 1 and code 2 arms of `t_call` share one `cur_off` site. The length test for each code runs before the
  lookup, as at base: a bad length answers 2 with `st` and `cv` unchanged (`fx[0..2]` is already written, as at base).
- `load_cv` (which re-ran `cur_off` on the out-of-range fallback, so CURRENT ran twice there) is removed; both
  fallbacks call `load_cv_at` with the offset already found.
- `cur_off` now has two sites (code 1/2, code 3), 562 * 1 fits the budget, and the policy makes it `#[inline(always)]` on both compilers; the
  generated Rust from pruvc and pruvc-rs is byte-identical.

## Appendix P28: resident clear / record / stop auto-continuation (M12)

Base main cccf833. Files: `bench/l3/budget/bud_auto.pruv` (new), `bench/l3/budget/bud_map.pruv` (`splice_blob`
added, nothing else changed), `bench/l3/budget/m12_test/` (new: `root.pruv`, `run_m12.py`, `harness.rs`, `hand.rs`,
`perf_ts.mjs`), `bench/l3/budget/ABI.md` (M12 section). No compiler change. Notes and logs in `work/p28` (not
committed).

### P28.1 What is ported

`clearAutoContinue`, `recordAutoContinue` and `stopAutoContinue` of the Node budget class (B:519-553,
REQUEST_BUDGET_SPEC 4.8), on the resident store (`bud_store` / `bud_map` / `bud_world`). Every decision is in Pruv
(`bud_auto::clear`, `record`, `stop`); the Rust host decodes the call, runs the counted effects (`findSession`, `save`,
`changed`) in the order Pruv writes them, and grows `st` on status 1. bootRestore / forget / dispose are P29.

- Lookup: `session_entry` resolves a packed session key with `bud_map::find_w`. `find_pair` walks the budget object's
  top-level pairs, keeps the last match and counts the matches (JS objects cannot hold duplicate keys; the store can,
  and the last wins as in `JSON.parse`). A delete (clear, falsy record) removes every matching pair (`drop_all`, one
  `edit` per pair, at most the counted number), so no earlier duplicate reappears.
- Records are stored in the shared V-word value format of the store (no new record layout, no per-unit text: strings
  are packed keys / V strings as everywhere else in the store). Admitted record packets arrive as JB bytes (`[u8]`) and
  are encoded once by `put_jv`.
- Edits go through one path, `edit`: the new blob length is computed, room is made once (`make_room` with reserve
  `m + m/2`, clamped to `m` when only `m` fits the free arena, so no Grow is raised while the edit fits) when the blob
  slot is too small, `bud_map::splice_blob` replaces `[begin, end)` with the new words, and the
  object's pair count is adjusted by -1 / 0 / +1.
- `splice_blob` (`ensures kept(st, old(st))`): in-slot edits move the tail backward when the blob grows and forward
  when it shrinks (no overlap clobber); a relocation copies the prefix to the arena top, writes the new words and the
  moved tail, then updates the entry's offset / capacity / length words, the arena top (word 10) and the live word (14).
  Statuses as the store: 0 ok, 2 invalid (bad entry, range or capacity). A relocation whose destination equals the
  old offset (an empty slot at the arena top) still updates capacity and the arena top.
- stop: owner = `findSession(pointed ? ref.sessionId : sessionId)` with the counted `findSession` calls (1 without a
  ref, 2 with one, also for stale refs); a found non-open pointed budget blocks the fallback (15.1 #23); a matching
  record with a truthy `stopped` returns without save; `stopped = true` overwrites in place or is appended; a
  synthetic record (key order `sessionId, userTurnId, count, stopped`) only when there is no record, the card is
  `working` and `card.by.sessionId` matches; another session's record is never overwritten; the save names the owner.

### P28.2 Intent / bug / accident (work/p28/classify.md)

| # | behaviour | class | treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | clear deletes `autoContinue` only when truthy (a stored falsy value stays) | accident (the class only writes truthy values) | kept exactly; crafted case |
| A2 | clear / record do not save or emit changed (caller saves) | intended | kept |
| A3 | record: falsy deletes, truthy is stored as given | intended | kept (any truthy V) |
| A4 | record: no state restriction | intended (4.8) | kept |
| A5 | record: no count maximum | intended (15.1 #22) | kept |
| A6 | record stores the caller's object by reference | accident of JS aliasing, unobservable across the oracle boundary | excluded domain: Pruv stores a copy |
| A7 | reassigning keeps the key position; a new key is appended; delete + add moves it last | intended (persisted order) | kept, key order compared |
| A8 | stop: `findSession` 1 or 2 calls, also for stale refs | intended | kept, counted |
| A9 | stop: a found non-open pointed budget blocks the fallback | intended (15.1 #23) | kept |
| A10 | stop: stale pointed ref falls back to the caller's budget | intended (4.8) | kept |
| A11 | stop: truthy `stopped` returns without save | intended | kept (truthiness) |
| A12 | stop: `stopped = true` in place or appended | intended | kept |
| A13 | stop: synthetic record conditions and key order | intended | kept |
| A14 | stop never overwrites another session's record | intended | kept |
| A15 | stop saves the owner, then changed | intended | kept |
| A16 | stop with a non-object truthy record is a no-op | accident, outside the typed domain | kept (falls out of the V walk) |

No bugs found. Only intended behaviour plus the two kept accidents (A1, A16) is compared with the oracle; A6 is
excluded.

### P28.3 Complexity, by flow

W = words of the budget blob, K = top-level pairs, T = nodes of the top-level values (strings are skipped in O(1) by
their length header), P = admitted packet bytes, R = record words.

| flow | bound | dominant step |
|---|---|---|
| clear | O(1) expected lookup + O(K + T) `find_pair` + O(W - end) tail move | the tail after `autoContinue` |
| record | O(P) encode + O(K + T) + O(W) splice (tail move, or relocation amortized by the 1.5x reserve, clamped to the exact size when only that fits) | encoding and tail |
| stop, flip in place | 1-2 lookups + O(K + T) + O(R) record field walk | `find_pair` (flat in text size) |
| stop, synthetic | 1-2 lookups + O(K + T) + O(\|sid\|) record + append | flat in text size |

Perf agrees: T and S are flat across sizes 100..10000 (119-123 / 179-191 ns), R and C grow with the text that is
encoded or moved, at or below hand's slope.

### P28.5 Hand Rust lane

`m12_test/hand.rs`: the same operations on a `HashMap` of sessions with `Vec<i64>` budgets in the same V words
(`pair()` walks the top-level pairs and keeps the last match, as `find_pair`); clear is `Vec::drain` of the pair plus
the count, record and stop splice or append in place. Same effects and output words (hdiff identical). The perf
harness loads both lanes from the same input before each batch, preallocates capacity the same way, and times only the
operation.

## Appendix P29: bootRestore / forgetSession / dispose and the lifecycle V-word integration (M12)

Base main 6c51b31. Files: `bench/l3/budget/bud_cleanup.pruv`, `bud_vlife.pruv`, `bud_vwords.pruv`, `bud_effect.pruv`
(new); `bench/l3/budget/m12_test/` (`root.pruv`, `harness.rs`, `run_m12.py`, `hand.rs` changed; `m12_facts.rs`,
`hand_life.rs`, `perf_life.rs` new). No shared module (bud_map, bud_store, bud_world, bud_auto, bud_card, bud_clock,
bud_charge, lib) and no compiler change. Notes and logs in `work/p29` (not committed).

### P29.1 What is ported

`bootRestore`, `forgetSession` and `dispose` of the Node budget class (B:555-572, REQUEST_BUDGET_SPEC 4.9), plus the
V-word integration of `attach`, `charge`, `halt`, `runStarted` / `runWaiting` / `runEnded` and the timer `FIRE` on the
M12 resident store, so the whole Q7 script runs (P28 cut Q7 at the first of these operations). Every decision is in
Pruv; the Rust host decodes the call, runs the effects in the order Pruv writes them, keeps virtual time and the timer
scheduler, answers the trusted facts (`unit`, `uuid`, `runningDelegationIds`) and grows a store on Grow.

- State: sessions are root 0 of one shared store; each budget instance owns a `World` store with clocks in root 1
  (keyed by budget id, owner session id as a framed blob, runs as children) and toolSeen in root 2. The host scheduler
  is a `BTreeMap` on `(due, seq)`; Pruv names a timer by (instance, budget id) and never sees the host token.
- Entries (`root.pruv`): `m12_life(inout st, inout clocks, op, rf, sid, arg, now)` for ops 1-10 and `m12_fire` for
  the timer callback. The reply is one framed `[i64]`: records `[code, payload_len, delay, effective, payload...]`
  for effects 1-16 (findSession, now, save, changed, unit, uuid, runningDelegationIds, cancelRecovery, stopMain,
  stopDelegation, stopAttachedTurns, timer.set, timer.clear, timerForget, holdQueued, announce) and a last record
  code 0 carrying the status, a session-grow flag and the result V (`bud_effect.pruv`).
- `bud_cleanup.pruv`: `boot_restore` drops the clock (timer.clear only for an armed timer) and splices `activeSince`
  out of the budget, no save; `forget_session` walks root 1 in insertion order and drops every clock whose owner blob
  equals the argument (`owner_matches`: one extension lookup, length and first-word reject, then `eq_range`);
  `dispose` emits timer.clear for armed timers in insertion order, then clears roots 1 and 2. A drop reclaims the
  clock with its runs.
- `bud_vlife.pruv` reads the V budget into the existing `bud_charge` / `bud_clock` views and writes the changed fields
  back in their stored key order; `bud_vwords.pruv` holds the V property, date and packed-key helpers.
- Grow atomicity: before the first write to either store, each entry plans room in both (`make_room`, `blob_fits`,
  `reserve_budget`; for halt the bound includes the next `runningDelegationIds` reply, read by a non-consuming peek
  `running_ids_words`). A Grow reply has an empty result and no effects and nothing has been written, so the host runs
  every op in place (no store clone) and on Grow rewinds the fact stream, grows the named store and retries; a debug
  assertion checks the empty Grow reply.

### P29.2 Intent / bug / accident (work/p29/classify.md)

| # | behaviour | class | treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | bootRestore of a session without a budget returns without effects | intended | kept, oracle-compared |
| C2 | bootRestore drops the clock (timer.clear of a truthy timer) and deletes `activeSince`, no save / changed | intended (D8, 15.1 #24) | kept, oracle-compared |
| C3 | bootRestore keeps used / state / halt / card / autoContinue and the key order | intended | kept, final sessions compared |
| C4 | forgetSession drops every clock owned by the argument in insertion order; unknown sid is a no-op | intended | kept, timer.clear order and final clocks compared |
| C5 | forgetSession / dispose leave the persisted `activeSince` | intended (15.1 #25) | kept |
| C6 | dispose clears truthy timers in clock insertion order (not due order), then clocks, then toolSeen; no settle | intended | kept, oracle-compared |
| C7 | cleanup is per instance; sessions are shared | intended | kept, oracle-compared |
| C8 | timer tokens / sequence numbers are global across instances | accident of the oracle scheduler | host-owned handle; the judge maps tokens 1:1 by first appearance |
| C9 | a delay > 2147483647 or < 1 runs after 1 ms (Node TimeoutOverflow) | accident of Node, kept | kept (bud_clock effective-delay rule); < 1 unreachable |
| C10 | FIRE re-arms on `runs.size > 0`, not on the consuming predicate | accident (15.1 #11), kept | kept: bud_clock FIRE checks the run count as Node does (bud_clock.pruv:323) |
| C11 | runWaiting / runEnded skip the owner check, SETTLE checks it | accident (15.1 #10) | excluded domain, unreachable |
| C12 | halt's stopDelegation keeps duplicates of the running-id answer, list order | intended | kept, oracle-compared |
| C13 | several `now()` reads in one call (halt: settle + at) | accident (15.1 #28) | one now value per call (KD-1); a `now` effect is still emitted at each Node read so counts and order match |
| C14 | a timer ref surviving its disposed instance | not reachable (every drop / dispose clears the timer first) | no row |
| C15 | runStarted on a closed current budget creates a clock | 15.1 #8 | kept |
| C16 | FIRE passes the ref object captured at arm time, so extra ref properties (e.g. `tag`) reach runningDelegationIds / stopAttachedTurns | accident of JS object capture | excluded domain: a ref is `{sessionId, budgetId}`; Pruv rebuilds it from the two ids |
| C17 | a session whose `budget` property is present but `undefined` keeps the key | not representable (sessions are persisted JSON) | no row |

No bugs in the oracle's intended behaviour. Intended behaviour and the kept accidents C9 / C10 / C15 are compared with
the oracle; C8 is normalised by the judge, C11 / C16 are known differences outside the reachable domain, C13 is kept
by count and order. Port bugs found by the audit are in P29.8.

### P29.3 Complexity, by flow

W = words of the session's budget blob, K / T = its top-level pairs / value nodes, C = clocks in the instance, R = runs
of a clock, G = toolSeen entries, I = running-id answer words.

| flow | bound | dominant step |
|---|---|---|
| bootRestore | O(1) expected lookup + O(K + T) property scan + O(W) splice + O(R) clock drop | the splice tail |
| forgetSession | O(C) walk + O(\|sid\|) compare per clock passing the length / first-word reject + O(R) per drop | the walk |
| dispose | O(C) walk for timer effects + O(C + R + G) clear | two walks of root 1 |
| attach | O(W) budget build + O(R) old clock drop | V assembly (D19) |
| charge, not halting | O(K + T) view + O(W) rewrite | V reassembly (D20) |
| halt | O(W + I) | the stop list |
| runStarted / runWaiting / runEnded, FIRE | O(1) clock lookup + O(K + T + W) budget rewrite | V reassembly (D21) |

Perf agrees: F and D grow linearly in C (10 / 50 / 100 clocks: 1.15 / 4.74 / 9.53 us and 1.64 / 7.34 / 14.63 us) with
a smaller slope than hand; O grows linearly in C (3.3 / 34.3 / 241.6 us at 100 / 1000 / 5000; the last step is
cache-bound in both lanes, hand 2.9 / 36.6 / 183.2); B, A, H and U are flat in the session count apart from cache
effects (B 1.8-3.6, A 6.3-8.8, H 4.1-5.9, U 5.0-8.8 us from 100 to 10000 sessions).

Compared per call: result, every effect with its arguments in order (timer tokens normalised by first appearance),
the session V at every session-carrying effect (`save`, `findSession` reply, `holdQueued`, FIRE / halt finds) against
the oracle's snapshot at the same point (observe mode only, outside the timed region; a copy of Q7-20261117-3 with r7's
saved state changed from halted to open now fails), a returned budget reference against the session as of that request, and after each step the final sessions (key order), clocks, toolSeen and the pending
timers. The cleanup checks also assert timer.clear order equals clock insertion order and that owner lookup removes
exactly the matching clocks. Grow atomicity was checked once with a debug-assertion build: forced session and clock
Grow on runStarted and a session Grow on FIRE before two long duplicate running ids leave both stores unchanged, and
the successful retry consumes the running-id reply exactly once. No shared module changed, so no consumer reruns.

### P29.5 Hand Rust lane

`m12_test/hand_life.rs`: sessions in a `HashMap` of ordered value maps (strings as `Vec<u16>`), clocks as a `Vec` of
structs (owner, runs, `since`, `armed`) in insertion order, the same virtual scheduler and the same facts. hdiff is
identical over all three corpora. `perf_life.rs` drives both lanes from the same prepared state; building, cloning
and encoding the inputs are outside the timed region; the call, effect handling and scheduler consumption (and any
Grow) are inside. The checksum covers every result, every effect in order and, after the timed region, every lane's final
sessions, clocks and armed timers (address and due time).

One review (Codex gpt-6.2-astra, ultra) over the whole P29 diff: 11 must-fix findings, no Grow-atomic violation (the
unwritten-reply path at the old B/bud_vlife.pruv:470 is unreachable), host and shared modules clean. 9 fixed in one
write step, 2 rejected; one re-check of the 9 fixes plus the perf deltas (below).
