Known gap left: two attaches on different sessions with the same uuid before either has a clock are not detected;
the check stays O(1) (current budget id and instance clock keys) instead of scanning sessions.

Perf effect of the fixes: P29.6 (A M +14%, B S / M +15-16%; B M stays in overlapping distributions, D23).

Re-check (same reviewer, once): 8 of the 9 fixes confirmed (rows 2-9). Row 1 was reported as not fixed, because the
non-find snapshot is read after the call and `scheduler.apply` (m12_test/harness.rs `observe_effects`), not at effect
time, and because the judge compares only `id` and `budget` of the session value, not the `sref` identity
(m12_test/run_m12.py `session_snapshot`). Resolution, decided in the main conversation with no further audit: the two
reads are equal by construction. The only non-find effects that carry a session (cancelRecovery 8, holdQueued 15,
save 3, announce 16) are emitted only by `halt` (B/bud_vlife.pruv:325, :341, :342, :344). The single session write
of that call, `write_reserved` (B/bud_vlife.pruv:324), comes before all of them. `halt` then returns, and its three
callers (:388, :504, :530) return its reply unchanged. The host's `apply` writes timers only, never sessions. So the
post-call read is the session as of each of those effects. A find (code 1) still uses the pre-call snapshot or the
core's recorded intermediate state. The mutated r7 repro is the proof that the content is now judged. `sref` identity
is not compared. The Pruv store is keyed by session id and has no reference identity, so this is out of domain. It is
recorded as a known gap, not a fix. Perf: no must-fix cell. B 100 / 1000 are +15.5% / +16.4% with equal allocations
and overlapping B 1000 distributions (D23). A 1000 is +14.3%, already within D19.

record / `[u8]` text rows already proposed (P13i2a, D14).

## Appendix P30: budget `raise` (bud_decide, M10b)

Base main 0fee851. Files: `bench/l3/budget/bud_decide.pruv` (new), `bench/l3/budget/m7_test/bud_facts.rs` (adds the
`unit` fact, setter and log), `bench/l3/budget/m10b_test/` (new: `root_m10b.pruv`, `driver_m10b.rs`, `hand_m10b.rs`,
`run_m10b.py`, `M10B_NOTES.md`). No shared module (bud_map, bud_store, bud_world, bud_halt, bud_auto, bud_cleanup,
bud_clock, lib) and no compiler change. Notes in `work/p30` (not committed). P31 reuses `unit_ok`, `scaled` and the
`refresh_raised` pattern (settle, refresh, text `activeSince` rewrite, nested halt) for extend / end.

### P30.1 What is ported

`raise(ref, size)` of the Node budget class (B:410-446). M10b is the M10 world plus op 13 (raise, flag = size code:
0 unlimited, 1 / 2 / 4 / 8). Every decision is in Pruv; the driver supplies time and the trusted `unit` answer
(`::bud_facts::unit`, `[0, t, d, c, r, ch]`, checked by `unit_ok`), runs timer effects and logs. The unit query is
synchronous at its reached position (P10H): the query log places `E unit` at the effect-word index Pruv passes.

- Order: missing or closed -> false; size 1 -> false (no query); unlimited -> set word 2, timerClear only if the clock
  is armed (field 16 cleared, since and `activeSince` kept), changed; numeric -> plan room, ask unit, per-key max of
  size x unit (checked <= 2^53-1 before any write), no change -> false; a raised time limit with a since-present clock
  on a non-unlimited budget -> settle then refresh, a text `activeSince` rewrite when the record kind changes, and a
  nested `bud_halt::halt` when refresh reports a time halt; changed last.
- Grow atomicity: room for the rewrite and the fixed part of a nested halt is planned before the unit query
  (`room_plan`, read-only) and applied only once the answer is valid and a refresh is needed, so a Grow retry is
  query-free and an invalid answer leaves the store unchanged. Status 2 / 3 paths write nothing; the nested-halt
  terminal path keeps settle and the raised limits (P30.8).

### P30.2 Intent / bug / accident (work/p30/classify.md)

| # | behaviour | class | treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | missing budget or closed -> false, no unit query, no changed | intent | oracle-compared |
| R2 | 'unlimited' on an unlimited budget -> false, nothing else | intent | oracle-compared |
| R3 | 'unlimited' sets the flag, timerClear only if armed, keeps since / `activeSince` / limits / used, changed, true | intent | oracle-compared |
| R4 | size 1 -> false without asking unit | intent | oracle-compared |
| R5 | per key limit = max(limit, size x unit[key]) | intent | oracle-compared |
| R6 | no key changed -> false (unit was asked, no changed) | intent | oracle-compared |
| R7 | time limit raised, clock has since, not unlimited -> settle then refresh (refresh may halt for time) | intent | oracle-compared |
| R8 | changed is the last effect, true | intent | oracle-compared |
| R9 | raise never resumes a halted budget; the max rewrite still applies | intent | oracle-compared |
| R10 | numeric raise on an unlimited budget still rewrites limits and returns true (15.1 #13) | accident, kept | oracle-compared (same output) |
| R11 | `budget.unlimited` truthiness: any truthy value counts in JS; word 2 is 1 only for `true` | accident | KD-P30-1, not generated |
| R12 | size x unit above 2^53-1 (JS rounds to a double) | accident (JS number) | KD-P30-2: status 2, nothing written |
| R13 | malformed unit answer or a value outside 0..2^53-1 | host fault | KD-P30-3: status 2, nothing written |
| R14 | size outside {1, 2, 4, 8, 'unlimited'} | excluded by the type | KD-P30-4: status 2 |
| R15 | settle when the clock owner session differs from the ref | never generated | `bud_clock` owner rule (as M9), not compared |

No oracle bugs. R1-R10 are compared with the Node oracle; R11-R14 are known differences judged by the spec.

### P30.3 Complexity, by flow

S / B = session / clock lookup (hash, probes, packed-key compare), O = owner-key compare, W = record words, D = stopped
delegation ids, I = their packed words. Unit frame and the five keys are fixed size.

| flow | time / extra space |
|---|---|
| R1, R4 | O(S) / O(1) |
| R2, R3 | O(S + B) / O(1), at most two effect words |
| R5, R6, R10 | O(S + B) / O(1), one fixed-size unit answer; R6 includes the read-only room plan |
| R7 | O(S + B + O) / O(1); a text rewrite adds O(W); a nested halt adds O(W + D + I) plus one lookup and owner compare |
| R8 | O(1) after the chosen path |
| R9 | as R5 / R6 or R7 |

A reservation may trigger the shared index rehash; a Grow retry copies the store through the shared growth path.
R7 uses the maintained active-run count and never scans runs. Checked by the perf run: every path is flat in D
(P30.5).

## Appendix P31: decide extend / end (bud_decide.pruv, M10b)

### P31.1 Semantics (B:449-477)

`decide(session, budgetId, choice, size)` returns `out = [6, code]`: 0 `{ok: true}`, 1 `not-found` (no session, no
budget or not the session's current id), 2 `not-halted`. Every decision is made in `bud_decide.pruv`; the host answers
two facts (`unit`, the P30 fact, and `releaseHeld` in the new `m10b_test/decide_facts.rs`) and runs effects. New
effect words: `[36]` save, `[38, reason (-1 = null, 0..4), wake (0 / 1)]` queueContinue, `[39]` dropHeld.

- extend (size 0 = unlimited, 1 / 2 / 4 / 8; an absent size is 1): unlimited sets word 2 with no unit query, otherwise
  limits[k] += size x unit[k] for the five keys (each sum checked <= 2^53-1 before any write); state open, halt
  deleted (the record is stored without its halt section), save, changed; when the budget has a clock, REFRESH
  without SETTLE (B:466): a timer set, or a nested `bud_halt` time halt when the time limit is still reached; then
  queueContinue(reason, no wake) when the halt had a reason (read in O(1) at the halt prefix the frame check proved), then `releaseHeld` asked synchronously at its position
  in the effect stream, and queueContinue(null, wake) when it answers 0 (nothing held).
- end: CLOSE('user-end') through the shared `bud_lifecycle::close_rec` (settle, state closed, ended = {user-end,
  now}, the clock dropped, the halt section kept), then dropHeld, save, changed.
- Grow atomicity: extend plans room for the stripped record, a since-text rewrite and, for a limited extend only
  (an unlimited budget is never armed, so it cannot re-halt for time), a nested halt (`bud_halt::halt_words`) before
  the unit query; end reserves the stored record's length before CLOSE (the closed
  record is never longer). A Grow writes nothing and asks nothing; status 2 / 3 paths write nothing except
  KD-P31-3. If a nested halt uses its slack word and the two queueContinue records no longer fit, the call returns
  the halt capacity status 6 (as P30's R8 fix).

### P31.2 Intent / bug / accident (work/p31/classify.md)

| # | behaviour | class | treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | absent session / budget or a non-current id -> not-found | intent | oracle-compared |
| X2 | current budget not halted -> not-halted | intent | oracle-compared |
| X3 | extend size 0 -> unlimited, no unit query | intent | oracle-compared |
| X4 | extend size s -> limits[k] += s x unit[k] | intent | oracle-compared |
| X5 | open, halt deleted, save, changed in that order | intent | oracle-compared |
| X6 | REFRESH without SETTLE: timer set or a nested time halt | intent | oracle-compared |
| X7 | queueContinue(reason, false) when the halt had a reason | intent | oracle-compared |
| X8 | releaseHeld at its place; false -> queueContinue(null, true) | intent | oracle-compared (position, session, budget id) |
| X9 | end: CLOSE('user-end'), halt kept, dropHeld, save, changed | intent | oracle-compared |
| X10 | size outside {0, 1, 2, 4, 8} multiplies whatever arrives | accident (excluded by the type) | KD-P31-1: status 2 before any write |
| X11 | limit + size x unit above 2^53-1 rounds silently | bug (JS number) | KD-P31-2: status 2 before any write |
| X12 | a releaseHeld answer outside {false, true} is coerced by truthiness | accident (host fault) | KD-P31-3: status 2 after the store; the host call already ran and cannot be undone. The same holds for an invalid `running_ids` answer inside a nested halt (as P30 raise) |
| X13 | writes before knowing room exists | host model | Grow before the unit query, nothing written |

X1-X9 are compared with the Node oracle; X10-X13 are checked by `check_decide_controls` (4 rejection paths, 2 Grow
retries, 1 invalid releaseHeld answer).

### P31.3 Complexity, by flow

S / B / O / W / D / I as P30.3.

| flow | time / extra space |
|---|---|
| X1, X2 | O(S) / O(1) |
| extend unlimited / numeric | O(S + B + W) / O(W): record frame check, room plan and one stripped-record copy; the halt reason is one word read; one fixed-size unit answer |
| extend with a clock | adds REFRESH O(1) or a nested halt O(W + D + I) plus one lookup and owner compare |
| end | O(S + B + W) / O(W): record copy, validation and the closed-record rewrite (W includes the kept halt's D ids) plus the clock drop O(clock runs) |
| releaseHeld / effects | O(1) words each |

Checked by the perf run (P31.5): extend and end grow linearly in D (the stored halt's stopped ids) with a lower slope
than hand.

## Appendix P31L: owned collection fields, Vec entry results, inout calls in expressions (both compilers)

### P31L.1 Rules (SPEC.md)

- R-6e-1 owned collection fields: non-generic structs and enum payloads may have `Vec<i64>`, `Vec<bool>` and
  `String` fields; other collection field types (HashMap, other element types, nested) and any collection field in
  a generic declaration stay `type/foreign_owned_type`. An owning initializer or replacement takes a call result or
  `move x`; a field read `r.f` is a borrowed view (passable to unmarked collection parameters and the catalog reads,
  never moved implicitly). Contracts and the verifier use the collection-local buffer model for `len(r.f)` and
  `r.f[i]`. Rust uses `::std::vec::Vec` / `::std::string::String` fields, the aggregate derives `Clone` without
  `Copy`, and moved initializers are stored without a clone. LLVM rejects such aggregates
  (`codegen/unsupported_type`, naming the aggregate).
- R-6e-2: `move p.f` only as a direct `take` argument of a call whose result is assigned back to the same field
  (`p.f = vec_push::<i64>(move p.f, 5);`); Rust passes `::std::mem::take(&mut p.f)`. Other field moves are
  `type/foreign_move`.
- R-6d-2 proved vector reads: in a verified build with `--foreign-checks requires|off`, `vec_get` is emitted as
  `get_unchecked` after its bounds precondition is proved, only when the program declares no user `trusted rust fn`
  (audit A1); a field operand is read in place.
- R-6f-1: an explicit-mode root `pub` non-generic function may return `Vec<i64>` / `Vec<bool>` as an ordinary
  Rust host entry (`pub fn`, `pub(crate) fn` under `raw_entries`); no C ABI (LLVM and `--rust-bindings` give `codegen/unsupported_type`). Other collection results
  stay `type/entry_signature`.
- R-6g-1: a user call with an `inout` argument may occur at any depth of one simple statement (or an
  `if` / `while` / `match` condition or scrutinee) when (1) the inout array is not mentioned elsewhere in the
  statement, (2) the call runs exactly once (not in a `while` condition, a right operand of `&&` / `||` or an
  if-expression branch), (3) the statement is not an element or field assignment, (4) no call with an effect other
  than `alloc` runs before it. Each violation is `type/inout_context` with its reason (message and fix). R-6g-1 replaces the
  docs/G5_SPEC.md §2.1 statement-boundary rule. The three forms of `g5_context_binary`, `g5_context_call_arg`
  and `g5_context_if_cond` are now accepted: `g5_context_if_cond` is removed, and the other two stay in
  must_reject (and tests/g5/fixtures.json `proof_reject`) as `verify/overflow` regressions, since their bodies still overflow.
  The rejected positions are covered by the new `tests/spec/r6g_1_*` rows.

### P31L.2 Small example (work copy, not a repository file)

Source: a struct `Rec { id: i64, data: Vec<i64> }`, `make(take v) -> Rec { Rec { id: 7, data: move v } }`, and
`sum_rec(r: Rec)` summing `vec_get::<i64>(r.data, i)` under `requires len(r.data) <= 1000` and an element range.
Generated Rust (`--trust-callers`, Python and Rust compilers byte-identical) against hand Rust:

| hand Rust | generated |
|---|---|
| `pub struct Rec { pub id: i64, pub data: Vec<i64> }` | `pub struct Rec { pub id: i64, pub data: ::std::vec::Vec<i64> }` (`#[derive(Clone, Debug)]`) |
| `Rec { id: 7, data: v }` | `return (Rec { id: 7i64, data: v });` (move, no clone) |
| `fn sum_rec(r: &Rec) -> i64` | `fn sum_rec__pruv_body(r: &Rec) -> i64` + wrapper `sum_rec(r: &Rec)` calling it (`#[inline(always)]`) |
| `while i < r.data.len() as i64` | `while (i < (r.data.len() as i64))` |
| `s = s + unsafe { *r.data.get_unchecked(i as usize) }` | `s = (s + (unsafe { *(r.data).get_unchecked((i) as usize) }));` (no bounds check) |

Perf (rustc -O, codegen-units=1, 1000 elements, 2,000,000 calls, 5 runs): hand 52.7-53.2 ns/call, generated
`--trust-callers` 52.7-53.1 ns/call (0.99-1.00x; one warm-up run 62.65 excluded). The default build adds the
public-entry runtime `requires` check (an O(n) `forall`, about 557 ns/call): that is the existing SPEC public-entry
behaviour, outside this row's gate.

## Appendix P31S: struct collections and typed resident entry state (both compilers)

### P31S.1 Rules (SPEC.md)

- R-6e-3 collections of owned aggregates: `Vec<S>` and `HashMap<i64, S>` for a non-generic, non-recursive struct
  `S` whose fields are scalars, plain value types or R-6e-1 owned fields. A state struct may hold such fields;
  nesting stops there (an owned aggregate may not hold them, a state struct is not a payload), and a zero-sized
  struct is not an element (audit #1), all `type/foreign_owned_type`. `vec_push::<S>` / `map_insert::<i64, S>`
  move the element in (constructor, call result or `move y`, else `type/foreign_move`). With owned fields,
  `vec_get::<S>(v, i)` is only a field-access receiver (`v[i as usize].f` or `get_unchecked` under R-6d-2) and
  `map_get::<i64, S>` only a `match` scrutinee binding a borrowed view (`match m.get(&k)`).
- R-6e-4 in-place map element update: `map_get_mut::<K, V>(inout P, k)` only as a direct `match` scrutinee; the
  `Some(r)` arm may read and assign fields of `r`, use R-6e-2 on `r.f` and pass `inout r`, but may not return,
  reassign, move or store `r`, mention the root of `P` (`type/recursive_borrow`) or contain `return` / `break` /
  `continue`. Rust emits one `match P.get_mut(&k)`; the verifier writes the final `r` back at arm exit. Under the
  R-6d-2 condition the R-6e-2 push becomes `P.f.push(x);` without `mem::take`.
- R-6f-2 typed resident state entries: the first parameter of an explicit-mode root `pub` entry may be
  `inout st: S` (non-generic struct, including a state struct), emitted as `pub fn e(st: &mut S, ...)` or
  `pub(crate) fn` under `raw_entries` where the host keeps a `PruvStore<S>`. `raw_entries` "c",
  `--rust-bindings` and LLVM reject it with `codegen/unsupported_type` naming the entry.
- R-6g-2 struct inout parameters: `inout x: S` for a non-generic struct, `x: &mut S`; field assignment (nested),
  R-6e-2 on `x.f`, `map_get_mut` on `x.f` and forwarding `inout x` are allowed; whole reassignment is
  `type/immutable`, a generic struct `type/inout_type`, `old(x)` `type/old_argument`. The caller knows only the
  callee's `ensures` about the argument after the call.
- Older SPEC lines (internal-only collection signatures, `inout` types, host-entry limits, unsupported list) now
  name the R-6f-2 / R-6g-2 exceptions (audit #17).

New tests: `tests/spec/r6e_3_{vec_records,map_read,bare_get,nested_payload,zero_sized}`,
`r6e_4_{touch,updated_value,stale_value,not_scrutinee,return_in_arm,root_in_arm}`,
`r6f_2_{state_entry,llvm_entry}`, `r6g_2_{struct_inout,whole_assign,generic}`; `r6e_2_replace_field.json` updated.

### P31S.2 Small example (work copy, not a repository file)

Source `tests/spec/r6e_4_touch.pruv`: `St { count: i64, recs: HashMap<i64, Record> }`,
`Record { hits: i64, log: Vec<i64> }`, entry `touch(inout st: St, k, x)` looks up `k` with `map_get_mut`, adds
`x` to `hits` and pushes `x` onto `log`. Generated Rust (default build; Python and Rust compilers byte-identical)
against hand Rust:

| hand Rust | generated |
|---|---|
| `pub struct St { pub count: i64, pub recs: HashMap<i64, Record> }` | same fields, `::std::collections::HashMap<i64, Record>` (`#[derive(Clone, Debug)]`) |
| `pub fn touch(st: &mut St, k: i64, x: i64) -> i64` | `touch__pruv_body(st: &mut St, ...)` + wrapper `pub fn touch(st: &mut St, ...)` with the entry `requires` check |
| `match st.recs.get_mut(&k)` | `match st.recs.get_mut(&k)` (one lookup) |
| `r.hits = r.hits + x;` | `r.hits = (r.hits + x);` |
| `r.log.push(x);` | `r.log.push(x);` (no `mem::take`, no clone) |
| `(r.log.len() as i64) < 1000000` | `((r.log.len() as i64) < 1000000i64)` |

No clone, no bounds check, no re-encoding per call (the state stays a `&mut St`). Perf (rustc -O, 1000 records,
20,000,000 calls, 15 alternating rounds): hand median 123.05 ms, generated 123.14 ms, ratio 1.001 (per-round
0.84-1.01), same checksum.

## Appendix P31T: second attempt stopped on a language gap (no budget change)

### P31T.1 What the typed session record needs

The hand lanes the debt cells are measured against keep the resident state as text-keyed maps of typed structs:
`m10b_test/hand_m10b.rs:181-182` (`sessions: HashMap<String, Budget>`, `clocks: HashMap<String, Clock>`),
`:119` (`Halt { stopped: Vec<String> }`), `:127` (`Clock { runs: HashMap<String, bool> }`) and `m12_test/hand_life.rs:188, 343`
(`HashMap<Text, ..>` with `Text = Vec<u16>`). D14 and D25 name the cause as the packed-key lookup (hash and
compare the packed session key in `bud_lifecycle::current_entry`, B/bud_lifecycle.pruv:192, then a second packed-key
lookup in `bud_clock::clock_of`, B/bud_clock.pruv:120) against hand's one `HashMap<String>` lookup.

### P31T.2 Gap (both compilers, same diagnostics)

Repros in `work/p31t/` (not repository files), each rejected by pruvc-rs (main 78c5ddb build) and pruvc with the same
code and line:

| repro | source | result | SPEC line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gap_str_key.pruv` | `pub struct St { sessions: HashMap<String, Budget> }` + `match map_get_mut::<String, Budget>(inout st.sessions, sid)` | `type/foreign_owned_type` line 3: "String cannot be a HashMap key: only i64, bool and Element type parameters can" | SPEC.md:379 (`K` is `i64` or `bool`), SPEC.md:469 (R-6e-3 `HashMap<i64, S>` only), SPEC.md:316 (`Element` is `i64` or `bool`) |
| `gap_map_field.pruv` | `pub struct Clock { active: i64, runs: HashMap<i64, bool> }` held in `HashMap<i64, Clock>` | `type/foreign_owned_type` line 3: "field runs cannot have the collection type HashMap<i64, bool>" | SPEC.md:442-444 (R-6e-1: only `Vec<i64>`, `Vec<bool>`, `String` fields) |
| `gap_vec_string.pruv` | `pub struct Halt { reason: i64, stopped: Vec<String> }` | `type/foreign_owned_type` line 1: "a Vec element cannot be the collection type String" | SPEC.md:379-380 (collections cannot be nested), SPEC.md:442-444 |

P31S listed the first one as not covered (Appendix P31S, "HashMap with non-i64 keys for aggregates"); the second
and third are the "nested aggregate collections" item there. `vec_at_mut` (in-place `Vec<S>` element update) is also
not covered, so a `Vec<Record>` indexed by a store slot cannot be updated in place either.

### P31T.3 Why no change was made

The only typed forms P31S allows key records by `i64`. Every way to reach one from a session or budget id text is a
workaround the brief rules out or that keeps the debt cause:

- keep `bud_map`'s packed-key index for the id and hold the body in `HashMap<i64, Record>`: two lookups per call
  (packed-key hash and compare, then an `i64` SipHash probe), more than today's D25 path, and the clock record
  still cannot hold its runs (`gap_map_field`) or the halt its stopped ids (`gap_vec_string`) without a flat side
  table;
- intern ids on the host into `i64` handles: the host would own session and budget identity and handle reclaim on
  delete / forgetSession, which are budget decisions (the rule: the host only does side effects);
- hash the id text in Pruv and chain colliding records: a hand-written hash table over `[i64]`, which is the current
  `bud_map` again.

The port itself (typed `bud_lifecycle` / `bud_halt` / `bud_clock` / `bud_charge` / `bud_decide` for M10b, about
2,300 source lines, plus the other consumers M4-M12 that share them) was not started, so D28 / D29 (shrink-in-place)
and D19-D24 (struct replies) were not started either. Q and perf were not rerun: no budget file changed, so every
consumer's Q and every debt cell stays as recorded in Appendix P29-P31 and §7.5.

### P31T.4 Proposed root row (P31K, before P31T)

Both compilers, SPEC.md, tests/: (1) aggregate maps keyed by text, `HashMap<String, S>` (and `HashMap<String, i64>`)
with a borrowed lookup key (`str` / `String` field view / `[u8]` slice) so one lookup hashes the caller's bytes without
an owned key copy, `map_get` / `map_get_mut` / `map_insert` / `map_remove` as in R-6e-3 / R-6e-4; (2) one level of
collection nesting inside an owned aggregate: `Vec<String>` and `HashMap<String, bool>` fields in a record held by a
state struct (`Halt.stopped`, `Clock.runs`); (3) `vec_at_mut` on `Vec<S>` with the R-6e-4 arm rules. Gate as P31S
(positive and negative tests in both, small example against hand Rust: one lookup, no clone, no bounds check). Then
P31T restarts with the M10b lane first (it owns D25, D26, D28, D29) and moves the shared modules for M4-M12 after it.

### P31T.5 Budget

About 20 minutes of the 2 hours, 0 of 24 delegations (the gap was found while reading the hand lanes and the two
repros took one compiler call each), 0 builds, no audit (no change to audit).

## Appendix P31T (attempt 3): stopped on disjoint root-field borrows (no budget change)

### P31T3.1 Rules used

Brief of 2026-11-20 (after P31K, main 4b075fd): M10b lane first (it owns D25, D26, D28, D29) with root `inout st: St`,
`sessions: HashMap<String, Budget>`, `clocks: HashMap<String, Clock>` shaped like `m10b_test/hand_m10b.rs:115-185`,
one lookup by borrowed key per record, in-place update through `map_get_mut` / `vec_at_mut`, struct replies with `Vec`
effects. Building a struct per call from a flat buffer and writing it back is forbidden; a new language gap stops the
step. The P31K rules in force: R-6e-4 (SPEC.md:481), R-6e-5 (text-keyed maps), R-6e-6 (one level of nesting), R-6e-7,
R-6f-1 (SPEC.md:580), R-6f-2 (root state entry), R-6g-2 (SPEC.md:662) and the inout argument rule (SPEC.md:621-625).

### P31T3.2 What the M10b transitions need

The numeric raise with a time-limit change settles the running interval and then re-arms the timer
(B/bud_decide.pruv:60, B/bud_clock.pruv:198): settle reads the clock's owner and interval start and adds to the
budget's used time; the re-arm reads the budget's new limit and settled used time and writes the clock's deadline and
re-halt flag. Decide extend / end apply the same transition. Hand Rust holds both records at once
(`sessions.get_mut(sid)` and `clocks.get_mut(bid)` on two fields of the same state). Two sequential single lookups do
not suffice: whichever record is looked up first is finished before the second is read, and mutating the clock first
breaks the paths that must leave the clock untouched (a bad `unit` answer, no matching budget).

### P31T3.3 Gap (both compilers, same diagnostics)

Repros in `work/p31t/` (not repository files), checked by this conversation with pruvc-rs (release build of 4b075fd)
and pruvc (`pruvc/pruvc.py --backend rust`):

| repro | source | result | SPEC line |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sibling_map_borrow.pruv` | in `refresh(inout st: St, sid: str, bid: str, now: i64)`, `match map_get_mut::<String, Budget>(inout st.sessions, sid) { Some(budget) => { match map_get_mut::<String, Clock>(inout st.clocks, bid) { Some(clock) => { budget.active_ms = ..clock.since_ms..; clock.armed = budget.active_ms < budget.limit_ms; } .. } } .. }` | 9:48 `type/recursive_borrow` "cannot use st inside a mutable collection Some arm" | SPEC.md:481 (R-6e-4: the root of `P` may not be mentioned in the arm) |
| `split_map_fields.pruv` | `fn refresh_maps(inout sessions: HashMap<String, Budget>, inout clocks: HashMap<String, Clock>, ..)` called as `refresh_maps(inout st.sessions, inout st.clocks, sid, bid, now)` | 26:16 `type/inout_argument` "an inout argument must be the whole name of a local array or an inout parameter, not a field" | SPEC.md:621-625 (fields are rejected as inout arguments), SPEC.md:662 (R-6g-2) |
| `reply_result.pruv` | `pub struct Reply { status: i64, effects: Vec<Effect> }`, `pub fn call(inout st: St) -> Reply ! alloc` | 5:5 `type/entry_signature` "host entry crate::call cannot have the type crate::Reply in the result" | SPEC.md:580 (R-6f-1: `Vec<i64>` / `Vec<bool>` / scalar results only) |

Positive control `single_map_controls.pruv` (two sequential `map_get_mut`, sessions then clocks, plus
`st.effects = vec_push::<Effect>(move st.effects, Effect { .. })` on a `St.effects: Vec<Effect>` field) is accepted by
both; the generated Rust is 7,018 bytes and byte-identical. So effects can be kept as a `Vec<Effect>` field of the
resident state (the host drains it after the call), but the reply struct itself cannot cross the entry; the first two
repros are the blocking gap.

### P31T3.4 Why no change was made

Every legal encoding is a workaround the brief rules out or keeps the debt cause:

- three lookups (read the clock scalars, mutate the budget, look the clock up again to write it): one more SipHash
  probe and compare per time-path call than hand, the D25 / D26 cause in another form;
- copy the clock out, mutate both, write it back with `map_insert`: the per-call copy workaround (and an owned key
  and `runs` map clone);
- merge the clock fields into the session's `Budget`: not the hand shape, and the shared clock-owner rule (one clock
  per budget id, owner tracked across sessions, `forgetSession`) is keyed by budget id, not session id;
- move settle / re-arm into the host: a budget decision on the host.

The worker (Codex gpt-6.2-sol, account Codex 2) stopped before porting: no file under bench/l3/budget/ changed, so
every consumer's Q and every debt cell (D14, D19-D30) stays as recorded in Appendix P29-P31 and §7.5. The worker
reran the current flat `q --set raise --py`: 300 exact / 0 cut / 0 fail (428 raise calls). The typed Q, `h`, `same` and
perf were not run (no typed entry exists).

### P31T3.5 Proposed root row (P31D, before P31T)

Both compilers, SPEC.md, tests/: (1) disjoint field borrows of the root state: inside the `Some` arm of
`map_get_mut(inout st.f, k)` allow `map_get_mut` / `vec_at_mut` / reads on a different field `st.g` (the arm still
rejects `st.f` and `st` as a whole), or equivalently allow `inout st.f` field paths as inout arguments when the
fields of one call are pairwise distinct; (2) struct entry results under R-6f-1: a root entry may return a non-generic
struct whose fields are scalars and `Vec<S>` of P31S element structs (`Reply { status, effects: Vec<Effect> }`).
Gate as P31S (positive and negative tests in both, generated Rust byte-identical, a small example against hand Rust:
two live `get_mut` on sibling fields, no clone). Then P31T restarts with the M10b lane.

### P31T3.6 Budget

About 60 minutes of the 2 hours; 1 of 24 delegations (write, Codex gpt-6.2-sol on Codex 2: typed port attempt, found
the gap and wrote the repros); 1 release build of pruvc-rs; repros re-checked here on both compilers; no audit (no
change to audit).

Cause of the gating cells by line (one fix attempt used, c2c7cb3 plus the perf items of 4adc42e; still over, so these are §7.5 debt D28 / D29):
- end M / L (1.85x / 1.86x; the flat lane was 1.12x / 0.89x): `halt` (root_m10b_typed.pruv:92-115) builds `b.stopped` with one `running_id` trusted call per
  running delegation, each a fresh `String` (the fact decodes the id into a temporary `Vec<u16>` and re-encodes it,
  m7_test/bud_facts.rs:235) plus a `vec_push` growth step, where hand takes the host's `Vec<String>` once
  (hand_m10b.rs:284). A trusted fn cannot return `Vec<String>` (R-6d-1, SPEC.md lists `String` and `Vec<i64>` only),
  so the per-id copy stays. Dropping the clock frees each run twice (`runs` key and the `run_order` copy). The typed
  Pruv slope is about 16 ns per id against hand 8 and flat 6, so the typed lane is slower than the flat lane it
  replaces from D = 50 on; the flat lane kept the stopped ids as words in its record and never built `String`s.
- extend M / L (1.14x / 1.07x; the flat lane was 0.63x / 0.42x): the same `halt` loop on the strip path plus the `run_order` duplicate: every new run
  allocates two strings (`runs` key, `run_order` copy, root_m10b_typed.pruv:296-298). `run_order` exists because
  observation needs insertion order and the ordinal cannot live in the map value: `HashMap<String, i64>` as a nested
  record field is rejected (`type/foreign_owned_type`, R-6e-6, SPEC.md:503-507).
- Fixed per call on every path: `Reply.effects` is a new `Vec` per call (no vec clear / truncate builtin; hand reuses
  its buffer with `effects.clear()`, hand_m10b.rs:190), which is the unlimited / end 1 vs 0 allocation, and `equal`
  (root_m10b_typed.pruv:36) compares `String` with `str` by a byte loop (no string comparison builtin).

### P31T5.5 Gap: an inout parameter's field as the inout argument of a user function

File bench/l3/budget/m10b_test/root_m10b_typed.pruv (`emit`, line 36, and every entry that builds `Reply.effects`);
rule SPEC.md:679 (6g whole-name inout arguments).
Minimal repro (`/tmp` file, rs compiler: `{"stage": "type", "line": 21, "col": 32, "code": "inout_argument"}`,
"an inout argument must be the whole name of a local array or an inout parameter, not a field"):

```
pub struct Effect { tag: i64 }
pub struct Out { fx: Vec<Effect> }
pub struct Rec { n: i64 }
pub struct St { recs: HashMap<String, Rec>, out: Out }

fn emit(inout o: Out, tag: i64) -> () ! alloc
{
  if len(o.fx) < 1099511627776 { o.fx = vec_push::<Effect>(move o.fx, Effect { tag: tag }); }
}

fn bump(inout r: Rec, inout o: Out) -> () ! alloc
{
  if r.n < 1000 { r.n = r.n + 1; }
  emit(inout o, r.n);
}

pub fn step(inout st: St, k: str) -> i64 ! alloc
{
  vec_clear::<Effect>(inout st.out.fx);
  match map_get_mut::<String, Rec>(inout st.recs, k) {
    Some(r) => { bump(inout r, inout st.out); }
    None => { }
  }
  return len(st.out.fx);
}
```

An `inout fx: Vec<Effect>` parameter fails the same way, and a record holding `Vec<Effect>` cannot be a map or
vector value (`foreign_owned_type`), so there is no other place to keep a reusable buffer. Proposed root row: allow a
field path of an inout parameter (`inout st.out`) as the inout argument of a user function when it is disjoint from
every live borrow (the R-6e-8 sibling rule extended from `map_get_mut` arms to user calls), in both compilers. With it,
`Reply.effects` moves to `St.out` and is reset with `vec_clear`, which removes the extra allocation in D25, D28 and D29.

### P31T5.6 Step 2

M4 (the session / clock / tool store consumer of bud_store) moved to typed resident state as its own lane, the same
way as M10b: `bench/l3/budget/m34_test/root_m4_typed.pruv` keeps `St { sessions: HashMap<String, Sess>, clocks:
HashMap<String, Clock>, tools: HashMap<String, Tool>, ... }` resident across `m4_op` / `m4_observe` calls, with an
order vector per map for observe order (deleted slots stay; a slot is live only when its ordinal matches).
`driver_m4_typed.rs` turns the q wire keys into `String` and back. The flat M4 lane (root_m4.pruv) is unchanged and
still green, so no consumer is half-moved: M4 runs whole on either lane.

Gap 2 (blocks a `Vec<String>` reply, worked around):

- File: root_m4_typed.pruv (Reply); SPEC.md:640 (R-6f-3, entry result struct fields).
- R-6f-3 allows `Vec<i64>`, `Vec<bool>` and `Vec<E>` of an owned aggregate E in an entry result struct, not
  `Vec<String>`, although R-6d-1 trusts a plain `Vec<String>` result. Both compilers give `type/entry_signature`.
- Minimal repro (both compilers, line 2 col 5):

```
pub struct Reply { keys: Vec<String> }
pub fn reply() -> Reply ! alloc {
  return Reply { keys: vec_new::<String>() };
}
```

- Workaround used: `Vec<Key>` with `Key { s: String, offset: i64 }` (accepted by both compilers).
- Proposed root row: allow `Vec<String>` fields in R-6f-3 entry result structs with the R-6d-1 trust rule.

Cause of the five gating cells, line by line:

1. Each timed call frees a whole map of String keys: forgetTurn drops a Turn with n activities, DROP / CLOSE drops
   a Clock with R runs.
2. The typed lanes hold every key twice: as the map key and as an owned `String` in the order vector.
3. The order vector exists only because observation (and the I2 recount) must visit the entries in insertion order,
   and SPEC.md:497-503 (R-6e-5) gives String-keyed maps no iteration: only map_get, map_get_mut, map_remove,
   map_lookup and map_insert.
4. The hand lanes (hand_m9.rs `runs: HashMap<String, bool>`, hand_m8 activities) keep one key per entry, so they free
   n (or R) Strings where the typed lane frees 2n; per entry the typed slope is about 16.6 ns (M9 drop, (1915.2 -
   423.7) / 90) against about 8.7 ns for hand, which matches the doubled free.
5. Fix attempt (one per cell, the same for all five): drop the order vector. It is not language-legal: without map
   iteration the observation order cannot be rebuilt, and Q compares that order. No other layout keeps one owned key
   per entry (a Vec-primary store still needs an owned key in the index map). The cells stay FAIL and are carried as
   debt rows D36 / D37 with this gap.

Gap 3 (blocks closing the M8 toolforget and M9 drop / close cells):

- Files: m8_test/root_m8_typed.pruv (Turn.activity_order), m9_test/root_m9_typed.pruv (Clock.order); SPEC.md:497-503
  (R-6e-5 text-keyed maps).
- Minimal repro (both compilers: `type/unknown_fn: unknown function map_keys`, line 5 col 40):

```
pub struct Clock { runs: HashMap<String, i64> }
pub struct St { clocks: HashMap<String, Clock> }
pub fn count(inout st: St, bid: str) -> i64 {
  match map_get::<String, Clock>(st.clocks, bid) {
    Some(c) => { let ks: Vec<String> = map_keys::<String, i64>(c.runs); return len(ks); }
    None => { return 0; }
  }
}
```

- Proposed root row: an insertion-ordered String-keyed map (or ordered borrowed iteration over its keys and values)
  so resident state needs no parallel `Vec<String>` order vector; check in both compilers that the generated Rust
  keeps one owned key per entry.

Gap 4 (worked around, no perf cell depends on it):

- File: m9_test/root_m9_typed.pruv:8 (Clock.runs); SPEC.md:509-514 (R-6e-6).
- `pub struct Run { waiting: bool } pub struct Clock { runs: HashMap<String, Run> } pub struct St { clocks:
  HashMap<String, Clock> } pub fn count(inout st: St) -> i64 { return len(st.clocks); }` is refused by both
  compilers with `type/foreign_owned_type: String-keyed maps require i64, bool or owned aggregate values`.
- Workaround used: `HashMap<String, i64>` with `2 * ordinal + waiting`.
- Proposed root row: allow owned records without nested collections as values of a map nested in a map value,
  with in-place `map_get_mut` and cross-compiler coverage.

### P31T6.5 Gap: remove that returns the value

R-6e-7 `map_remove::<K, V>(inout P, k) -> bool` drops the value, so code that must work on an entry and then remove it looks it up twice. Repro `work/p31t6/map_take/take.pruv` (pruvc-rs: `{"stage": "type", "code": "unknown_fn", "message": "unknown function map_take"}`); the legal two-lookup form `twolookups.pruv` compiles to `st.clocks.get_mut(bid)` then `st.clocks.remove(bid).is_some()`.

Proposed root row:

| P31R | Both compilers (pruvc, pruvc-rs), SPEC.md, tests/ | Root package before the next P31T attempt. `map_take::<K, V>(inout P, k) -> Option<V>` on `HashMap<i64 | String, S | i64 | bool>` (including R-6e-6 nested maps): removes the entry and moves the owned value out in one lookup (Rust `P.remove(k)`, borrowed `str` key for `String`), the `Some(v)` binding owned and mutable in its arm; the verifier clears presence and subtracts one from the length only when present (as R-6e-7). Positive and negative tests in both compilers, the repro `take.pruv`, small example vs hand Rust at M / L (one hash, no clone). Then M10b `end` becomes one `map_take` of the clock (D29). |

### Audit

One audit (Codex gpt-6.2-astra, read-only over the diff). One recheck of the must-fix items (Codex gpt-6.2-astra, check mode, on be99610): both fixed.

- Must-fix 1, M12 `attach` lost the stored budget when `origin` was a 30-deep array sent through the raw V interface (typed dump 0 words, hand 316): `replace_wire` deleted the old root first and `attach_fresh` took root 0 as success (root_m12_typed.pruv:298, :1296). Fixed as listed above. Recheck: fixed; a closed budget re-attached over raw V with a 30-deep array `origin` gives the same 284-word dump on rs typed and hand.
- Must-fix 2, the M10b driver logged `E unit` before walking the effects, so the unit-before-clear order check (run_m10b.py:337) could not catch a reorder: fixed as listed above. Recheck: fixed by reading; a clear emitted before the consumption now logs before `E unit` and fails the order check. M10b stays 300 / 300 on both sets and H 10 / 10 on rs and py.
- Must-fix 3, the worker notes for D51 described the reverted change: annotated in `work/p31t9/P31T9_W3_NOTES.md` (not committed).
- Advisory: the M9 `perf --typed` table measures typed and hand on pre-decoded input, while the flat lane's time includes parsing (driver_m9.rs:709, run_m9.py:746). The flat and typed M9 tables are therefore not comparable with each other; typed vs hand is.

### Budget

Delegations: 8 calls of 20. W1 M12 (Codex gpt-6.2-sol high, write), W2 M10 / M7 / M9 (Codex gpt-6.2-sol high, write), W3 M11 / M10b (Codex gpt-6.2-sol high, write), one audit call rejected on its input before running, the audit (Codex gpt-6.2-astra), the recheck (Codex gpt-6.2-astra; the first call could not read its brief, the continuation inlined it). Ended before the 01:06 KST deadline.

### Gaps

- D63: an `inout` `HashMap` parameter cannot be reassigned as a whole (`type/immutable` on rs and py), so a value taken with `map_take` cannot be put back through a shared module's map-typed inout parameter; this blocks the M7 close single lookup (D43). Repro `work/p31t9/gap_inout_map/repro.pruv` with `rs.out` / `py.out`.
- No other new gap. The M12 cost (D49 / D50) is the node-per-value document store, not a language gap: a contiguous typed word store is the next fix.

### P32b.5 Generated vs hand (M4 `session_put` replace, after the one perf fix)

Generated (`work/m34/gen_m4_typed.rs:373-381`, rs):

```rust
match st.sessions.get_mut(key) {
    Some(session) => {
        session.blob.clear();
        let mut i: i64 = 0i64;
        while (i < (blob.len() as i64)) {
            session.blob.push((unsafe { *blob.get_unchecked((i) as usize) }));
            i = (i + 1i64);
        }
    }
```

Hand (`perf_headroom/host/src/bin/m4_hand.rs:122-125`):

```rust
let existed = if let Some(v) = self.sessions.get_mut(&self.k1[..]) {
    v.clear();
    v.extend_from_slice(blob);
    true
```

The put path now matches hand in allocation; after the audit key fix and the `needs_escape` fast path the remaining 2.5x is `session_get` (`blob_copy` per get) and `reply()` (7 empty Vecs per op), D79.

### P32c.5 Generated vs hand

Generated `bud_delay.rs` (pruvc-rs, from `bud_delay.pruv`):

```rust
pub fn delay_bits(num: bool, bits: i64) -> i64 {
    if ((num && (bits >= 4607182418800017408i64)) && (bits <= 4746794007244308480i64)) {
        return bits;
    }
    return 4607182418800017408i64;
}
```

Old hand clamp in `host.rs`: `V::Num(d) if *d >= 1.0 && *d <= 2147483647.0 => *d, _ => 1.0`. Non-negative doubles order like their bits; negative doubles have negative bits, so the two agree on every input (boundary program above). Timer cells: timer_cycle 159.2 ns, timer_fire 85.8 ns (host harness, non-gating).

`bud_tlife::running_valid` (Pruv) replaces the Rust frame walk: it checks `a[0] == 0`, `0 <= count <= n - 2`, then per frame `units >= 0`, `running_frame_words(units) <= n - pos`, zero padding in the last word, and `pos == n` at the end; `units > 2^30` is refused before the word count is computed.

## Appendix P31K: text-keyed aggregate maps, one-level nesting, map_remove and vec_at_mut (both compilers)

### P31K.1 Rules (SPEC.md)

- R-6e-5 text-keyed maps: `HashMap<String, V>` for `V` = `i64`, `bool` or an owned aggregate, wherever the
  `i64`-keyed map is allowed. `map_get` / `map_get_mut` / `map_remove` / contract `map_lookup` borrow a `str`
  or a read of a `String` binding or field (Rust: the `&str` itself or `.as_str()`; one hash, no key copy).
  `map_insert` takes an owned `String` (call result or `move`); a borrowed `String` read there is
  `type/foreign_move`, a `str` value an argument type mismatch (audit #4). `[u8]` keys stay rejected. The verifier
  indexes the map by `strkey(n, a)`, one uninterpreted function (byte length, byte array) without axioms: equal
  strings give equal keys, and a model collision between distinct strings can only prove fewer facts.
- R-6e-6 one level of nesting: an owned aggregate may hold `Vec<String>`, `HashMap<String, bool>` and
  `HashMap<i64, bool>` fields and still be an element / value of the R-6e-3 collections. Deeper nesting,
  such records as direct fields or as `Option` / `Result` payloads are `type/foreign_owned_type`. Inside a
  mutable `Some` arm the nested fields take `vec_push` / `map_insert` (R-6d-2: `.push(x)` / `.insert(k, v)`)
  and `map_remove`; `len` and `map_get` read them; `vec_get` on `Vec<String>` is not supported. A root `pub`
  function may borrow such a record; like R-6f-2 resident state its collection lengths are a caller obligation
  (the record comes from this program's entries), not a per-call check (audit #2, see P31K.4).
- R-6e-7 `map_remove::<K, V>(inout P, k) -> bool` (`.remove(&k).is_some()`, borrowed key for `String`;
  the verifier clears the presence bit and subtracts one from the length only when present) and
  `vec_at_mut::<S>(inout P, i)` on `Vec<S>` with the R-6e-4 arm rules
  (`match P.get_mut(<usize as ::std::convert::TryFrom<i64>>::try_from(i).unwrap_or(usize::MAX))`, audit #1; `Some` iff `0 <= i < len`, binder
  written back to that index). Non-entry `inout` map / vector parameters are allowed only when the value /
  element is an owned aggregate; other collection inout stays `type/inout_type`.

Proof decisions (main): `strkey` is created lazily on the first `String` key so programs without text keys
keep their exact SMT (an eager declaration turned `must_reject/g10a_v_wait_equal` from `assert` into
`verify_unknown`); the implementation's first draft allowed `inout Vec<i64>` and was narrowed to aggregate
elements (`must_reject/g5_inout_type_vec` stays rejected).

New tests (37, accept and reject, run by `tests/spec_trace.py` on both compilers): `tests/spec/r6e_5_*` (14:
`bool_value`, `borrowed_insert_key`, `bytes_key`, `bytes_lookup`, `distinct_key_terms`, `i64_value`,
`insert_moved_key`, `literal_key`, `llvm`, `lookup_field_contract`, `lookup_keeps_key`, `lookup_postcondition`,
`str_key_charge`, `str_param_key`), `r6e_6_*` (11: `frame`, `inner_insert`, `inner_push`, `map_field`,
`map_field_vec`, `map_of_vec`, `option_payload`, `record_field`, `vec_of_vec`, `vec_string`, `vec_string_read`),
`r6e_7_*` (12: `inner_remove`, `remove_alias`, `remove_i64`, `remove_llvm`, `remove_str`, `vec_at_mut`,
`vec_at_mut_bounds`, `vec_field_place`, `vec_inout_forward`, `vec_llvm`, `vec_not_scrutinee`,
`vec_recursive_borrow`). The three P31T gap repros (`gap_str_key`, `gap_map_field`, `gap_vec_string`,
Appendix P31T) now compile on both compilers with byte-identical output.

### P31K.2 Small example (bench/l3/p31k/)

`p31k.pruv`: `St { sessions: HashMap<String, Session> }`, `Session { used: i64, stopped: Vec<String>,
runs: HashMap<String, bool> }`; `charge(inout st, sid: str, x)` adds to `used` in place, `halt(inout st, sid: str,
name: str)` removes `name` from `runs` and pushes an owned copy onto `stopped`. `gen.rs` is the rs output
(py byte-identical), `hand.rs` the hand Rust, `driver.rs` the timing driver (`rustc -O`).

| hand Rust (`hand.rs`) | generated (`gen.rs`) |
|---|---|
| `match st.sessions.get_mut(sid)` | `match st.sessions.get_mut(sid)` (one hash of the caller's bytes, no key copy) |
| `r.used += x;` | `r.used = (r.used + x);` |
| `(r.stopped.len() as i64) < 1_000_000` | `((r.stopped.len() as i64) < 1000000i64)` |
| `r.runs.remove(name).is_some()` | `r.runs.remove(name).is_some()` (borrowed key) |
| `r.stopped.push(name.to_string())` | `pruv_g6_string_new()` + `pruv_g6_string_push_str(owned, name)` + `r.stopped.push(owned)` (one allocation each) |
| - | wrapper: one `sid.len()` / `name.len()` 2^40 branch, entry budget |

No clone, no bounds check, no re-encoding of the state per call.

Measured with `bench/l3/p31k/driver.rs` (same driver links hand and gen), 7 alternating rounds per cell,
`/usr/bin/time -l` for RSS, machine load average about 6-8 during the run.

| size | hand median [range] | gen median [range] | gen / hand | RSS hand / gen |
|---|---|---|---|---|

## Appendix P31D: disjoint root-field borrows and struct entry results (both compilers)

### P31D.1 Rules (SPEC.md)

- R-6e-8 disjoint field borrows: inside the `Some` arm of `map_get_mut` / `vec_at_mut` on the field path
  `P = x.f1...fn`, the arm may use any field path `x.g1...gm` of the same root that is disjoint from `P`
  (neither is a prefix of the other): read, assign, pass as an `inout` place and open a nested
  `map_get_mut` / `vec_at_mut` arm on it, to any depth over pairwise disjoint paths. `x` as a whole, `P`, a
  prefix of `P` and a path through `P` stay `type/recursive_borrow`. Rust emits nested
  `match x.f.get_mut(..)` arms over sibling fields (Rust's own disjoint field borrows), no clone. The verifier
  is unchanged: it already writes the binder back into the arm-exit value of `x` along `P` only.
- R-6f-3 struct entry results: a root `pub` non-generic function may return a non-generic struct with at least
  one collection field whose fields are plain values, `Vec<i64>`, `Vec<bool>` or `Vec<E>` for an owned
  aggregate `E` (R-6e-3) without R-6e-6 nested collections. Rust returns it by value (fields `pub`); `HashMap`
  fields, nested-collection elements and deeper nesting stay `type/entry_signature`; the LLVM backend rejects
  it with `codegen/unsupported_type` (no C ABI, as R-6f-1).

Why option (a), path-aware `Some`-arm locks, and not (b), pairwise-distinct `inout st.f` arguments: the gap in
Appendix P31T (attempt 3) is two live element borrows of sibling maps, which is exactly a nested arm. (a) changes
one check (the `recursive_borrow` lookup compares field paths instead of root names) and needs no new
call-site aliasing rule, no new verifier havoc of several places per call, and no codegen change, since nested
`get_mut` on sibling fields is what rustc already accepts. (b) would need a second aliasing rule for calls and
does not by itself give two live element borrows. So `f(inout x.f, inout x.g)` stays `type/inout_argument`
(section 6g whole-name rule); the P31T repro `split_map_fields` is still rejected with that code on both compilers.

Implementation: py `pruvc/check.py` records each mutable `Some`-arm borrow as (root, field path) and each
field-access root with its outermost path; `lookup` rejects only on overlap (one path a prefix of the other, a
bare root always overlaps). Rust `check.rs` mirrors it (`map_roots: Vec<(String, Vec<String>)>`, `field_place`,
`expr_with_path`). `is_result_record` is added to both entry checks. Codegen and the verifier are untouched.
After the audit (P31D.4) a `match` on an extended field path `Q` of an `inout` root or element binding also holds
(root, `Q`) for its arms (`match_inout_path` / `match_paths` / `match_path_held` in both), so an overlapping
assignment, move or `inout` pass is `type/recursive_borrow` while disjoint siblings stay usable; and
`is_result_record` rejects `[T]` / `str` fields.

New tests (17, run by `tests/spec_trace.py` on both compilers): `tests/spec/r6e_8_*` accept `sibling_maps`,
`sibling_vecs`, `sibling_write`, `nested_sibling_ok`; reject (`type/recursive_borrow`) `same_field`,
`same_path_read`, `parent_path`, `whole_root`, `match_payload` (audit A1), `match_move` (recheck); accept `match_sibling_ok`.
`tests/spec/r6f_3_*` accept `reply_entry`, `plain_entry`; reject
`map_field`, `nested_element`, `array_field` (audit C1) (`type/entry_signature`) and `llvm_entry` (`codegen/unsupported_type`).
`r6e_4_root_in_arm` now uses the root as a whole (`g(st)`), since a disjoint scalar field read is accepted under
R-6e-8. The P31T attempt 3 repros: `sibling_map_borrow` and `reply_result` compile on both compilers,
`split_map_fields` stays `type/inout_argument`.

bid, now)` holds `get_mut` on both maps at once and moves time from the clock into the budget; `poll(inout st,
sid) -> Reply ! alloc` returns `Reply { status, effects: Vec<Effect> }` (R-6f-3). `gen.rs` is the py output,
the rs output is byte-identical (`cmp`, and `gen.rs.foreign.json`); `hand.rs` the hand Rust, `driver.rs` the
timing driver (`rustc -O --edition 2021`, same checksum for hand and gen).

|---|---|
| `match st.sessions.get_mut(sid) { Some(budget) =>` | `match st.sessions.get_mut(sid) { Some(budget) => {` |
| `match st.clocks.get_mut(bid) { Some(clock) =>` | `match st.clocks.get_mut(bid) { Some(clock) => {` (second live `get_mut`, sibling field) |
| `if 0 <= clock.since_ms && ... budget.active_ms <= 1_000_000_000_000` | same guard, `(*clock).since_ms` / `(*budget).active_ms` |

| `effects.push(Effect { .. })`, `Reply { status, effects }` | `pruv_g6_vec_push__..(effects, Effect { .. })` (moves the vec), `return (Reply { status: status, effects: effects });` |
| - | wrapper: one `sid.len()` / `bid.len()` 2^40 branch |

## Appendix P31N: scalar map fields, trusted Vec<String>, vec_clear and string_eq (both compilers)

### P31N.1 Rules (SPEC.md)

- R-6e-6 widened: an owned aggregate may also have `HashMap<String, i64>` and `HashMap<i64, i64>` fields (next to
  the `bool`-valued maps), when the record is used as a collection element or value in the program. Inside a
  `map_get_mut` `Some` arm on the outer map, `map_get`, `map_get_mut`, `map_insert`, `map_remove` and `len` work
  on the nested map with a borrowed `str` key. A mutable scalar binder is read with `*v` or `v` and assigned with
  `*v = x` or `v = x`. Rust emits `c.runs.get_mut(name)`, `*v = ..`, `.insert` / `.remove` in place, no clone.
- R-6d-1 widened: a trusted fn may return `Vec<String>` with `! alloc` (Rust backend only). The host's owned
  strings move in without a copy; the wrapper checks the vector length and each element length against 2^40
  (representation failure, section 7). Its `ensures` may use `len(result)`.
- R-6e-9: `vec_get::<String>(v, i)` borrows a `str` from a `Vec<String>` place (local, parameter or field) as a
  direct `str` argument of a user fn, the text key of `map_get` / `map_get_mut` / `map_remove`, or an operand of
  `string_eq` / `len`; other uses are `type/foreign_owned_type`. The verifier proves `0 <= i < len(v)`.
- R-6e-10: `vec_clear::<T>(inout P) -> ()` is a whole statement on an owned mutable local, an `inout` parameter
  or a mutable (nested) field; Rust emits `P.clear();` (capacity kept, no `alloc`). The verifier sets the length
  to 0 and keeps sibling fields and outer elements. `inout` `Vec<T>` parameters are allowed for non-entry fns; a
  call to a callee that may clear (directly or by forwarding) havocs the argument length at the call site
  (`vec_resize_params`), and loops drop such operands from the length-keep set.
- R-6e-11: `string_eq(a, b) -> bool` on borrowed `String` / `str` / `[u8]` / R-6e-9 operands; Rust compares
  borrowed byte slices (`a.as_bytes() == b.as_bytes()`), no owned copy. The verifier states equal lengths and
  equal bytes on `[0, n)` (one bound variable per use). A field or element operand borrows its root place for the
  call, so moving that root in the same call is `type/foreign_borrow`.

Implementation: py first (`pruvc/check.py`, `typeinfo.py`, `foreign.py`, `foreign_codegen.py`, `codegen.py`,
`verify.py`, `refine.py`, `vast.py`, `vparser.py`, `llvmgen.py` rejects), then the Rust port of the same 11
places (`pruv-core` ast / check / codegen / dump / foreign / gtype / llvmgen / mono / parser, `pruv-proof`
symbolic / sys). The LLVM backend rejects the new features with `codegen/unsupported_type`.

New tests (run by `tests/spec_trace.py` on both compilers): `tests/spec/r6e_6_*` accept `scalar_map_field`,
`string_map_field`, `i64_map_field`, `deep_map_field` (reject); `r6d_1_vec_string_*` accept `result`, `index`,
`moved`; `r6e_9_*` accept `borrowed_keys`, reject `element_let`, `temp_vector`, `unproved_element`; `r6e_10_*` accept `vec_clear`,
`clear_call_soundness`, reject `clear_borrowed`; `r6e_11_*` accept `string_eq`, `eq_different_lengths`, reject
`eq_non_text`, `eq_moved_root`, `eq_moved_elem`. `tests/must_reject/g5_inout_type_vec.pruv` now uses an inout `HashMap<i64, i64>`
(an inout `Vec` is legal under R-6e-10; same code `type/inout_type`).

### P31N.2 Small example (bench/l3/p31n/)

`p31n.pruv`: `Clock { owner: String, since_ms, runs: HashMap<String, i64> }` held in
`St { clocks: HashMap<String, Clock>, out: Vec<i64> }`. `tick(inout st, sid, name, now)` counts a run in place in
the nested scalar map; `halt(inout st, sid, who)` takes `running_ids(sid) -> Vec<String>` from the trusted crate
`p31n_facts`, clears `st.out`, checks the owner with `string_eq` and removes each id with a borrowed element key.

| hand Rust (`hand.rs`) | generated (`gen.rs`) |
|---|---|
| `match st.clocks.get_mut(sid) { Some(c) =>` | same |
| `match c.runs.get_mut(name) { Some(v) => if *v < 1e12 { *v += 1 }` | same, `*v = (*v + 1i64)` |
| `c.runs.insert(name.to_string(), 1)` | `string_new` + `string_push_str` then `pruv_g6_map_insert__string__i(mem::take(&mut c.runs), k, 1)` (moves the map, one `len < 2^40` check) |

| `for (i, id) in ids.iter().enumerate() { c.runs.remove(id.as_str())` | `while i < ids.len()`, `c.runs.remove(ids[usize::try_from(i)..].as_str())` (checked index, R-6d-2 under a trusted fn) |

## Appendix R03L: array move into a record and named predicates for json (both compilers)

Main decision 2026-11-20 (docs/L3_R03.md §7): close R03 gaps G4 and G1 before R03 C. G3 and G2 were optional
within the 2.5 h budget and are queued (R03L.5). R03 C (rescan removal, in-scanner UTF-8, D32/D33) is not started.

### R03L.1 Rules (SPEC.md)

- R-6e-12 (G4): `move x` transfers an owned array local or a `take x: [T]` parameter into a struct field, enum
  payload, local initializer, assignment, return or `take` argument with no copy. Array fields and indexed elements
  cannot be moved; moving a plain or `inout` array parameter is `type/array_alias`. A `take` parameter needs an
  explicit `move` argument. A read after a definite or possible move is `type/foreign_move`; a loop must restore a
  moved binding on every continuing path (`type/foreign_loop_move`). Rust takes `Vec<T>` and emits the value
  directly; the verifier charges zero units for the move. LLVM moves local arrays by emptying the source slot and
  rejects `take` array parameters (`codegen/unsupported_type`).
- R-6-2 (G1): `pred fn p(x: T, ..) -> bool { return <expr>; }` names one contract expression (quantifiers,
  aggregates, struct field reads allowed; no effects, contracts, cost or type parameters, else
  `type/pred_signature`). Each use in `requires` / `ensures` / `invariant` / `assert` / `decreases` is replaced by
  the body at the arguments, so `ensures p(result)` is proved from the code and `requires p(d)` is checked at every
  call; nothing is assumed. `pub pred fn` is used across modules by path. A call in code is `type/pred_in_code`.
  An argument using a name the body binds is `type/call_in_contract`.
- Rust in-place `truncate`: when over half the capacity is unused after `truncate`, emit `shrink_to_fit` so a moved
  buffer does not keep its growth slack (both compilers, byte-identical output). LLVM keeps the capacity (R03L.5).

Implementation: py first (`pruvc/check.py`, `codegen.py`, `foreign.py`, `llvmgen.py`, `modules.py`, `vast.py`,
`vparser.py`), then the Rust port of the same places (`pruv-core` abi / ast / bindings / check / codegen / foreign
/ lexer / llvmgen / modules / mono / parser, `pruvc` driver). b_root Rust output is byte-identical between the
compilers.

## Appendix P31F: language roots for the P31T5.5 repro (both compilers)

P31F adds the four language gaps that P31T attempt 5 hit in the M10b tool state (P31T5.5). The py
compiler was changed first, then pruvc-rs. Both emit byte-identical Rust for every new fixture. LLVM
rejects the new forms with a diagnostic (`codegen/unsupported_type`); it does not miscompile them.
P31T attempt 6 was not started.

### P31F.1 Rules (SPEC.md)

- R-6g-3 (new, after R-6g-2): a user function can take a field path `x.f[.g...]` as an `inout`
  argument. The root `x` can be an `inout` parameter, a local, or a match/`get_mut` element binding.
  Paths in one call must be pairwise disjoint: no path is a prefix of another, a root and its path
  are not both passed, and the same path is not passed twice. A path that overlaps a held borrow or
  a pending write-back is rejected. Rust passes `&mut x.f` directly (no `mem::take` and no
  write-back). R-6e-8 and R-6g-1 now point at R-6g-3 for paths.
- R-6f-3 (addition): an entry result struct can have `Vec<String>` fields. The vector moves to the
  host; there is no element copy. A nested `Vec<Vec<String>>` field is still rejected.
- R-6e-13 (new): read-only `for (k, v) in P` over a place `P: HashMap<String, T>` where
  `T = i64 | bool | S` (S is a nongeneric value struct). Rust: `for (k, &v) in P.iter()` (`v` is
  borrowed for S), and `k` is `&str`. The iteration order is unspecified. The verifier assumes
  nothing about the order or the count. Contracts that depend on these (an invariant over the
  visit order, a cost bound on the count) are rejected. Inside the body you cannot insert, remove,
  or assign to `P`, its key, or an outer place reached through the binders. You cannot store a
  binder into an owned slot or move it into a constructor, and you cannot `return` from the body.
  The rule rejects i64-keyed maps, Vec values, non-place sources, and LLVM.
- R-6e-6 (addition): a record held in a map (`HashMap<String, R>`) can itself contain a
  `HashMap<String, R2>` of records. insert, remove, get, and `get_mut` work through the outer
  `get_mut` binding. Removing the parent while an inner borrow is live is rejected, as are
  overlapping inner borrows, collection-valued inner records, and moving (`take`) a root that owns a
  record map (`foreign_move`).

### P31F.2 Tests

- Spec fixtures: 41 new. 12 accept: `r6e_13_{aggregate,bool,bool_fn,scalar}`,
  `r6e_6_record_map_field`, `r6f_3_vec_string_field`,
  `r6g_3_{binder_field,collection_paths,disjoint_arm,match_sibling,nested_local,siblings}`. 29 reject:
  `r6e_13_{assign_binder,assign_key,assign_place,cost,count,ctor_binder,i64_key,inout_path,insert,invariant_entry,invariant_preserved,llvm,non_place,order,remove,return,store_binder,vec}`,
  `r6e_6_record_map_{collection_value,overlap,remove_parent,take_root}`,
  `r6f_3_nested_vec_string_field`,
  `r6g_3_{equal_path,held_path,match_overlap,missing_writeback,root_and_path,statement_overlap}`.
- Runtime fixtures (pruv vs hand Rust, same output): `p31f_inout_field` (the P31T5.5 repro shape:
  `step` emits into `&mut st.out` inside a `get_mut` arm), `p31f_map_iter`, and
  `p31f_nested_record_map`.

### P31F.3 Repro: generated vs hand

Generated (`p31f_inout_field`, both compilers byte-identical):

```rust
fn step__pruv_body(st: &mut St, k: &str) -> i64 {
    st.out.fx.clear();
    match st.recs.get_mut(k) { Some(r) => { pruv_m_f_1_4_bump(r, &mut st.out); } None => {} }
    return (st.out.fx.len() as i64);
}
```

Hand:

```rust
pub fn step(st: &mut St, k: &str) -> i64 {
    st.out.fx.clear();
    if let Some(r) = st.recs.get_mut(k) { bump(r, &mut st.out); }
    st.out.fx.len() as i64
}
```

The only extra work in the generated code is in `emit`: a single `fx.len() < 2^40` capacity compare
before each `push`. There is no clone, no `mem::take`, and no write-back. `map_iter` `total` matches
the hand source (`for (k, &v) in st.vals.iter()`).

## Appendix P31R: `map_take` (both compilers)

P31R adds the root package proposed in P31T6.5: take a map entry out by value in one lookup. The py
compiler and pruvc-rs were changed in parallel from one fixed design. Both emit byte-identical Rust.
LLVM rejects the new call with `codegen/unsupported_type`, as it does for `map_remove`. M10b `end`
(D29) is not rewritten here; it stays with P31T attempt 8.

### P31R.1 Rule (SPEC.md)

- R-6e-14 (new, after R-6e-13): `map_take::<K, V>(inout P, k) -> Option<V>` with `K = i64 | String`
  and `V = i64 | bool | S` (S an owned aggregate struct, including R-6e-6 records with nested
  collections). `P` follows the R-6e-4 / R-6e-7 place rules, including a nested map field `r.sub`
  of a `get_mut` element binding. `k` is borrowed like `map_remove` (R-6e-5) and may not mention
  the root of `P`. The call is allowed only as the direct scrutinee of a `match` statement
  (`type/foreign_contract` elsewhere), so the result is never discarded and an `Option` of a record
  with nested collections never exists as a value. Inside a `map_get_mut` / `vec_at_mut` /
  `map_get` arm or a `for (k, v) in Q` body whose place overlaps `P`: `type/recursive_borrow`.
  The arms are not restricted: `P` is no longer borrowed after the call. `Some(v)` binds an owned,
  mutable value (assign, `inout v`, `move v`).
- Rust: `match P.remove(key) { Some(mut v) => ... None => ... }` with `map_remove`'s key text. One
  lookup, no clone, no `get` / `get_mut`.
- Verifier (both compilers): `map_remove`'s branch, returning the old value. With `has = d[k]`:
  assume `has => n > 0`, result `If(d[k], Some(a[k]), None)` read from the map before the store,
  then `P := Map(Store(d, k, False), a, n - If(has, 1, 0))` written back along the field path.
  The loop changed-variable analysis counts the root of `P` as written.

### P31R.2 Tests

- Spec fixtures: 13 new. 6 accept: `r6e_14_take_{record,scalar,mut_binder,nested,other_field,proc_binder}`. The record

### P31R.3 Example: generated vs hand (`bench/l3/p31r`)

Generated (both compilers byte-identical):

```rust
fn end__pruv_body(st: &mut St, bid: &str) -> i64 {
    match st.clocks.remove(bid) {
        Some(mut c) => {
            if c.armed {
                return c.used;
            }
            return 0i64;
        }
        None => {
            return (-1i64);
        }
    }
}
```

Hand:

```rust
pub fn end(st: &mut St, bid: &str) -> i64 {
    match st.clocks.remove(bid) {
        Some(c) => { if c.armed { c.used } else { 0 } }
        None => -1,
    }
}
```

`rekey` takes the clock, bumps it, and inserts it under a new key. Generated code builds the key
with `String::new()` + `push_str(to)`. Hand uses `to.to_string()`. The pub wrappers add the `str`
length guard (one compare per argument, cold panic path).

### P31R.4 Numbers (M = 1e3 clocks / 2e6 calls, L = 1e5 clocks / 1e7 calls; 7 alternating runs, median; pruv / hand)

| Cell | M time ms | M RSS KiB | L time ms | L RSS KiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| end / rekey loop | 187.45 / 180.84 (1.037) | 1968 / 2240 (0.879) | 3184.59 / 3126.99 (1.018) | 40832 / 42336 (0.964) |

`python3 tools/perf_gate.py work/p31r/perf_cells.json`: FAIL on time M and L. The ranges overlap
(M 159-230 vs 159-200 ms, L 3142-3348 vs 3080-4060 ms), so wall time alone does not settle it. The
one fix attempt was a cause probe with `/usr/bin/time -l` instructions retired:

| Build | M instructions | L instructions |
|---|---|---|
| gen | 2.50-2.55 G | 16.20 G |
| hand (`to.to_string()`) | 2.32-2.36 G | 15.33 G |
| hand probe (`String::new()` + `push_str`) | 2.53-2.55 G | 16.72 G |

With the same key construction, gen retires 0.98x (M) / 0.935x (L) of hand's instructions, so
`map_take` is at or below hand. The gap is the key: amortized `RawVec` growth through the
non-inlined `finish_grow` vs one exact allocation. pruv has no exact-allocation `str -> String`
copy. Debt D46, language row P31R-Q1. The gate stays FAIL.

## Appendix P31G: P31T attempt-7 language gaps (both compilers)

Branch `lair/read-and-do-the-work-adf0`, not merged. Goal: close the language gaps that P31T attempt 7 worked
around (D41, D43, D44, D46), each as a SPEC rule with positive and negative tests in both compilers, Python first
and the Rust port in the same commit, generated Rust byte-identical, no clone where hand Rust has none.

### P31G.1 Rules landed

| Rule | Gap | Surface | Rust | LLVM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-6e-15 | D46 (P31R-Q1) | `string_from(text: str) -> String` catalog op, `! alloc`, ensures length and content equal | `text.to_string()` after the 2^40 guard (exact allocation) | rejected (`codegen/unsupported_type`) |
| R-6e-16 | gap 6 (D41, D43) | `p.g = move p.f;` / `let t: T = move p.f;` on an owned field; the next statement must restore `p.f` (no use, return or loop exit in between) | `::std::mem::take(&mut p.f)` | rejected |
| R-6e-4 (extended) | gap 2 (D41) | `*r = e;` / `r = e;` replaces a record binder in a `map_get_mut` / `vec_at_mut` `Some` arm; `e` is a constructor, call or `move` of an owned local (else `type/foreign_move`) and does not mention `r` or the root (else `type/recursive_borrow`) | `*row = e;` | rejected |
| R-6e-17 | gap 3 (D44) | a `Vec<i64>` / `Vec<bool>` place passed to an unmarked `[i64]` / `[bool]` parameter of a user function; not to `take` / `inout`, not as a value (`let`, return, field) | `x.f.as_slice()` | rejected |
| R-6g-4 | gap 1 | `inout n: i64 | bool` on non-entry user functions; caller passes `inout x` of a mutable place of that type; alias rules as R-6g-1 / R-6g-3; `old(n)` stays `type/old_argument`; root entries stay `type/entry_signature` | `n: &mut i64`, `*n = e`, call `&mut x` | rejected |
| R-6f-4 | gap 5 | `take key: String` parameter on a Rust-host `pub` entry (with or without state) | `key: String` (moved in once) | rejected (C ABI) |

Gap 4 (entry returning a state struct with `String` / `HashMap` fields) is not landed: design note in P31G.6, row D60.

### P31G.6 Gap 4 design (queued, D60)

Repro: `pub fn init() -> St` with `St { rows: HashMap<String, Row>, name: String }`. R-6f-3 admits a root entry
result struct only when every field is a plain value or a `Vec` of plain values / R-6e-3 aggregates, so a
`String` or `HashMap` field is `type/entry_signature`. Codegen would already return `St` by value; the missing
part is the trust boundary: R-6f-3 trusts 2^40 length bounds on returned buffers, and a `St` handed back to an
R-6f-2 entry as `inout st` must carry the same bounds for the map size, every key and every nested `String`.
Proposed R-6f-5 "State struct entry results": a root `pub` entry may return a non-generic struct that is valid
R-6f-2 resident state; the per-buffer bounds are asserted at return (not trusted) so the later entry can assume
them; LLVM keeps `codegen/unsupported_type`. Tests: accept `init` then put/get through R-6f-2 entries; reject a
map of nested collections; reject on LLVM.

## Appendix P32L: language rules for the P32b compiler gaps (both compilers)

Branch `lair/read-and-do-it-on-cf07`, not merged. Goal: close the compiler gaps that P32 attempt 2 worked around
(D81, then D73, then D74), each as a SPEC rule or rule extension with positive and negative tests in both compilers,
Python first and the Rust port in the same commit, generated Rust byte-identical, no clone, copy or widening that
hand Rust lacks. The bench L3 sources are not switched to the new forms here (D84).

### P32L.1 Rules landed

| Rule | Gap | Surface | Rust | LLVM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-6e-3 / R-6f-3 (extended) | D81 | a non-generic struct with a `[u8]` field is an owned aggregate: a `HashMap<String, V>` / `HashMap<i64, V>` value and a state-struct field; `vec_get(v, i).f` borrows array fields as it borrows collections; an entry result record may not hold `Vec<E>` of such an `E` | field `Vec<u8>`, filled with `data.to_vec()` once | rejected (`codegen/unsupported_type`) |
| R-6f-6 | D73 | a Rust host entry takes `x: S` (borrowed) or `take x: S` (moved) of an owned aggregate `S`, including `Vec<i64>`, `Vec<bool>`, `String` and `[u8]` fields; field lengths trusted as for R-6f-2 state (borrowed and `take`; the host keeps them at most 2^40); `requires` on `x` checked at entry; a struct with an `[i64]`, `[bool]` or `str` field or a generic struct is outside the rule and keeps the plain-value / R-6e-6 entry paths | `x: &S` / `x: S` | rejected; `raw_entries` "c" rejects too |
| R-6f-3 (enum results) | D74 | a root `pub` entry returns a non-generic enum whose payloads are plain values, `Vec<i64>`, `Vec<bool>` or R-6f-3 records without a `Vec<String>` field, at least one owned (`Vec<String>` payloads stay `type/foreign_owned_type` at the enum declaration, as before) | `pub fn e(..) -> E`, variants moved out | rejected |
| R-6d-2 (one sentence) | D74 repro | `vec_push(vec_new(), x)` under unchecked catalog calls | `::std::vec![x]` (one allocation, `x` moved) | unchanged (the LLVM bindings shim still exports the `vec_new` / `vec_push` helpers its entries call) |

R-6f-5 stays reserved for the D60 proposal (P31G.6, state struct entry results), so the D73 rule is R-6f-6.

and D73-2 all fixed, no new regression on the same paths. Evidence: the four regression tests compile identically on

helper discovery pass, so the LLVM bindings stopped exporting the `vec_new` helper the LLVM entry still calls. Fix:
`foreign_shim` (pruvc and pruvc-rs) always emits the `vec_new` and `vec_push` helpers a program uses, as it already
did for `vec_get`; the test links and prints the expected lines in all six modes, py and rs bindings identical.

### P32L.6 Design note

D81 needed no new syntax: `[u8]` was already an owned buffer for locals and parameters; the change lets the
aggregate test count it as owned, emits it as `Vec<u8>`, and keeps buffered records out of R-6f-3 `Vec<E>` result
elements (their C-free host shape is not settled). D73 reuses the R-6f-2 trust boundary (field lengths trusted at
the entry, `requires` checked) and the existing borrow / `take` checker, so alias and use-after-move are the
R-6e-12 / R-6g-1 errors. D74 reuses R-6f-3 records as payloads; the enum must have one owned payload so plain
enums keep their old value path. The `vec_push(vec_new(), x)` sentence was the only codegen change needed to meet
1.0x on the enum result; it is a peephole under unchecked catalog calls only, so the checked path is unchanged.
The rule was first drafted as R-6f-5 and renamed R-6f-6 because R-6f-5 is the D60 proposal.

## Appendix P32M: holder records, vec_extend_from_slice and moving a take aggregate (both compilers)

Branch `lair/read-and-follow-the-brief-e5a7`, not merged. Goal: land D90, D95 and D85 as SPEC rules with positive
and negative tests in both compilers, Python first and the Rust port in the same commit, generated Rust
byte-identical, no `Box`, clone or per-element loop that hand Rust lacks. The bench L3 sources are not touched.

### P32M.1 Rules landed

| Rule | Gap | Surface | Rust | LLVM |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-6e-6 (holder records) | D90 | a non-generic record may have direct fields of a nested-collection record type (with `Vec<String>` or nested map fields) besides scalar, plain-value, R-6e-1 owned and `[u8]` fields; the holder is itself an owned aggregate: a `Vec` element, a `HashMap<i64, H>` / `HashMap<String, H>` value including a root state field, a local, a `take` parameter and a result; built per field from a call result or `move x`; `e.b.f` reads borrow, `e.b.f` assignment and push work in place, also in a `map_get_mut` arm; `inout e.b` passes to a user function. A holder inside a holder and holder `Option` / `Result` payloads stay `type/foreign_owned_type` | plain nested struct `Entry { ordinal: i64, b: Budget }`, fields moved | rejected (`codegen/unsupported_type`, D83) |
| R-6e-18 | D95 | `vec_extend_from_slice::<T>(inout P, s: [T]) -> ()` for `T` `i64` or `bool`, a whole statement under `! alloc`, place rules of R-6e-10; other `T` is `type/foreign_owned_type`, a borrowed vector is `type/inout_argument`. The verifier proves `len(old P) + len(s) <= 2^40`, then sets the length, keeps the prefix, makes the suffix equal to `s` and keeps sibling fields | `P.extend_from_slice(&(s)[..]);` | rejected (D83) |
| R-6e-12 (extended) | D85 | `move x` of an owned local or `take` parameter of a non-generic struct type (R-6e-1 aggregate or R-6e-6 record) into a struct field or enum payload, as in `return St { s: move s };`; a later read is `type/foreign_move` | `St { s: s, k: k }`, no clone | unchanged |

The brief listed `u8` for D95; `Vec<u8>` is not a type in the language (`parse/element_storage_type`, "u8 is only an
array element type"), so R-6e-18 has no `u8` place to extend and covers `i64` and `bool`.

test rejects it on both compilers. Item 4 flagged `S { n: i64 }` being movable against the first SPEC wording; the

array-field case instead.

### P32M.6 Design note

D90 reuses the R-6e-6 nested-record machinery one level up: a holder is a record whose fields are scalars, owned
buffers or nested-collection records, and it inherits their move and borrow rules, so no new ownership state was
needed. Both compilers compute the holder set once after type parameters are checked (`holder_records`), the
direct-field reject now looks at the nested set instead of "any record with collection fields", and the owned
aggregate positions accept holders. Holders are not nested further and are not `Option` / `Result` payloads, which
keeps the map-arm update and the verifier's field havoc at one level, matching the M12 shape that needed it. D95 is
a catalog entry with an `inout` vector and a borrowed slice; the verifier treats it as a resize with a fresh array
whose prefix and suffix are fixed by two quantifiers, as `vec_resize` does. D85 makes pruvc consume the `Move` child
of a struct literal or enum constructor the way pruvc-rs already did, so the rule is the rs behaviour, written in
R-6e-12, with the existing use-after-move check. pruvc now uses the pruvc-rs owned-aggregate set for `move`, so a
struct with an array field other than `[u8]` is not an owned aggregate and `move` of it is `type/foreign_move` in
both compilers; a struct of scalar fields only stays a (value) aggregate and may be moved, as in pruvc-rs before.

## Appendix P33: the zero-site inline rule (L4, applied under the rule 3 exception) and local proof gates (L5), both compilers

Conclusion: the L4 zero-site rule was first rejected (time regression vs base, rule 3), then re-applied on 2026-11-21
by user decision, which added a rule 3 exception: when every cell stays below 1.0x hand, a few % of time may be given
for a two-digit % gain in code size or compile time (`__text` -15.8%, rustc CPU -30%). The lost time is owed as debt
D110/D113 (P26c per-entry inline from host call-site info is the means to win it back). The compilers, SPEC.md and
tests are restored from 0ee93ca. The L5 survey found no removable guard. The measurements below are the record.

### P33.1 Rule (L4, applied)

The tried R-7-3 inline policy pass (`pruvc/inline_policy.py`, `pruvc-rs/crates/pruv-core/src/inline_policy.rs`, the
same rule in both) promoted a non-pinned, non-recursive `#[inline]` fn with

`always = incl <= INLINE_SMALL or calls == 1 or (calls >= 2 and incl * (calls - 1) <= INLINE_BUDGET)`

instead of `calls <= 1`. The pass does not look at visibility: any fn with zero textual call sites in the output
was covered, which in the gated families means the host entries (`pub fn m11_load`, ...) that the harness calls
through closures; the pass does not see harness calls. Under the old (current) rule such a fn gets `#[inline(always)]`, forcing
it into every harness call. The tried rule gave always only when `incl <= 8` and kept `#[inline]` otherwise. When codegen
emits a wrapper and `X__pruv_body` for a `pub fn`, in-crate calls go to the body, so a large `pub fn` that `main`
calls keeps `#[inline]` on the wrapper and its body (two call sites, wrapper and `main`) is decided by the usual
budget. A small `pub fn` may be emitted without a separate body (`tiny_entry` in the new test). Pinned / explicit attributes (section 6f),
recursion, the P18d `__pruv_fp` triple and the thresholds are unchanged. Both compilers emitted byte-identical Rust
(`tests/diff_rust.py --fuzz-count 20`).

### P33.2 Tests

- `pruvc-rs` `inline_policy` unit tests and `tests/check_generated.py` `INLINE_PAIRS`: (8 lines, 0 sites) always,
  (9, 0) not always, (9, 1) always; the existing pairs are unchanged.
- `tests/spec/r7_3_inline_entry.pruv` (accept): a large uncalled `pub fn` keeps `#[inline]`, its `__pruv_body` and a
  small uncalled `pub fn` get `#[inline(always)]`.
- `tests/spec/r7_3_inline_entry_called.pruv` (reject): a call from `main` does not promote the large wrapper.
- SPEC.md "Inline policy (generated Rust)": the promotion bullet and the Tests line. `tests/run_all_rows.txt` is
  unchanged (`--list-rows` diff empty). No checked-in golden of generated Rust changed. The revert removes the two
  fixtures, the unit asserts, the `INLINE_PAIRS` rows and the SPEC.md text; `git diff d7c2240 -- pruvc pruvc-rs
  SPEC.md tests` is empty.

- One fix attempt, a size cut-off: no threshold separates `t_put` from the M11 entries whose copies the rule removes
  (incl 1160 to 3309). This is D110 (rejected attempt).
- RSS is +16 KiB over base (P33 1.13-1.16x hand). The fixed-share RSS debt was already open from P13.

Perf gate on the P33 build: `tools/perf_gate.py work/p33/perf_cells.json` gave VERDICT PASS (37 cells, 0 fail, 6 debt
RSS cells, `work/p33/perf_gate.txt`). The gate compares to hand, not to base; the base comparison above is what
rejected the rule.

### P33.5 L5: local proof gates

A read-only survey of M11 `sol.rs` and the codegen sites in both compilers found four kinds of guard left in the
text:

1. `load_be` width 8: `<[u8; 8]>::try_from(get_unchecked(i..i+8)).unwrap()`, at `pruvc/codegen.py:3435` and
   `codegen.rs:4671`.
2. `load_be` width 4: `copy_from_slice`, at `pruvc/codegen.py:3439` and `codegen.rs:4675`.
3. `__pruv_small` `[..n]` (`pruvc/codegen.py:2819`, `codegen.rs:3701`), which has no calls in M11.
4. The last re-compare in the cold `pruv_len_slow` path, at `pruvc/codegen.py:275` and `codegen.rs:5533`.

In verified builds the source and target lengths of both conversions are equal, so the length-mismatch panic is
unreachable. An opt-level 3 asm probe of the two `load_be` patterns alone gives an 8-byte load and `rev` for width 8
and a 4-byte load, `rev` and zero extension for width 4, with no `unwrap_failed` or `len_mismatch` call. The
`unwrap_failed` calls found in the M11 binary are in `main`, the perf loop, closures and std.

The probe covers these two conversions only; it does not show that no such call remains in every M10 / M11 entry,
or that removing the text has no time or size effect. No guard was removed:
- The result checks and the refusal order are unchanged.
- No verification machinery was added.

The text residue is D111. The cold refusal-path compare is D112, to fold with the D100 / D101 entry-check work.

### P33.7 Note for P26c

Dropping the forced `#[inline(always)]` on every zero-site entry cut M11 `__text` 16% and H/1000 RSS by one page
(+32 -> +16 KiB over hand), but cost M10 putback and M11 R/B time. The M11 host entries keep the forced attribute at
d7c2240. Next means: decide inline per entry from host call-site information (harness call sites from P26c, or a
per-entry source attribute, section 6f), and gate it against base time on M10 and M11 as well as H RSS.
